body:
[should-fix] This treats apostrophes inside a valid Lean identifier as a character literal. I reproduced `declaration_line("namespace Example
theorem lemma'a' : True := by trivial
end Example
", "Example.lemma'a'")` raising `found 0`: `_lean_code` changes the declaration to `theorem lemma    : ...`. The catalogue name validator explicitly permits apostrophes, so a valid selected headline can be rejected. Please use identifier-boundary-aware character recognition (the shared scanner fix in #509 covers this distinction) and add a regression through catalogue loading while preserving the raw-string handling.

body: Nit: the attribute condition pins repository id, `refs/heads/main` and `push`, but not the workflow. Any other workflow on `main` that is triggered by `push` and requests `id-token: write` would also satisfy it. Today none does: `abstracts.yml` and `docs.yml` don't request it. Either add `assertion.workflow_ref.startsWith('cslib-community/complexitylib/.github/workflows/lean_action_ci.yml@')` to the condition (the existing provider needs `providers update-oidc`, because the setup step only creates it), or reword the claim to: "Pull requests and forks cannot obtain write access; on `main`, only this job requests an OIDC token."

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+# Build caches
+
+Complexitylib's build has two caches. Both are optional: `lake build` without them compiles
+everything it needs.
+
+**Local artifact cache.** `lakefile.toml` enables Lake's content-addressed artifact cache, so a
+module built in one checkout (a worktree, an agent sandbox, a second clone) is reused by every
+other checkout on the same machine with the same inputs. Outputs are hard-linked back into
+`.lake/build`. `lake cache clean` empties it; it lives in the Lean toolchain's directory under
+`~/.elan` unless `LAKE_CACHE_DIR` says otherwise.
+
+**Remote cache.** CI uploads the build outputs of every commit on `main`; `scripts/cache/get.sh`
+downloads them for the nearest cached ancestor of your `HEAD`:
+
+```bash
+scripts/cache/get.sh   # Mathlib's cache, then Complexitylib's outputs
+lake build             # compiles only what you changed
+```
+
+A complete set of library and test outputs is about 70 MB compressed. Outputs are platform
+independent (`platformIndependent = true`), so Linux CI builds serve macOS checkouts.
+`COMPLEXITYLIB_CACHE_URL` overrides the location; set it to an empty string to skip the
+Complexitylib download.
+
+## Trust and privacy
+
+Downloaded `.olean` files are trusted by Lean: imported modules are not re-checked by the
+kernel, and their compiled code (tactics, macros, initializers) runs during your build. Whoever
+can write to the cache could therefore make a false theorem appear proved or run code on your
+machine. The cache is set up so that this is no more trust than building `main` already
+requires:
+
+- Only the `main` push job of this repository can write. It authenticates with GitHub's OIDC
+  token through Workload Identity Federation, restricted to this repository's numeric id, the
+  `main` ref and the `push` event; no credentials are stored in GitHub. Pull requests, forks and
+  other workflows cannot obtain write access.

body: 1. [must-fix] This is not a spending cap. The setup creates an alerts-only budget, and budget notifications can lag for hours. Removing public reads after delivery also leaves storage/uploads/function costs running. Describe the $10 setting as a delayed, best-effort mitigation with residual exposure, including in the PR description. [Google budget behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets), [notification delivery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-programmatic-notifications#delivery_for_notifications_to_pubsub).

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+# Build caches
+
+Complexitylib's build has two caches. Both are optional: `lake build` without them compiles
+everything it needs.
+
+**Local artifact cache.** `lakefile.toml` enables Lake's content-addressed artifact cache, so a
+module built in one checkout (a worktree, an agent sandbox, a second clone) is reused by every
+other checkout on the same machine with the same inputs. Outputs are hard-linked back into
+`.lake/build`. `lake cache clean` empties it; it lives in the Lean toolchain's directory under
+`~/.elan` unless `LAKE_CACHE_DIR` says otherwise.
+
+**Remote cache.** CI uploads the build outputs of every commit on `main`; `scripts/cache/get.sh`
+downloads them for the nearest cached ancestor of your `HEAD`:
+
+```bash
+scripts/cache/get.sh   # Mathlib's cache, then Complexitylib's outputs
+lake build             # compiles only what you changed
+```
+
+A complete set of library and test outputs is about 70 MB compressed. Outputs are platform
+independent (`platformIndependent = true`), so Linux CI builds serve macOS checkouts.
+`COMPLEXITYLIB_CACHE_URL` overrides the location; set it to an empty string to skip the
+Complexitylib download.
+
+## Trust and privacy
+
+Downloaded `.olean` files are trusted by Lean: imported modules are not re-checked by the
+kernel, and their compiled code (tactics, macros, initializers) runs during your build. Whoever
+can write to the cache could therefore make a false theorem appear proved or run code on your
+machine. The cache is set up so that this is no more trust than building `main` already
+requires:
+
+- Only the `main` push job of this repository can write. It authenticates with GitHub's OIDC
+  token through Workload Identity Federation, restricted to this repository's numeric id, the
+  `main` ref and the `push` event; no credentials are stored in GitHub. Pull requests, forks and
+  other workflows cannot obtain write access.
+- The writer can create objects but not delete them, so a published artifact can never be
+  replaced. Lake checks every downloaded artifact against the hash recorded in the mapping.
+- Merge-gating CI always builds from source; the cache only saves local build time.
+
+The cache contains only build outputs of commits on `main` (sources that are public in this
+repository); build logs and machine paths are not uploaded. Downloads are anonymous HTTPS
+requests to Google Cloud Storage; the bucket keeps no access logs.
+
+## Maintainer runbook
+
+The cache runs in a dedicated Google Cloud project maintained by Samuel Schlesinger.
+
+**Setup.** `PROJECT=<id> BILLING_ACCOUNT=<id> ALERT_EMAIL=<address> scripts/cache/setup-gcs.sh`
+creates, in order (each step can be rerun alone, e.g. `setup-gcs.sh alert`):
+
+| Step | Creates |
+| --- | --- |
+| `project` | the project, billing link and APIs |
+| `bucket` | `gs://complexitylib-lake-cache` (`us-east1`), public read by object name without listing, no soft delete or versioning, revision mappings expire after 180 days |
+| `writer` | the GitHub identity pool and provider, and the `lake-cache-writer` service account (create + read on the bucket only) |
+| `budget` | a monthly budget (default 10 USD) with alerts at 50/90/100 % and a Pub/Sub topic |
+| `killswitch` | a Cloud Run function that removes public read when the budget is reached or the egress alert fires |
+| `alert` | an alert on more than 20 GB sent per hour, to the kill switch and `ALERT_EMAIL` |
+| `variables` | prints the `gh variable set` commands for the three repository variables |
+
+CI skips the upload until the repository variable `LAKE_CACHE_BUCKET` is set.
+
+**Costs.** Storage and egress are small at this size: each `main` push uploads only modules whose
+outputs changed, and Cloud Storage's free tier covers 5 GB of storage and 100 GB of egress per
+month in `us-east1`. The budget alerts and the kill switch bound abuse of the public bucket.

Raising either threshold leaves the old lower-threshold resources publishing to the same kill-switch topic, so they can still disable the cache. Find/update the existing resources, or implement and document their deliberate replacement before changing a threshold.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# One-time maintainer setup of the remote build cache on Google Cloud. See scripts/cache/README.md.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   PROJECT=<new-project-id> BILLING_ACCOUNT=<id> [ALERT_EMAIL=<address>] \
+#     scripts/cache/setup-gcs.sh [step...]
+#
+# Steps (default: all, in order): project bucket writer budget killswitch alert variables.
+# Each step can be rerun on its own. Optional settings: BUCKET (complexitylib-lake-cache),
+# REGION (us-east1, inside Cloud Storage's free tier), BUDGET_USD (10), EGRESS_ALERT_GB (20 per
+# hour). Billing account and e-mail are arguments so that they never enter the repository.
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+
+: "${PROJECT:?set PROJECT to the id of a new, dedicated Google Cloud project}"
+BUCKET="${BUCKET:-complexitylib-lake-cache}"
+REGION="${REGION:-us-east1}"
+BUDGET_USD="${BUDGET_USD:-10}"
+EGRESS_ALERT_GB="${EGRESS_ALERT_GB:-20}"
+REPO="cslib-community/complexitylib"
+REPO_ID="1420662136"          # `gh api repos/cslib-community/complexitylib --jq .id`
+WRITER="lake-cache-writer@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
+KILLER="lake-cache-kill-switch@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
+TOPIC="lake-cache-limits"
+POOL="github"
+PROVIDER="complexitylib"
+
+gc() { echo "+ gcloud $*" >&2; gcloud "$@"; }
+project_number() { gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" --format='value(projectNumber)'; }
+
+step_project() {
+  gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || gc projects create "$PROJECT"
+  gc billing projects link "$PROJECT" --billing-account="${BILLING_ACCOUNT:?set BILLING_ACCOUNT}"
+  gc services enable --project="$PROJECT" storage.googleapis.com iam.googleapis.com \
+    iamcredentials.googleapis.com sts.googleapis.com pubsub.googleapis.com \
+    billingbudgets.googleapis.com monitoring.googleapis.com cloudfunctions.googleapis.com \
+    run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com \
+    eventarc.googleapis.com
+}
+
+step_bucket() {
+  gcloud storage buckets describe "gs://$BUCKET" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
+    gc storage buckets create "gs://$BUCKET" --project="$PROJECT" --location="$REGION" \
+      --uniform-bucket-level-access --soft-delete-duration=0 --default-storage-class=STANDARD
+  # Revision mappings older than 180 days are dropped; artifacts are shared between revisions
+  # and are pruned separately (README: "Pruning").
+  local lifecycle
+  lifecycle="$(mktemp)"
+  echo '{"rule":[{"action":{"type":"Delete"},"condition":{"age":180,"matchesPrefix":["r0/"]}}]}' \
+    > "$lifecycle"
+  gc storage buckets update "gs://$BUCKET" --no-versioning --lifecycle-file="$lifecycle"
+  rm -f "$lifecycle"
+  # Anyone may read an object by name (Lake downloads without credentials); nobody may list.
+  gc storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding "gs://$BUCKET" \
+    --member=allUsers --role=roles/storage.legacyObjectReader
+}
+
+step_writer() {
+  gcloud iam workload-identity-pools describe "$POOL" --project="$PROJECT" --location=global \
+    >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
+    gc iam workload-identity-pools create "$POOL" --project="$PROJECT" --location=global \
+      --display-name="GitHub Actions"
+  gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers describe "$PROVIDER" --project="$PROJECT" \
+    --location=global --workload-identity-pool="$POOL" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
+    gc iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc "$PROVIDER" --project="$PROJECT" \
+      --location=global --workload-identity-pool="$POOL" \
+      --issuer-uri=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
+      --attribute-mapping='google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository_id=assertion.repository_id,attribute.ref=assertion.ref,attribute.event_name=assertion.event_name' \
+      --attribute-condition="assertion.repository_id == '$REPO_ID' && assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && assertion.event_name == 'push'"
+  gcloud iam service-accounts describe "$WRITER" --project="$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**Requested: add plain `trans`, `fst'` and `snd'`.** The tidy `fun_prop` set has these in `PolyTime/Basic.lean` for two reasons. `comp'` infers the intermediate encoding only from the outer function, and the bare `fst`/`snd` cannot infer the other component's encoding. Without plain counterparts, `fun_prop` fails on these plain goals at `d57db0ef`, although tidy `fun_prop` proves all of their tidy forms:

```lean
example (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc (encPair encB encC)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).1) enc encB := by fun_prop  -- fails: cannot infer ?enc₂
example (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc (encPair encB encC)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).1) enc encB := by fun_prop  -- also fails
example (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc (encList encNat)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).length) enc encUnary := by fun_prop  -- fails
example (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc (encPair encNat encBool)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => !(f a).2) enc encBool := by fun_prop  -- fails
```

The M2 batches restate verifiers over `encPair enc encBits`, so projections of pair-valued hypotheses will be common. With the following added to this section, all four examples go through and the PR's own plain examples still pass. I checked this in a scratch file importing `Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime`.

```lean
/-- Compose in execution order. This lets `fun_prop` infer the intermediate encoding from the
inner function when it cannot be inferred from the outer function. -/
@[fun_prop]
theorem trans {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encMid)
    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encMid encOut) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encOut :=
  hg.comp hf

/-- Project the first component of a pair-valued function computable in polynomial time. -/
@[fun_prop]
theorem fst' {β₁ β₂ : Type u} {enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool} {enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool}
    {f : α → β₁ × β₂} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn (encPair enc₁ enc₂)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x).1) encIn enc₁ :=
  (fst enc₁ enc₂).comp hf
```

Add `snd'` in the same way. Please also add the four examples to `ComplexityTests/PolyTimePlain.lean`.

+/-! ### Bridges to `ComputableInPolyTime` -/
+
+/-- **Plain and tidy polynomial time agree.** `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime` unfolds to
+the right-hand side of
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut ↔ ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength.symm
+
+/-- A function computable in polynomial time is tidily computable in polynomial time. The tidy
+machine adds linear overhead to both bounds. -/
+theorem ComputableInPolyTime.tidy (h : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime.mp h
+
+/-- A function tidily computable in polynomial time is computable in polynomial time, by the same
+machine within the same bounds. -/
+theorem ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  h.exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength
+
+/-- `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy` for dot notation on a tidy hypothesis. It is
+a `fun_prop` transition rule, so every tidy certificate also proves plain goals. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut) : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  .of_tidy h
+
+/-- **A polynomial time bound alone suffices.** A function computable by some machine within a time
+bound polynomial in the length of the encoded input, with any space bound, is computable in
+polynomial time: within `t` steps the machine visits at most `c t + c` work-tape cells. -/
+theorem ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime {t : ℕ → ℕ} {s : α → ℕ}
+    (ht : PolynomiallyBounded t)
+    (h : ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut (fun a => t (encIn a).length) s) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  let ⟨c, h⟩ := h.exists_space_linear
+  ⟨t, fun n => c * t n + c, ht, by fun_prop, h⟩

+The rules that need a machine construction, proved through the tidy calculus. Together with
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime` they make `fun_prop` prove
+plain goals from plain hypotheses and tidy certificates. -/

body:
**Requested: this `fun_prop` claim is too strong.** `fun_prop` tries transition theorems only on atoms that it cannot decompose further: `fvarAppCase`, and the `else` branch of `constAppCase` in `Mathlib/Tactic/FunProp/Core.lean`. The plain rules split a decomposable plain goal, so a tidy certificate stated compositionally for the whole goal is never tried. Even with the rules from the comment on `snd` below, this still fails:

```lean
example (hlist : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime list enc encBits)
    (htest : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : α × Bool => test p.1 p.2)
      (encPair enc encBool) encBool) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).any (test a)) enc encBool := by
  fail_if_success fun_prop  -- `bitsAnyWithInput` is never reached
  polytime                  -- works, and so does `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`
```

Several statements overclaim:
- "from any tidy certificate" (here);
- "every tidy certificate also proves plain goals" (line 183);
- "plain goals from plain hypotheses and tidy certificates" (line 205);
- in the PR body, "plain goals are as easy to discharge as tidy ones".

Suggested wording: "`fun_prop` decomposes a plain goal with the plain closure rules. It proves the remaining atoms from plain hypotheses or, through the transition, from tidy certificates. For a tidy certificate stated compositionally, such as the `…WithInput` scans, use `polytime` or `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`." Please add the example above to the tests and a line to the PR's limitations.

body:
**Requested change: say that this departs from the textbook convention.** Charging the value to the space bound is reasonable for a notion that mirrors the tidy calculus. It is not the textbook convention, though, and it differs from the library's own plain `ComputableInLogSpace`, whose docstring says "the input and the output are not charged". In Arora–Barak Ch. 4 and Papadimitriou §2.5, a space bound counts only the work tapes. The output tape is write-only and can be much longer than the bound; a log-space transducer writes a polynomial-length output.

**Consequence.** At sublinear bounds, `ComputableInSpace` and `ComputableInO` are strictly stronger than their names say. Against this head, I checked that `ComputableInLogSpace (id : List Bool → List Bool) encBits encBits` holds (copy machine, `c = 0`) while `¬ComputableInSpace (id : List Bool → List Bool) encBits encBits fun w => Nat.log2 w.length` (take an input of length `2 ^ (c + 2)`). Only one direction holds: `ComputableInSpace … (log₂ ∘ length) → ComputableInLogSpace`. So these notions cannot state FL or log-space and polylog-space reductions, which #456 lists among the things the plain API must express. A public theorem with a `ComputableInSpace` hypothesis at a sublinear bound would also cover far fewer functions than its name suggests.

Two smaller points in the same paragraph:
- The composition rationale belongs to the tidy calculus, where a value is kept on a work tape. Transducer space classes compose without the condition, by recomputing output bits (Arora–Barak §4.3).
- The paragraph cites Arora–Barak Chapter 4 without saying that it departs from it.

**Proposed fix (minimal).**
- In this module docstring and in the `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace` docstrings, say that the value is charged, unlike [AroraBarak09, Chapter 4] and [Papadimitriou94]. Say that `ComputableInSpace f encIn encOut (fun a => Nat.log2 (encIn a).length)` is therefore strictly stronger than `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInLogSpace`, which is the transducer notion.
- Justify the condition by the same-bound equivalence with the tidy notions, not by composition.
- Pin the gap with the test suggested on `ResourceBoundsPlain.lean`.

If the coordinator would rather give these names the textbook meaning, the alternative is to drop the value condition from `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace`, keeping it for `ComputableInPolySpace`. `.tidy` would then take the value bound as a hypothesis, and the iffs would read `plain ∧ value bound ↔ tidy`. That is a larger change, and I don't require it.

Requested: reject directory symlinks before using `rglob`. `Path.rglob("*.lean")` does not descend through a nested symlink directory, so neither that directory nor its Lean children reaches the `is_symlink()` check below.

This is an incomplete graph, not the advertised conservative fallback; the existing file-symlink test does not cover it.

Please inspect directory entries explicitly and fall back for directory symlinks, including the library root directory, with a regression for an existing tracked directory symlink.

For example, `lean_lib Demo` at `.` together with `lean_lib Base` at `srcDir = "Demo"` maps `Demo/Base/Extra.lean` to both `Demo.Base.Extra` and `Base.Extra`. +        if any(not isinstance(xs, list) or any(not isinstance(x, str) for x in xs)
+               for xs in parsed.values()):
+            raise ValueError("invalid import names")
+        return parsed
+    except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError) as error:
+        raise FullCheck(f"invalid native header-parser response: {error}") from error
+
+
+def source_modules(root: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, str], set[str], set[str]]:
+    if (root / "lakefile.lean").exists():
+        raise FullCheck("dynamic Lake configuration is outside quick-check scope")
+    try:
+        config = tomllib.loads((root / "lakefile.toml").read_text())
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+        raise FullCheck(f"cannot read Lake configuration: {error}") from error
+    if config.get("srcDir", ".") != ".":
+        raise FullCheck("package source directory is outside quick-check scope")
+    libraries = config.get("lean_lib", [])
+    if not isinstance(libraries, list) or not libraries:
+        raise FullCheck("no Lake libraries were discovered")
+    modules: dict[str, str] = {}
+    aggregates: set[str] = set()
+    roots: set[str] = set()
+    allowed = {"name", "srcDir", "leanOptions", "allowNonModules"}
+    for library in libraries:
+        if not isinstance(library, dict) or set(library) - allowed:
+            raise FullCheck("custom Lake library roots/globs/options need full checks")
+        name = library.get("name", "")
+        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)*", name):
+            raise FullCheck("unsupported library name")
+        source = root / library.get("srcDir", ".")
+        if source.is_symlink() or not source.resolve().is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
+            raise FullCheck("library source directory escapes the checkout")
+        relative = Path(*name.split("."))
+        aggregator = source / relative.with_suffix(".lean")
+        directory = source / relative
+        if not aggregator.is_file() or not directory.is_dir():
+            raise FullCheck(f"missing library root {name}")
+        roots.add(name)
+        aggregates.add(name)
+        for path in [aggregator, *sorted(directory.rglob("*.lean"))]:
+            if path.is_symlink() or not path.resolve().is_relative_to(source.resolve()):
+                raise FullCheck("symlinked source file is outside quick-check scope")
+            parts = path.relative_to(source).with_suffix("").parts
+            if any(not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*", part) for part in parts):
+                raise FullCheck("unsupported source module path")
+            module = ".".join(parts)
+            if module in modules:
+                raise FullCheck(f"ambiguous local module {module}")
+            modules[module] = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+    return modules, aggregates, roots
+
+
+def make_plan(root: Path, base_ref: str = "origin/main", parser=None) -> Plan:
+    if git(root, "ls-files", "--unmerged", "-z"):
+        raise FullCheck("unresolved merge entries")
+    reference = git(root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--end-of-options", f"{base_ref}^{{commit}}").strip()
+    bases = git(root, "merge-base", "--all", reference, "HEAD").splitlines()
+    if len(bases) != 1:
+        raise FullCheck("comparison needs exactly one merge base")
+    base = bases[0]
+    fields = git(root, "diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-renames", "--name-status", "-z", base, "--").split("\0")
+    fields = fields[:-1] if fields[-1] == "" else fields
+    if len(fields) % 2:
+        raise FullCheck("unexpected Git change-list format")
+    changes = list(zip(fields[::2], fields[1::2]))
+    changes += [("A", p) for p in git(root, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z").split("\0") if p]
+    for status, path in changes:
+        if status not in {"A", "M"}:
+            raise FullCheck(f"deleted, renamed or unusual change: {path}")
+        if not path.endswith(".lean"):
+            raise FullCheck(f"non-Lean change: {path}")
+    modules, aggregates, roots = source_modules(root)
+    by_path = {path: module for module, path in modules.items()}

body: [P2] Register this private construction rule locally. `@[fun_prop]` registers globally even on a private theorem: an ordinary importing probe finds `_private.…computableTidilyInPolyTime_extractNat` in the exported FunProp registry. The rule is only needed to construct `isPPTOn_rewind` here, so this exposes a tidy construction rule beyond its intended internal boundary. Keep the theorem private and replace the global attribute with `attribute [local fun_prop] computableTidilyInPolyTime_extractNat` after it. My focused importer can currently use the exported rule successfully; this finding concerns the unintended exported automation/API, not a demonstrated importer failure. — independent Codex worker review_559

+/-!
+# Schnorr identification under the discrete-logarithm assumption
+
+Schnorr's identification scheme ([BonehShoup2023], Section 19.1) over a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`:
+the key is a description `d`, drawn from a setup law, a uniform secret `α` and the public key
+`u = α • g`. An impersonator sees the description and the encoded public key and sends a
+commitment word `t`; the verifier draws a uniform challenge word `c` of `k n` bits; the
+impersonator answers with a word `z`. Challenges and responses are read as binary numbers modulo
+the group order `q`, and the verifier accepts when `t` encodes `z • g - c • u`; on genuine group
+elements this is Schnorr's check `z • g = t + c • u`.
+
+Rewinding an impersonator gives a discrete-logarithm adversary, `SchnorrImpersonator.rewind`. It
+runs the impersonator to its commitment, answers two independent uniform challenges from the same
+state, and computes `(c - c')⁻¹ (z - z')` modulo `q`, inverting by Fermat's little theorem. For each
+security parameter, if `2 ^ k ≤ q` for every description the setup can produce,
+
+  `ε ≤ 1 / 2 ^ k + √ε'`,

+where `ε` is the impersonator's success probability and `ε'` the discrete-logarithm success
+probability of the rewinding adversary (`succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le`, Theorem 19.1).
+The rewinding adversary is uniform strict PPT whenever the impersonator is and `k` is computable
+in polynomial time. Under the discrete-logarithm assumption, with negligible `1 / 2 ^ k`, every
+uniform strict PPT impersonator therefore succeeds with negligible probability
+(`negligible_schnorrDirectGame`).
+
+The impersonator may use fresh randomness in its second stage; its state is a word. Challenges
+are bit strings because strict PPT machines sample them exactly; they cannot sample `ZMod q`
+exactly, which matters for the honest prover and for simulation but not for this reduction.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.SchnorrImpersonator`: a two-stage word adversary.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.schnorrDirectGame`: the direct impersonation attack.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.SchnorrImpersonator.rewind`: the rewinding
+  discrete-logarithm adversary.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le`: `ε ≤ 1 / 2 ^ k + √ε'`
+  at each security parameter.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.isPPTOn_rewind`: the rewinding adversary is uniform strict
+  PPT.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.negligible_schnorrDirectGame`: Schnorr identification is
+  secure against direct attacks under the discrete-logarithm assumption.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Section 19.1.
+* [C.-P. Schnorr, *Efficient Signature Generation by Smart Cards*][Schnorr1991]
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section

+namespace Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily
+
+open Probability Turing.MultiTapeTM Protocols
+
+variable {F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily}
+
+variable (F) in
+/-- A uniform impersonator against Schnorr identification. Its first stage sees the security
+parameter, the group description and the encoded public key, and returns a commitment word and a
+state word; its second stage sees the security parameter, the state and the challenge word. -/
+structure SchnorrImpersonator where
+  /-- Commit, keeping a state word. -/
+  commit : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)
+  /-- Respond to a challenge word from the state word. -/
+  respond : ℕ → List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)
+
+/-- Both stages of an impersonator are uniform strict PPT in their whole inputs. -/
+def SchnorrImpersonator.IsPPT (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) : Prop :=
+  IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc encBits)) (encPair encBits encBits)
+      (fun input => A.commit input.1 input.2) ∧
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits encBits)) encBits
+      (fun input => A.respond input.1 input.2)
+
+variable (F) in
+/-- The direct impersonation attack on Schnorr identification ([BonehShoup2023], Attack
+Game 18.1), with challenges of `k n` bits. The verifier accepts when the commitment encodes
+`z • g - c • u`. -/
+noncomputable def schnorrDirectGame (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ) : Game := do
+  let d ← setup n
+  let α ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let ts ← ProbComp.eval (A.commit n (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d)))
+  let c ← BitString.uniformList (k n)
+  let z ← ProbComp.eval (A.respond n (ts.2, c))
+  return decide (ts.1 = F.encode d ((ofBits z : ZMod (F.order d)) • F.generator d -
+    (ofBits c : ZMod (F.order d)) • (α • F.generator d)))
+
+/-- The extracted witness `(c - c')⁻¹ (z - z')` modulo `q`, computed on natural numbers with the
+inverse as a `(q - 2)`nd power. -/
+def extractNat (q c z c' z' : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  ((c % q + q - c' % q) % q) ^ (q - 2) % q * ((z % q + q - z' % q) % q) % q
+
+/-- The rewinding discrete-logarithm adversary (proof of [BonehShoup2023], Theorem 19.1): run the
+impersonator to its commitment, answer two independent uniform `k n`-bit challenges from the same
+state, and output the extracted witness in binary. -/
+noncomputable def SchnorrImpersonator.rewind (k : ℕ → ℕ) (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ)
+    (input : F.Desc × List Bool) : ProbComp (List Bool) := do
+  let ts ← A.commit n input
+  let c ← BitString.sampleList (k n)
+  let c' ← BitString.sampleList (k n)
+  let z ← A.respond n (ts.2, c)
+  let z' ← A.respond n (ts.2, c')
+  return (extractNat (F.order input.1) (ofBits c) (ofBits z) (ofBits c') (ofBits z')).bits
+
+/-! ### The exact bound -/
+
+/-- Binary digits, least significant first, read as a number (a private copy of the bridge in
+`Classes/Counting/Space.lean`). -/
+private theorem ofBits_eq_lsbValue (w : List Bool) : ofBits w = BitString.lsbValue w := by
+  induction w with
+  | nil => rfl
+  | cons b w ih =>
+    change Nat.bit b (ofBits w) = b.toNat + 2 * BitString.lsbValue w
+    rw [ih]
+    cases b <;> simp [Nat.bit, Nat.add_comm]
+
+/-- Distinct `k`-bit challenges are distinct modulo `q` when `2 ^ k ≤ q`. -/
+private theorem challenge_ne {q k : ℕ} (hkq : 2 ^ k ≤ q) {c c' : BitString k} (hc : c ≠ c') :
+    (ofBits (List.ofFn c) : ZMod q) ≠ ofBits (List.ofFn c') := by
+  intro h
+  rw [ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff', ofBits_eq_lsbValue, ofBits_eq_lsbValue,
+    Nat.mod_eq_of_lt ((BitString.lsbValue_lt _).trans_le (by simpa using hkq)),
+    Nat.mod_eq_of_lt ((BitString.lsbValue_lt _).trans_le (by simpa using hkq))] at h
+  exact hc (List.ofFn_injective (BitString.lsbValue_injective (by simp) h))
+
+/-- Fermat's little theorem gives the inverse in `extractNat`. -/
+private theorem extractNat_cast {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] {c z c' z' : ℕ}
+    (hc : (c : ZMod q) ≠ c') :
+    (extractNat q c z c' z' : ZMod q) = ((c : ZMod q) - c')⁻¹ * ((z : ZMod q) - z') := by
+  have hsub (a b : ℕ) : (((a % q + q - b % q) % q : ℕ) : ZMod q) = (a : ZMod q) - b := by
+    rw [ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_sub ((Nat.mod_lt _ (Fact.out : q.Prime).pos).le.trans
+      (Nat.le_add_left _ _)), Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_mod, ZMod.natCast_mod, ZMod.natCast_self,
+      add_zero]
+  have hne : (c : ZMod q) - c' ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hc
+  have hinv : ((c : ZMod q) - c') ^ (q - 2) = ((c : ZMod q) - c')⁻¹ := by
+    refine eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_left ?_
+    rw [← pow_succ, show q - 2 + 1 = q - 1 by have := (Fact.out : q.Prime).two_le; lia,
+      ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one hne]
+  simp only [extractNat, Nat.cast_mul, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_pow, hsub, hinv]
+
+/-- Schnorr's protocol on encoded commitments and binary responses, with statements carrying their
+group description; only its verifier is used. -/
+private noncomputable def wordProtocol (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (m : ℕ) :
+    SigmaProtocol ℕ ((d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) (List Bool) (BitString m) (List Bool) where
+  State := Unit
+  commit _ _ := PMF.pure ([], ())
+  respond _ _ _ _ := []
+  verify y t c z := decide (t = F.encode y.1 ((ofBits z : ZMod (F.order y.1)) • F.generator y.1 -
+    (ofBits (List.ofFn c) : ZMod (F.order y.1)) • y.2))
+
+/-- Schnorr key generation at a security parameter, with the description in the statement. -/
+private noncomputable def wordKeyGen (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc)
+    (n : ℕ) : PMF (ℕ × (d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) := do
+  let d ← setup n
+  let α ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  return (α.val, ⟨d, α • F.generator d⟩)
+
+/-- The relation: `x` is a discrete logarithm of the public key. -/
+private def wordRelation (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (x : ℕ) (y : (d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) :
+    Prop :=
+  (x : ZMod (F.order y.1)) • F.generator y.1 = y.2
+
+private noncomputable instance (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) :
+    DecidableRel (wordRelation F) := fun _ _ => Classical.propDecidable _
+
+/-- The extractor of `wordProtocol`. -/
+private def wordExtract (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (m : ℕ) (y : (d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d)
+    (_ : List Bool) (c : BitString m) (z : List Bool) (c' : BitString m) (z' : List Bool) : ℕ :=
+  extractNat (F.order y.1) (ofBits (List.ofFn c)) (ofBits z) (ofBits (List.ofFn c')) (ofBits z')
+
+/-- An impersonator as a typed impersonator for `wordProtocol`. -/
+private noncomputable def SchnorrImpersonator.typed (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n m : ℕ) :
+    SigmaProtocol.Impersonator ((d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) (List Bool) (BitString m)
+      (List Bool) where
+  State := List Bool
+  commit y := ProbComp.eval (A.commit n (y.1, F.encode y.1 y.2))
+  respond s c := ProbComp.eval (A.respond n (s, List.ofFn c))
+
+private theorem schnorrDirectGame_eq (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ) :
+    F.schnorrDirectGame setup k A n =
+      (wordProtocol F (k n)).directAttack (wordKeyGen F setup n) (A.typed n (k n)) := by
+  simp only [schnorrDirectGame, SigmaProtocol.directAttack, wordKeyGen, wordProtocol,
+    SchnorrImpersonator.typed, BitString.uniformList, Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+    Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.bind_bind, PMF.pure_bind, PMF.bind_map,
+    Function.comp_def]
+
+private theorem specialSoundOn (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) {k : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ}
+    (hkq : ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, 2 ^ k n ≤ F.order d) :
+    (wordProtocol F (k n)).SpecialSoundOn (wordKeyGen F setup n) (wordRelation F)
+      (wordExtract F (k n)) := by
+  rintro ⟨x, d, u⟩ hkey t c z c' z' hc hz hz'
+  have hd : d ∈ (setup n).support := by
+    simp only [wordKeyGen, Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+      Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.mem_support_bind_iff, PMF.mem_support_pure_iff,
+      Prod.mk.injEq, Sigma.mk.injEq] at hkey
+    obtain ⟨d', hd', -, -, -, hdd, -⟩ := hkey
+    exact hdd ▸ hd'
+  simp only [SigmaProtocol.Accepts, wordProtocol, decide_eq_true_eq] at hz hz'
+  have heq := F.encode_injective d (hz.symm.trans hz')
+  have hcne := challenge_ne (hkq d hd) hc
+  simp only [wordRelation, wordExtract, extractNat_cast hcne, mul_smul]
+  rw [sub_smul, sub_eq_sub_iff_sub_eq_sub.mp heq, ← sub_smul,
+    inv_smul_smul₀ (sub_ne_zero.mpr hcne)]
+
+/-- Reading back the binary digits of a number recovers it. -/
+private theorem ofBits_bits (r : ℕ) : ofBits r.bits = r := Nat.foldr_bit_bits r
+
+/-- The rewinding adversary wins the discrete-logarithm game exactly when its output is a witness
+for the generated statement. -/
+private theorem decide_wordRelation (d : F.Desc) (α : ZMod (F.order d)) (r : ℕ) :
+    decide (wordRelation F r ⟨d, α • F.generator d⟩) =
+      decide (((ofBits r.bits : ℕ) : ZMod (F.order d)) = α) := by
+  rw [ofBits_bits]
+  exact decide_eq_decide.mpr ⟨fun h => F.smul_generator_injective d h, fun h => by
+    simp only [wordRelation, h]⟩
+
+private theorem oneWayGame_eq (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ) (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator)
+    (n : ℕ) :
+    SigmaProtocol.oneWayGame (wordKeyGen F setup n) (wordRelation F)
+        ((A.typed n (k n)).rewind (wordExtract F (k n))) =
+      F.discreteLogGame setup (A.rewind k) n := by
+  simp only [SigmaProtocol.oneWayGame, wordKeyGen, discreteLogGame,
+    SigmaProtocol.Impersonator.rewind, SchnorrImpersonator.rewind, SchnorrImpersonator.typed,
+    ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure, BitString.eval_sampleList, BitString.uniformList,
+    Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind, Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.bind_bind,
+    PMF.pure_bind, PMF.bind_map, Function.comp_def, wordExtract, decide_wordRelation]
+
+/-- **Schnorr identification against direct attacks, exact form** ([BonehShoup2023],
+Theorem 19.1): at each security parameter where every possible group has at least `2 ^ k n`
+elements, an impersonator's success probability is at most `1 / 2 ^ k n + √ε'`, where `ε'` is the
+discrete-logarithm success probability of the rewinding adversary. -/
+theorem succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ) (hkq : ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, 2 ^ k n ≤ F.order d) :
+    (Game.succProbability (F.schnorrDirectGame setup k A n) : ℝ) ≤
+      1 / 2 ^ k n + √(Game.succProbability (F.discreteLogGame setup (A.rewind k) n)) := by
+  have h := SigmaProtocol.succProbability_directAttack_le (specialSoundOn setup hkq)
+    (A.typed n (k n))
+  rw [oneWayGame_eq] at h
+  rw [schnorrDirectGame_eq]
+  simpa only [Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin, Nat.cast_pow,
+    Nat.cast_ofNat] using h
+
+/-! ### Efficiency of the rewinding adversary -/
+
+/-- The extracted witness is computable in polynomial time from the group description and the
+four binary numbers. -/
+@[fun_prop]

+in polynomial time. Under the discrete-logarithm assumption, with negligible `1 / 2 ^ k`, every
+uniform strict PPT impersonator therefore succeeds with negligible probability
+(`negligible_schnorrDirectGame`).
+
+The impersonator may use fresh randomness in its second stage; its state is a word. Challenges
+are bit strings because strict PPT machines sample them exactly; they cannot sample `ZMod q`
+exactly, which matters for the honest prover and for simulation but not for this reduction.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.SchnorrImpersonator`: a two-stage word adversary.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.schnorrDirectGame`: the direct impersonation attack.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.SchnorrImpersonator.rewind`: the rewinding
+  discrete-logarithm adversary.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le`: `ε ≤ 1 / 2 ^ k + √ε'`
+  at each security parameter.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.isPPTOn_rewind`: the rewinding adversary is uniform strict
+  PPT.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.negligible_schnorrDirectGame`: Schnorr identification is
+  secure against direct attacks under the discrete-logarithm assumption.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Section 19.1.
+* [C.-P. Schnorr, *Efficient Signature Generation by Smart Cards*][Schnorr1991]
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily
+
+open Probability Turing.MultiTapeTM Protocols
+
+variable {F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily}
+
+variable (F) in
+/-- A uniform impersonator against Schnorr identification. Its first stage sees the security
+parameter, the group description and the encoded public key, and returns a commitment word and a
+state word; its second stage sees the security parameter, the state and the challenge word. -/
+structure SchnorrImpersonator where
+  /-- Commit, keeping a state word. -/
+  commit : ℕ → F.Desc × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)
+  /-- Respond to a challenge word from the state word. -/
+  respond : ℕ → List Bool × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)
+
+/-- Both stages of an impersonator are uniform strict PPT in their whole inputs. -/
+def SchnorrImpersonator.IsPPT (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) : Prop :=
+  IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair F.encDesc encBits)) (encPair encBits encBits)
+      (fun input => A.commit input.1 input.2) ∧
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits encBits)) encBits
+      (fun input => A.respond input.1 input.2)
+
+variable (F) in
+/-- The direct impersonation attack on Schnorr identification ([BonehShoup2023], Attack
+Game 18.1), with challenges of `k n` bits. The verifier accepts when the commitment encodes
+`z • g - c • u`. -/
+noncomputable def schnorrDirectGame (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ) : Game := do
+  let d ← setup n
+  let α ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let ts ← ProbComp.eval (A.commit n (d, F.encode d (α • F.generator d)))
+  let c ← BitString.uniformList (k n)
+  let z ← ProbComp.eval (A.respond n (ts.2, c))
+  return decide (ts.1 = F.encode d ((ofBits z : ZMod (F.order d)) • F.generator d -
+    (ofBits c : ZMod (F.order d)) • (α • F.generator d)))
+
+/-- The extracted witness `(c - c')⁻¹ (z - z')` modulo `q`, computed on natural numbers with the
+inverse as a `(q - 2)`nd power. -/
+def extractNat (q c z c' z' : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  ((c % q + q - c' % q) % q) ^ (q - 2) % q * ((z % q + q - z' % q) % q) % q
+
+/-- The rewinding discrete-logarithm adversary (proof of [BonehShoup2023], Theorem 19.1): run the
+impersonator to its commitment, answer two independent uniform `k n`-bit challenges from the same
+state, and output the extracted witness in binary. -/
+noncomputable def SchnorrImpersonator.rewind (k : ℕ → ℕ) (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ)
+    (input : F.Desc × List Bool) : ProbComp (List Bool) := do
+  let ts ← A.commit n input
+  let c ← BitString.sampleList (k n)
+  let c' ← BitString.sampleList (k n)
+  let z ← A.respond n (ts.2, c)
+  let z' ← A.respond n (ts.2, c')
+  return (extractNat (F.order input.1) (ofBits c) (ofBits z) (ofBits c') (ofBits z')).bits
+
+/-! ### The exact bound -/
+
+/-- Binary digits, least significant first, read as a number (a private copy of the bridge in
+`Classes/Counting/Space.lean`). -/
+private theorem ofBits_eq_lsbValue (w : List Bool) : ofBits w = BitString.lsbValue w := by
+  induction w with
+  | nil => rfl
+  | cons b w ih =>
+    change Nat.bit b (ofBits w) = b.toNat + 2 * BitString.lsbValue w
+    rw [ih]
+    cases b <;> simp [Nat.bit, Nat.add_comm]
+
+/-- Distinct `k`-bit challenges are distinct modulo `q` when `2 ^ k ≤ q`. -/
+private theorem challenge_ne {q k : ℕ} (hkq : 2 ^ k ≤ q) {c c' : BitString k} (hc : c ≠ c') :
+    (ofBits (List.ofFn c) : ZMod q) ≠ ofBits (List.ofFn c') := by
+  intro h
+  rw [ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff', ofBits_eq_lsbValue, ofBits_eq_lsbValue,
+    Nat.mod_eq_of_lt ((BitString.lsbValue_lt _).trans_le (by simpa using hkq)),
+    Nat.mod_eq_of_lt ((BitString.lsbValue_lt _).trans_le (by simpa using hkq))] at h
+  exact hc (List.ofFn_injective (BitString.lsbValue_injective (by simp) h))
+
+/-- Fermat's little theorem gives the inverse in `extractNat`. -/
+private theorem extractNat_cast {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] {c z c' z' : ℕ}
+    (hc : (c : ZMod q) ≠ c') :
+    (extractNat q c z c' z' : ZMod q) = ((c : ZMod q) - c')⁻¹ * ((z : ZMod q) - z') := by
+  have hsub (a b : ℕ) : (((a % q + q - b % q) % q : ℕ) : ZMod q) = (a : ZMod q) - b := by
+    rw [ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_sub ((Nat.mod_lt _ (Fact.out : q.Prime).pos).le.trans
+      (Nat.le_add_left _ _)), Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_mod, ZMod.natCast_mod, ZMod.natCast_self,
+      add_zero]
+  have hne : (c : ZMod q) - c' ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hc
+  have hinv : ((c : ZMod q) - c') ^ (q - 2) = ((c : ZMod q) - c')⁻¹ := by
+    refine eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_left ?_
+    rw [← pow_succ, show q - 2 + 1 = q - 1 by have := (Fact.out : q.Prime).two_le; lia,
+      ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one hne]
+  simp only [extractNat, Nat.cast_mul, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_pow, hsub, hinv]
+
+/-- Schnorr's protocol on encoded commitments and binary responses, with statements carrying their
+group description; only its verifier is used. -/
+private noncomputable def wordProtocol (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (m : ℕ) :
+    SigmaProtocol ℕ ((d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) (List Bool) (BitString m) (List Bool) where
+  State := Unit
+  commit _ _ := PMF.pure ([], ())
+  respond _ _ _ _ := []
+  verify y t c z := decide (t = F.encode y.1 ((ofBits z : ZMod (F.order y.1)) • F.generator y.1 -
+    (ofBits (List.ofFn c) : ZMod (F.order y.1)) • y.2))
+
+/-- Schnorr key generation at a security parameter, with the description in the statement. -/
+private noncomputable def wordKeyGen (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc)
+    (n : ℕ) : PMF (ℕ × (d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) := do
+  let d ← setup n
+  let α ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  return (α.val, ⟨d, α • F.generator d⟩)
+
+/-- The relation: `x` is a discrete logarithm of the public key. -/
+private def wordRelation (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (x : ℕ) (y : (d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) :
+    Prop :=
+  (x : ZMod (F.order y.1)) • F.generator y.1 = y.2
+
+private noncomputable instance (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) :
+    DecidableRel (wordRelation F) := fun _ _ => Classical.propDecidable _
+
+/-- The extractor of `wordProtocol`. -/
+private def wordExtract (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily) (m : ℕ) (y : (d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d)
+    (_ : List Bool) (c : BitString m) (z : List Bool) (c' : BitString m) (z' : List Bool) : ℕ :=
+  extractNat (F.order y.1) (ofBits (List.ofFn c)) (ofBits z) (ofBits (List.ofFn c')) (ofBits z')
+
+/-- An impersonator as a typed impersonator for `wordProtocol`. -/
+private noncomputable def SchnorrImpersonator.typed (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n m : ℕ) :
+    SigmaProtocol.Impersonator ((d : F.Desc) × F.Carrier d) (List Bool) (BitString m)
+      (List Bool) where
+  State := List Bool
+  commit y := ProbComp.eval (A.commit n (y.1, F.encode y.1 y.2))
+  respond s c := ProbComp.eval (A.respond n (s, List.ofFn c))
+
+private theorem schnorrDirectGame_eq (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ) :
+    F.schnorrDirectGame setup k A n =
+      (wordProtocol F (k n)).directAttack (wordKeyGen F setup n) (A.typed n (k n)) := by
+  simp only [schnorrDirectGame, SigmaProtocol.directAttack, wordKeyGen, wordProtocol,
+    SchnorrImpersonator.typed, BitString.uniformList, Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+    Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.bind_bind, PMF.pure_bind, PMF.bind_map,
+    Function.comp_def]
+
+private theorem specialSoundOn (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) {k : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ}
+    (hkq : ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, 2 ^ k n ≤ F.order d) :
+    (wordProtocol F (k n)).SpecialSoundOn (wordKeyGen F setup n) (wordRelation F)
+      (wordExtract F (k n)) := by
+  rintro ⟨x, d, u⟩ hkey t c z c' z' hc hz hz'
+  have hd : d ∈ (setup n).support := by
+    simp only [wordKeyGen, Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+      Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.mem_support_bind_iff, PMF.mem_support_pure_iff,
+      Prod.mk.injEq, Sigma.mk.injEq] at hkey
+    obtain ⟨d', hd', -, -, -, hdd, -⟩ := hkey
+    exact hdd ▸ hd'
+  simp only [SigmaProtocol.Accepts, wordProtocol, decide_eq_true_eq] at hz hz'
+  have heq := F.encode_injective d (hz.symm.trans hz')
+  have hcne := challenge_ne (hkq d hd) hc
+  simp only [wordRelation, wordExtract, extractNat_cast hcne, mul_smul]
+  rw [sub_smul, sub_eq_sub_iff_sub_eq_sub.mp heq, ← sub_smul,
+    inv_smul_smul₀ (sub_ne_zero.mpr hcne)]
+
+/-- Reading back the binary digits of a number recovers it. -/
+private theorem ofBits_bits (r : ℕ) : ofBits r.bits = r := Nat.foldr_bit_bits r
+
+/-- The rewinding adversary wins the discrete-logarithm game exactly when its output is a witness
+for the generated statement. -/
+private theorem decide_wordRelation (d : F.Desc) (α : ZMod (F.order d)) (r : ℕ) :
+    decide (wordRelation F r ⟨d, α • F.generator d⟩) =
+      decide (((ofBits r.bits : ℕ) : ZMod (F.order d)) = α) := by
+  rw [ofBits_bits]
+  exact decide_eq_decide.mpr ⟨fun h => F.smul_generator_injective d h, fun h => by
+    simp only [wordRelation, h]⟩
+
+private theorem oneWayGame_eq (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ) (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator)
+    (n : ℕ) :
+    SigmaProtocol.oneWayGame (wordKeyGen F setup n) (wordRelation F)
+        ((A.typed n (k n)).rewind (wordExtract F (k n))) =
+      F.discreteLogGame setup (A.rewind k) n := by
+  simp only [SigmaProtocol.oneWayGame, wordKeyGen, discreteLogGame,
+    SigmaProtocol.Impersonator.rewind, SchnorrImpersonator.rewind, SchnorrImpersonator.typed,
+    ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure, BitString.eval_sampleList, BitString.uniformList,
+    Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind, Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.bind_bind,
+    PMF.pure_bind, PMF.bind_map, Function.comp_def, wordExtract, decide_wordRelation]
+
+/-- **Schnorr identification against direct attacks, exact form** ([BonehShoup2023],
+Theorem 19.1): at each security parameter where every possible group has at least `2 ^ k n`
+elements, an impersonator's success probability is at most `1 / 2 ^ k n + √ε'`, where `ε'` is the
+discrete-logarithm success probability of the rewinding adversary. -/
+theorem succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (A : F.SchnorrImpersonator) (n : ℕ) (hkq : ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, 2 ^ k n ≤ F.order d) :
+    (Game.succProbability (F.schnorrDirectGame setup k A n) : ℝ) ≤
+      1 / 2 ^ k n + √(Game.succProbability (F.discreteLogGame setup (A.rewind k) n)) := by
+  have h := SigmaProtocol.succProbability_directAttack_le (specialSoundOn setup hkq)
+    (A.typed n (k n))
+  rw [oneWayGame_eq] at h
+  rw [schnorrDirectGame_eq]
+  simpa only [Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin, Nat.cast_pow,
+    Nat.cast_ofNat] using h
+
+/-! ### Efficiency of the rewinding adversary -/
+
+/-- The extracted witness is computable in polynomial time from the group description and the
+four binary numbers. -/
+@[fun_prop]

+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.Homomorphic.GSW.Serialized.Evaluation
+public import Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Boolean.Modular.InnerProduct
+public import Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Boolean.Modular.Subtract
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.Nat.Bits
+import Mathlib.Data.List.GetD
+
+/-!
+# Selected-row GSW decryption circuits
+
+The input order is the complete serialized secret followed by the complete serialized ciphertext.
+The row selected by the existing total decoder is used on every input, without a key-generation
+or noise hypothesis. Arithmetic circuits preserve residues modulo the word modulus.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.inputWidth`: the complete raw input length.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.circuit`: the actual total raw-input decryptor.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.correct`: agreement with serialized decryption
+  on every well-sized raw input, including widths zero and one and both half-open decoder ties.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.depth_circuit_le`: explicit logarithmic depth.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.size_circuit_le`: explicit polynomial gate count.
+
+## References
+
+* [C. Gentry, A. Sahai, B. Waters][GentrySahaiWaters2013], Sections 3.1 and 3.4.
+* [C. Gentry][Gentry2009], Definition 4: augmented decryption takes all key and ciphertext bits.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit
+
+open Cslib.Circuits Cslib.Circuits.Boolean Cslib.BitString
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+variable {n w : ℕ}
+
+/-- Secret bits precede all square-matrix ciphertext bits. -/
+abbrev inputWidth (n w : ℕ) : ℕ := n * w + ((n + 1) * w) * ((n + 1) * w)
+
+/-- Interpret the raw first block with the same total decoder as the serialized scheme. -/
+private def inputSecret (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) : Fin n → ZMod (2 ^ w) :=
+  decodeSecret n w (List.ofFn (fstBits x))
+
+/-- Interpret every raw ciphertext bit, including ciphertexts outside encryption support. -/
+private def inputCiphertext (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) : Ciphertext n w :=
+  decodeCiphertext n w (List.ofFn (sndBits x))
+
+private theorem inputSecret_apply (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (j : Fin n) :
+    inputSecret x j = ((BitString.equivFin w (block (fstBits x) j) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) := by
+  simp only [inputSecret, decodeSecret, Cslib.Matrix.ofBinary_apply,
+    Cslib.Matrix.binaryEntry, Fin.val_zero, zero_mul, zero_add,
+    listRow_eq_ofFn w j, ofList_ofFn, Nat.foldr_bit_ofFn, BitString.val_equivFin_eq_sum]
+
+/-- Recompose any row's binary word by the same place values as the circuit word convention. -/
+private theorem rowWord_cast (C : Ciphertext n w) (row : Fin (n + 1) × Fin w) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
+    ((BitString.equivFin w (fun l => C row (j, l)) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      recomposeMatrix w (bitMatrix (ZMod (2 ^ w)) C) row j := by
+  simp only [BitString.val_equivFin_eq_sum, Nat.cast_sum, Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_pow,
+    Nat.cast_ofNat, recomposeMatrix, bitCompose, bitMatrix_apply]
+
+private theorem inputCiphertext_apply (x : BitString (inputWidth n w))
+    (i j : Fin (n + 1)) (k l : Fin w) :
+    inputCiphertext x (i, k) (j, l) = x (Fin.natAdd (n * w)
+      (finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (i, k), finProdFinEquiv (j, l)))) := by
+  rw [inputCiphertext, decodeCiphertext_apply]
+  let p := finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (i, k), finProdFinEquiv (j, l))
+  have hp : (i.val * w + k.val) * ((n + 1) * w) + j.val * w + l.val = p.val := by
+    simp only [p, finProdFinEquiv, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Fin.val_mk]
+    ring
+  rw [hp, List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (by simp), List.getElem_ofFn]
+  rfl
+
+/-- The selected row is the last binary digit of the leading expanded-secret coordinate. -/
+private def selectedRow (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Fin (n + 1) × Fin w :=
+  (0, ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩)
+
+/-- Wire one selected-row word directly out of the complete ciphertext input. -/
+private def rowInputs (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
+    Fin w → Fin (inputWidth n w) :=
+  fun l => Fin.natAdd (n * w)
+    (finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (selectedRow n w hw), finProdFinEquiv (j, l)))
+
+private theorem eval_rowInputs (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
+    (Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw j)).eval interpretation x =
+      fun l => inputCiphertext x (selectedRow n w hw) (j, l) := by
+  funext l
+  rw [Circuit.eval_wiring]
+  exact (inputCiphertext_apply x 0 j ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩ l).symm
+
+/-- Consecutive selected-row words paired with the unexpanded secret, omitting column zero. -/
+private def rowTail (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) : BitString (n * w) :=
+  fun i => inputCiphertext x (selectedRow n w hw)
+    ((finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1.succ, (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).2)
+
+private theorem block_rowTail (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) (j : Fin n) :
+    block (rowTail x hw) j = fun l => inputCiphertext x (selectedRow n w hw) (j.succ, l) := by
+  funext l
+  simp only [rowTail, block, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
+
+/-- Feed the complete secret and the non-leading selected-row words to the inner product. -/
+private def productInputs (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Fin (n * w + n * w) → Fin (inputWidth n w) :=
+  Fin.append (m := n * w) (n := n * w)
+    (Fin.castAdd (((n + 1) * w) * ((n + 1) * w)))
+    (fun i => rowInputs n w hw (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1.succ (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).2)
+
+private theorem append_comp_productInputs (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) :
+    x ∘ productInputs n w hw = Fin.append (fstBits x) (rowTail x hw) := by
+  funext i
+  refine Fin.addCases (fun j => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i
+  · simp only [Function.comp_apply, productInputs, Fin.append_left, fstBits]
+  · simp only [Function.comp_apply, productInputs, Fin.append_right, rowTail]
+    exact (inputCiphertext_apply x 0 (finProdFinEquiv.symm j).1.succ
+      ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩ (finProdFinEquiv.symm j).2).symm
+
+/-- The actual selected-row modular inner product, reading directly from raw inputs. -/
+private def productSum (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Circuit signature (inputWidth n w) w :=
+  (Modular.innerProduct n w).comp (Circuit.wiring signature (productInputs n w hw))
+
+private theorem productSum_cast (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) :
+    ((BitString.equivFin w ((productSum n w hw).eval interpretation x) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      ∑ j : Fin n, recomposeMatrix w (bitMatrix (ZMod (2 ^ w)) (inputCiphertext x))
+        (selectedRow n w hw) j.succ * inputSecret x j := by
+  rw [productSum, Circuit.eval_comp, Circuit.eval_wiring, append_comp_productInputs,
+    Modular.val_eval_innerProduct, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_sum]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro j _
+  rw [Nat.cast_mul, ← inputSecret_apply, block_rowTail, rowWord_cast, mul_comm]
+
+/-- Subtract the selected row's inner product from its leading word, modulo `2 ^ w`. -/
+private def phase (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Circuit signature (inputWidth n w) w :=
+  (Modular.subtract w).comp
+    ((Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)).append (productSum n w hw))
+
+/-- The raw circuit phase is exactly the original selected-row residue on every input. -/
+private theorem phase_cast (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) :
+    ((BitString.equivFin w ((phase n w hw).eval interpretation x) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      decryptionPhase (inputSecret x) (inputCiphertext x) (selectedRow n w hw) := by
+  let a := (Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)).eval interpretation x
+  let b := (productSum n w hw).eval interpretation x
+  have ha : ((BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      recomposeMatrix w (bitMatrix (ZMod (2 ^ w)) (inputCiphertext x)) (selectedRow n w hw) 0 := by
+    dsimp only [a]
+    rw [eval_rowInputs]
+    exact rowWord_cast _ _ _
+  have hb := productSum_cast x hw
+  change ((BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) = _ at hb
+  have hv : (BitString.equivFin w ((phase n w hw).eval interpretation x) : ℕ) =
+      (2 ^ w - (BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ)) % 2 ^ w := by
+    simpa only [phase, Circuit.eval_comp, Circuit.eval_append] using Modular.val_eval_subtract a b
+  rw [hv, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_add,
+    Nat.cast_sub (Nat.le_of_lt (BitString.equivFin w b).isLt), ZMod.natCast_self]
+  simp only [ha, hb, decryptionPhase, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm, zero_add]
+
+private theorem testBit_wordValue (x : BitString w) (i : Fin w) :
+    (BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ).testBit i.val = x i := by
+  simpa only [BitVec.getLsbD, toNat_word_eq_equivFin] using getLsbD_word x i
+
+/-- Implement the actual width-zero, width-one and top-two-bit decoder cases. -/
+private def decodeWord (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature w 1 :=
+  if h₀ : w = 0 then Circuit.oneGate (.const false) Fin.elim0
+  else if h₁ : w = 1 then Circuit.wiring signature (fun _ => ⟨0, by omega⟩)
+  else ((Formula.input ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩).xor (.input ⟨w - 2, by omega⟩)).toCircuit
+
+/-- The scalar decoder is computed on every modular word, including both quarter ties. -/
+private theorem eval_decodeWord (x : BitString w) :
+    (decodeWord w).eval interpretation x 0 =
+      decode w ((BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) := by
+  have hv : (((BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)).val) =
+      (BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) := by
+    rw [ZMod.val_natCast, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (BitString.equivFin w x).isLt]
+  by_cases h₀ : w = 0
+  · subst w
+    simp [decodeWord, interpretation]
+  · by_cases h₁ : w = 1
+    · subst w
+      simp only [decodeWord, Nat.one_ne_zero, ↓reduceDIte, Circuit.eval_wiring,
+        Function.comp_apply, decode_one, hv]
+      exact (testBit_wordValue x 0).symm
+    · have hw : 2 ≤ w := by omega
+      rw [decode_eq_xor_highBits hw, hv]
+      simp only [decodeWord, h₀, h₁, ↓reduceDIte, Formula.eval_toCircuit,
+        Formula.eval_xor, Formula.eval_input]
+      rw [testBit_wordValue x ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩,
+        testBit_wordValue x ⟨w - 2, by omega⟩]
+
+private theorem depth_decodeWord_le (w : ℕ) : (decodeWord w).depth ≤ 3 := by
+  unfold decodeWord
+  split_ifs
+  · simp
+  · simp
+  · exact (Formula.depth_toCircuit_le _).trans
+      ((Formula.depth_xor_le _ _).trans (by simp))
+
+private theorem size_decodeWord_le (w : ℕ) : (decodeWord w).size ≤ 5 := by
+  unfold decodeWord
+  split_ifs <;> simp
+
+/-- The actual total GSW decryptor, with all raw secret and ciphertext bits as inputs. -/
+def circuit (n w : ℕ) : Circuit signature (inputWidth n w) 1 :=
+  if hw : 0 < w then (decodeWord w).comp (phase n w hw)
+  else Circuit.oneGate (.const false) Fin.elim0
+
+/-- All raw inputs agree with typed GSW decryption, without generation or noise hypotheses. -/
+private theorem eval_circuit (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) :
+    (circuit n w).eval interpretation x 0 = decrypt (inputSecret x) (inputCiphertext x) := by
+  by_cases hw : 0 < w
+  · rw [circuit, dite_eq_left hw, Circuit.eval_comp, eval_decodeWord, phase_cast x hw,
+      decrypt_eq_decode_decryptionPhase hw]
+    rfl
+  · have hz : w = 0 := by omega
+    subst w
+    simp [circuit, interpretation]
+
+/-- The selected-row construction has logarithmic depth in both parameter dimensions. -/
+theorem depth_circuit_le (n w : ℕ) :
+    (circuit n w).depth ≤ 28 + 18 * Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) + 12 * Nat.clog 2 n := by
+  have hp : ∀ hw, (productSum n w hw).depth ≤
+      17 + 16 * Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) + 12 * Nat.clog 2 n := by
+    intro hw
+    exact (Circuit.depth_comp_le _ _).trans (by
+      simpa only [Circuit.depth_wiring, add_zero] using Modular.depth_innerProduct_le n w)
+  have hphase : ∀ hw, (phase n w hw).depth ≤
+      25 + 18 * Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) + 12 * Nat.clog 2 n := by
+    intro hw
+    have ha := Circuit.depth_append_le
+      (Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)) (productSum n w hw)
+    simp only [Circuit.depth_wiring, zero_max] at ha
+    have hc := Circuit.depth_comp_le (Modular.subtract w)
+      ((Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)).append (productSum n w hw))
+    have hs := Modular.depth_subtract_le w
+    have hi := hp hw
+    change (phase n w hw).depth ≤ _ at hc
+    omega
+  unfold circuit
+  split_ifs with hw
+  · have hc := Circuit.depth_comp_le (decodeWord w) (phase n w hw)
+    have hd := depth_decodeWord_le w
+    have hp := hphase hw
+    omega
+  · simp only [Circuit.depth_oneGate]
+    omega
+
+/-- Polynomial gate count includes all unused fallback gates in the balanced construction. -/
+theorem size_circuit_le (n w : ℕ) :
+    (circuit n w).size ≤ 131 * (n + 1) * (w + 1) ^ 2 := by
+  unfold circuit
+  split_ifs with hw
+  · simp only [Circuit.size_comp, phase, productSum, Circuit.size_append,
+      Circuit.size_wiring, zero_add]
+    have hd := size_decodeWord_le w
+    have hs := Modular.size_subtract_le w
+    have hi := Modular.size_innerProduct_le n w
+    nlinarith [Nat.zero_le n, Nat.zero_le (n * w), Nat.zero_le (n * w ^ 2)]
+  · simp only [Circuit.size_oneGate]
+    nlinarith [Nat.zero_le n, Nat.zero_le (n * w), Nat.zero_le (n * w ^ 2)]
+
+/-- The serialized contract required by generic refresh: every well-sized raw pair is covered. -/
+theorem correct (n w : ℕ) (secret ciphertext : List Bool)

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body: Please qualify the inverse claim by a prime modulus and a nonzero residue, or simply say that `unitInv p j` computes `(j + 1) ^ (p - 2)` modulo `p` by repeated multiplication. `unitInv_inSpace` itself is quantified over arbitrary `p, j`; the actual inverse theorem `Reader.cast_unitInv_eq` in `Reader/Arith.lean` uses `[Fact p.Prime]` and `j < p - 1`. For example, 3 is a unit modulo 8 but `3 ^ (8 - 2) % 8 = 1`, not its inverse 3. The new unqualified sentence overstates what this certificate says.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body: Both this new docstring and the one on `eval_mem_reedSolomon` call the code “of dimension `k`”, but these statements allow arbitrary evaluation maps and arbitrary `k`. With one evaluation position and `k = 2`, the code cannot have dimension two. The later `finrank_reedSolomon` theorem needs distinct points and `k ≤ Fintype.card ι`. Please use “with degree bound `k`” or simply `reedSolomon α k` in both. The existing definition docstring repeats the same phrase and could be corrected alongside them; no theorem change is needed.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
`forkingAlgorithm` filters the returned position only by `j < q`. For `program _ := pure (some 0, ())`, `q = 1`, `H = Bool`, acceptance is 1 and the fork succeeds with probability 1/2, yet both query lists are empty. Thus `take (j + 1)` equality does not establish that the named query exists, as the module/PR claim for extraction.

Please either validate the named position against the actual transcript (updating acceptance accordingly), or add a valid-naming hypothesis to the semantic support API. The resulting theorem should establish `j.val < out.2.length` and the corresponding fact for `out'`, with equality of the queries at `j`. Keep the unrestricted numeric lemma if useful. Check a zero-query program that returns `some 0`, alongside the existing genuine one-query client; the invalid name must not imply a common query.

@@ -0,0 +1,251 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Oracle.Transcript
+public import Complexity.Probability.Forking
+import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Presample
+import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Repeat
+import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+import Complexity.Probability.Product
+
+/-!
+# Forking oracle programs
+
+An oracle program `P s : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)`, with explicit coins
+`s`, asks queries whose answers lie in a finite set `H` and finally names one of its queries by
+its position, or none. Forking runs it with uniform answers and, if it names the query at
+position `j`, runs it again on the same coins with the same answers before `j` and fresh answers
+from `j` on. Both runs ask the same first `j + 1` queries (`mem_support_fork`), so the named
+query is the same, while its two answers differ.
+
+`runWithAnswers` runs a program on a list of answers, deterministically, recording its queries.
+Answering queries from `q` presampled uniform answers has the law of answering them uniformly as
+they come, when the program asks at most `q` queries: this is the presampling theorem
+`ProbOracleComp.HasQueryBounds.eval_presample` (`interpret_uniform_eq`). Hence the general forking
+lemma (`Probability.Forking.le_add_sqrt_fork`) bounds the acceptance probability of the program
+with uniform answers by `q / |H| + √(q · frk)` (`le_add_sqrt_fork`).
+
+The coins are explicit: the second run replays them. A program with private randomness is put in
+this form by drawing its coins in advance. The statements are exact; no efficiency is involved.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.runWithAnswers`: run on a list of answers, recording the queries.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.indexBelow`: the named position, if it is below `q`.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.forkingAlgorithm`: a program on coins and an answer vector, for forking.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.interpret_uniform_eq`: uniform answers as they come, or presampled.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.le_add_sqrt_fork`: the forking lemma for oracle programs.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.mem_support_fork`: both runs of a successful fork ask the same queries up to
+  the named one, and answer it differently.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.take_runWithAnswers`: a program's first `n + 1` queries depend only on its
+  first `n` answers.
+
+## References
+
+* [M. Bellare, G. Neven, *Multi-Signatures in the Plain Public-Key Model and a General Forking
+  Lemma*][BellareNeven2006], Lemma 1.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Lemma 19.8.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.OracleComp
+
+open Probability
+
+variable {Query H α : Type}
+
+/-- Run a program on a list of answers, in order, answering `default` once the list is exhausted;
+return its result and its queries, in order. -/
+def runWithAnswers (default : H) : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α → List H → α × List Query
+  | .pure a, _ => (a, [])
+  | .liftBind q cont, answers =>
+    ((runWithAnswers default (cont (answers.headD default)) answers.tail).1,
+      q :: (runWithAnswers default (cont (answers.headD default)) answers.tail).2)
+
+/-- A program's first `n + 1` queries depend only on the first `n` answers. -/
+theorem take_runWithAnswers (default : H) (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) :
+    ∀ {answers answers' : List H} {n : ℕ}, answers.take n = answers'.take n →
+      (runWithAnswers default program answers).2.take (n + 1) =
+        (runWithAnswers default program answers').2.take (n + 1) := by
+  induction program with
+  | pure a => intros; rfl
+  | liftBind q cont ih =>
+    intro answers answers' n h
+    cases n with
+    | zero => rfl
+    | succ n =>
+      have hsplit : answers.headD default = answers'.headD default ∧
+          answers.tail.take n = answers'.tail.take n := by
+        cases answers <;> cases answers' <;> simp_all
+      simp only [runWithAnswers, List.take_succ_cons, hsplit.1, ih _ hsplit.2]
+
+/-! ### Presampled answers -/
+
+/-- Answering the lifted program from a saved list is running it on that list. -/
+private theorem eval_run_withSampleList (default : H)
+    (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) (answers : List H) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((fun (result, next, _) => (result, next)) <$>
+      (interpret (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun n => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin n))
+        (withSampleList default fun v _ s => (pure (v, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))))
+          (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+            program)).run ((), answers)) =
+      PMF.pure ((runWithAnswers default program answers).1, ()) := by
+  induction program generalizing answers with
+  | pure a => rfl
+  | liftBind q cont ih =>
+    change _ = PMF.pure ((runWithAnswers default (cont (answers.headD default)) answers.tail).1, ())
+    rw [← ih (answers.headD default) answers.tail]
+    rfl
+
+/-- Answering lifted queries uniformly as they come is answering them uniformly. -/
+private theorem eval_run_uniform [Fintype H] [Nonempty H]
+    (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((interpret (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun n => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin n))
+        (fun _ s => do
+          let value ← ProbComp.uniform H
+          (pure (value, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))))
+          (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+            program)).run ()) =
+      (interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program).map (·, ()) := by
+  have hstate : (fun (_ : Query) (s : Unit) => do
+      let value ← ProbComp.uniform H
+      (pure (value, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))) =
+      fun _ s => (fun a => (a, s)) <$> ProbComp.uniform H := by
+    funext _ s
+    rw [map_eq_bind_pure_comp]
+    rfl
+  have heval : ProbComp.eval (interpret (fun _ => ProbComp.uniform H) program) =
+      interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program := by
+    change interpret ProbComp.unifOracle (interpret _ program) = _
+    rw [interpret_interpret]
+    congr 1
+    funext q
+    exact ProbComp.eval_uniform H
+  rw [interpret_interpret]
+  simp only [ProbOracleComp.interpret_query]
+  rw [hstate, run_interpret_stateless, ProbComp.eval_map, heval]
+
+/-- `q` uniform samples, collected in a list, are the entries of a uniform vector. -/
+private theorem eval_replicate_uniform [Fintype H] [Nonempty H] (q : ℕ) :
+    ProbComp.eval (replicate q (ProbComp.uniform H)) =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin q → H)).map List.ofFn := by
+  induction q with
+  | zero =>
+    have hconst : (List.ofFn : (Fin 0 → H) → List H) = Function.const _ [] :=
+      funext fun _ => List.ofFn_zero
+    rw [replicate_zero, ProbComp.eval_pure, hconst, PMF.map_const]
+  | succ q ih =>
+    rw [replicate_succ, ← Probability.PMF.pi_uniformOfFintype, Probability.PMF.pi_fin_succ,
+      Probability.PMF.pi_uniformOfFintype]
+    simp only [ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_map, ProbComp.eval_uniform, ih, PMF.map_bind,
+      PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, List.ofFn_succ, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ]
+
+/-- The lazy law of uniform answers is the law of `q` presampled uniform answers, for a program
+asking at most `q` queries: an instance of the presampling theorem
+`ProbOracleComp.HasQueryBounds.eval_presample`. -/
+theorem interpret_uniform_eq [Fintype H] [Nonempty H] (default : H)
+    (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) {size : Query → ℕ} {q maxSize : ℕ}
+    (hq : (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+      program).HasQueryBounds size q maxSize) :
+    interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin q → H)).map fun h =>
+        (runWithAnswers default program (List.ofFn h)).1 := by
+  have hp := hq.eval_presample (ProbComp.uniform H) default
+    (fun v _ s => (pure (v, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))) ()
+  rw [eval_run_uniform, ProbComp.eval_bind, eval_replicate_uniform] at hp
+  simp only [eval_run_withSampleList, PMF.bind_map, Function.comp_def] at hp
+  have hfst := congrArg (PMF.map Prod.fst) hp
+  simp only [PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def] at hfst
+  rw [show PMF.map (fun x => x) (interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program) =
+    interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program from PMF.map_id _] at hfst
+  rw [← hfst, PMF.map_bind]
+  simp only [PMF.pure_map]
+  rfl
+
+/-! ### Forking -/
+
+/-- The named position, if it is below `q`. -/
+def indexBelow (q : ℕ) (position : Option ℕ) : Option (Fin q) :=
+  position.bind fun j => if h : j < q then some ⟨j, h⟩ else none
+
+/-- A program with explicit coins as an algorithm on coins and `q` answers, for the general
+forking lemma: the named position below `q`, and the result with the queries. -/
+def forkingAlgorithm {S β : Type} (default : H) (q : ℕ)
+    (program : S → OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)) (s : S) (h : Fin q → H) :
+    Option (Fin q) × ((Option ℕ × β) × List Query) :=
+  (indexBelow q (runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h)).1.1,
+    runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h))
+
+variable {S β : Type} [Fintype H] [Nonempty H] [DecidableEq H]
+
+/-- **The forking lemma for oracle programs** ([BellareNeven2006], Lemma 1): if a program with
+explicit coins asks at most `q` queries, and names a position below `q` with probability `acc`
+when its queries are answered uniformly as they come, then forking it succeeds with probability
+`frk` such that `acc ≤ q / |H| + √(q · frk)`. -/
+theorem le_add_sqrt_fork (first : PMF S)
+    (program : S → OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)) (default : H)
+    {size : Query → ℕ} {q maxSize : ℕ}
+    (hq : ∀ s, (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+      (program s)).HasQueryBounds size q maxSize) :
+    ((do
+      let s ← first
+      let result ← interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) (program s)
+      return (indexBelow q result.1).isSome : PMF Bool) true).toReal ≤
+      q / Fintype.card H + √(q * ((Forking.fork first (forkingAlgorithm default q program)).map
+        Option.isSome true).toReal) := by
+  have hacc : (do
+      let s ← first
+      let result ← interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) (program s)
+      return (indexBelow q result.1).isSome : PMF Bool) =
+      Forking.accept first (forkingAlgorithm default q program) := by
+    simp only [Forking.accept, forkingAlgorithm, Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+      Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure]
+    refine congrArg _ (funext fun s => ?_)
+    rw [interpret_uniform_eq default (program s) (hq s), PMF.bind_map]
+    rfl
+  rw [hacc]
+  exact Forking.le_add_sqrt_fork first _
+
+/-- A successful fork of a program reruns it on the same coins with answers that agree before the
+named position `j` and differ at it; both runs name `j` and ask the same first `j + 1`
+queries. -/
+theorem mem_support_fork {first : PMF S}
+    {program : S → OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)} {default : H} {q : ℕ}
+    {j : Fin q} {out out' : (Option ℕ × β) × List Query}
+    (hfork : some (j, out, out') ∈
+      (Forking.fork first (forkingAlgorithm default q program)).support) :
+    ∃ s ∈ first.support, ∃ h h' : Fin q → H, (∀ i < j, h i = h' i) ∧ h j ≠ h' j ∧
+      out = runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h) ∧
+      out' = runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h') ∧
+      out.1.1 = some j.val ∧ out'.1.1 = some j.val ∧ out.2.take (j + 1) = out'.2.take (j + 1) := by
