body: [P2] State explicitly that this is an erased-abort view, not the full interactive verifier view. An identification verifier already received the commitment before deciding the challenge; restarting does not erase that observation. By contrast, aborted signing attempts can remain unpublished. The implemented projection to `none` is coherent and matches the agreed milestone, but this paragraph currently makes its justification sound like full interactive-view ZK. Please distinguish the two views and leave full-view simulation as a separate claim. Lyubashevsky 2009 makes the ID-retry/signature-publication distinction on PDF page 7: https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/978-3-642-10366-7_35.pdf#page=7 . No interaction-model redesign is requested. — Codex review_559

+/-!
+# Sigma protocols with aborts
+
+In lattice-based Sigma protocols the prover may refuse to answer a challenge: in Lyubashevsky's
+*Fiat–Shamir with aborts* ([Lyubashevsky2009], [Lyubashevsky2012]) it withholds every response
+that would leak information about its witness. Such a protocol is an ordinary `SigmaProtocol`
+whose responses are `Option Z`. The prover answers `none` to abort, and the verifier is expected
+to reject `none`.
+
+Aborted runs are never published: an identification prover starts over, and a signer retries

body: [P3] Qualify this easy-instance argument by `w > 0`, and document the zero-width exception. At `w = 0`, every word decodes to the zero integer vector, so this experiment returns false for every adversary, even with no rows, one column and bound 1; meanwhile the integer vector `[1]` is an SIS solution modulo 1. I checked both facts in a warning-strict Lean probe. This does not invalidate `decode_toBinary`, whose `2β < q` premise excludes that example, but the current unconditional claim that larger bounds make the experiment easy is false at this allowed parameter. A documentation clarification suffices. — Codex review_559

+/-!
+# The short integer solution problem with power-of-two moduli
+
+A short integer solution ([Ajtai1996]) for a matrix `A ∈ ℤ_q^{n×ι}` and a bound `β` is a nonzero
+integer vector `z` with every coordinate in `[-β, β]` and `A z ≡ 0 (mod q)`
+(`SIS.IsSolution`). It is a predicate for any modulus and index types, so that protocols can
+extract solutions for matrices such as `[A | T]`.
+
+The SIS experiment draws a uniform `A ∈ ℤ_q^{n×m}` with `q = 2 ^ w`, and gives a program the
+unary security parameter and the row-major binary word of `A`, as for `DecisionLWE`. The program
+answers with `m` residues of `w` bits each, read through their centered representatives in
+`(-q/2, q/2]` (`SIS.decode`), and wins when these form a short integer solution. `SIS n m w β`
+asserts that every uniform strict PPT program wins with negligible probability.
+
+The centered reading loses nothing when `2 β < q`: every short integer solution is decoded from
+the word of its own residues (`SIS.decode_toBinary`). Larger bounds make the experiment easy once
+`m > n`: every nonzero kernel vector modulo `q` then qualifies, and `2 ^ (w - 1)` times a kernel

Fixed in `16b8e361` and `9f7e34d0`:
- **Validity.** `forkingAlgorithm` now names a position only through `validIndex q count position`, which needs `j < q` and `j < count`, where `count` is the number of queries the run actually made.
- **Acceptance** is measured by the matching counted run, `countingUniform`, through the presampling equality `run_interpret_countingUniform_eq`.
- **`mem_support_fork`** now also gives `∃ query, out.2[j]? = some query ∧ out'.2[j]? = some query`, alongside the truncated-list equality.
- **Regression test.** `nameWithoutAsking := pure (some 0, ())` with `q = 1` has fork success probability `0`.
- The numeric Bellare–Neven lemma is unchanged. All six gates pass.

@@ -0,0 +1,251 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Oracle.Transcript
+public import Complexity.Probability.Forking
+import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Presample
+import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Repeat
+import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+import Complexity.Probability.Product
+
+/-!
+# Forking oracle programs
+
+An oracle program `P s : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)`, with explicit coins
+`s`, asks queries whose answers lie in a finite set `H` and finally names one of its queries by
+its position, or none. Forking runs it with uniform answers and, if it names the query at
+position `j`, runs it again on the same coins with the same answers before `j` and fresh answers
+from `j` on. Both runs ask the same first `j + 1` queries (`mem_support_fork`), so the named
+query is the same, while its two answers differ.
+
+`runWithAnswers` runs a program on a list of answers, deterministically, recording its queries.
+Answering queries from `q` presampled uniform answers has the law of answering them uniformly as
+they come, when the program asks at most `q` queries: this is the presampling theorem
+`ProbOracleComp.HasQueryBounds.eval_presample` (`interpret_uniform_eq`). Hence the general forking
+lemma (`Probability.Forking.le_add_sqrt_fork`) bounds the acceptance probability of the program
+with uniform answers by `q / |H| + √(q · frk)` (`le_add_sqrt_fork`).
+
+The coins are explicit: the second run replays them. A program with private randomness is put in
+this form by drawing its coins in advance. The statements are exact; no efficiency is involved.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.runWithAnswers`: run on a list of answers, recording the queries.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.indexBelow`: the named position, if it is below `q`.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.forkingAlgorithm`: a program on coins and an answer vector, for forking.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.interpret_uniform_eq`: uniform answers as they come, or presampled.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.le_add_sqrt_fork`: the forking lemma for oracle programs.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.mem_support_fork`: both runs of a successful fork ask the same queries up to
+  the named one, and answer it differently.
+* `Cslib.OracleComp.take_runWithAnswers`: a program's first `n + 1` queries depend only on its
+  first `n` answers.
+
+## References
+
+* [M. Bellare, G. Neven, *Multi-Signatures in the Plain Public-Key Model and a General Forking
+  Lemma*][BellareNeven2006], Lemma 1.
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Lemma 19.8.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.OracleComp
+
+open Probability
+
+variable {Query H α : Type}
+
+/-- Run a program on a list of answers, in order, answering `default` once the list is exhausted;
+return its result and its queries, in order. -/
+def runWithAnswers (default : H) : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α → List H → α × List Query
+  | .pure a, _ => (a, [])
+  | .liftBind q cont, answers =>
+    ((runWithAnswers default (cont (answers.headD default)) answers.tail).1,
+      q :: (runWithAnswers default (cont (answers.headD default)) answers.tail).2)
+
+/-- A program's first `n + 1` queries depend only on the first `n` answers. -/
+theorem take_runWithAnswers (default : H) (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) :
+    ∀ {answers answers' : List H} {n : ℕ}, answers.take n = answers'.take n →
+      (runWithAnswers default program answers).2.take (n + 1) =
+        (runWithAnswers default program answers').2.take (n + 1) := by
+  induction program with
+  | pure a => intros; rfl
+  | liftBind q cont ih =>
+    intro answers answers' n h
+    cases n with
+    | zero => rfl
+    | succ n =>
+      have hsplit : answers.headD default = answers'.headD default ∧
+          answers.tail.take n = answers'.tail.take n := by
+        cases answers <;> cases answers' <;> simp_all
+      simp only [runWithAnswers, List.take_succ_cons, hsplit.1, ih _ hsplit.2]
+
+/-! ### Presampled answers -/
+
+/-- Answering the lifted program from a saved list is running it on that list. -/
+private theorem eval_run_withSampleList (default : H)
+    (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) (answers : List H) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((fun (result, next, _) => (result, next)) <$>
+      (interpret (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun n => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin n))
+        (withSampleList default fun v _ s => (pure (v, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))))
+          (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+            program)).run ((), answers)) =
+      PMF.pure ((runWithAnswers default program answers).1, ()) := by
+  induction program generalizing answers with
+  | pure a => rfl
+  | liftBind q cont ih =>
+    change _ = PMF.pure ((runWithAnswers default (cont (answers.headD default)) answers.tail).1, ())
+    rw [← ih (answers.headD default) answers.tail]
+    rfl
+
+/-- Answering lifted queries uniformly as they come is answering them uniformly. -/
+private theorem eval_run_uniform [Fintype H] [Nonempty H]
+    (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((interpret (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun n => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin n))
+        (fun _ s => do
+          let value ← ProbComp.uniform H
+          (pure (value, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))))
+          (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+            program)).run ()) =
+      (interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program).map (·, ()) := by
+  have hstate : (fun (_ : Query) (s : Unit) => do
+      let value ← ProbComp.uniform H
+      (pure (value, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))) =
+      fun _ s => (fun a => (a, s)) <$> ProbComp.uniform H := by
+    funext _ s
+    rw [map_eq_bind_pure_comp]
+    rfl
+  have heval : ProbComp.eval (interpret (fun _ => ProbComp.uniform H) program) =
+      interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program := by
+    change interpret ProbComp.unifOracle (interpret _ program) = _
+    rw [interpret_interpret]
+    congr 1
+    funext q
+    exact ProbComp.eval_uniform H
+  rw [interpret_interpret]
+  simp only [ProbOracleComp.interpret_query]
+  rw [hstate, run_interpret_stateless, ProbComp.eval_map, heval]
+
+/-- `q` uniform samples, collected in a list, are the entries of a uniform vector. -/
+private theorem eval_replicate_uniform [Fintype H] [Nonempty H] (q : ℕ) :
+    ProbComp.eval (replicate q (ProbComp.uniform H)) =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin q → H)).map List.ofFn := by
+  induction q with
+  | zero =>
+    have hconst : (List.ofFn : (Fin 0 → H) → List H) = Function.const _ [] :=
+      funext fun _ => List.ofFn_zero
+    rw [replicate_zero, ProbComp.eval_pure, hconst, PMF.map_const]
+  | succ q ih =>
+    rw [replicate_succ, ← Probability.PMF.pi_uniformOfFintype, Probability.PMF.pi_fin_succ,
+      Probability.PMF.pi_uniformOfFintype]
+    simp only [ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_map, ProbComp.eval_uniform, ih, PMF.map_bind,
+      PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, List.ofFn_succ, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ]
+
+/-- The lazy law of uniform answers is the law of `q` presampled uniform answers, for a program
+asking at most `q` queries: an instance of the presampling theorem
+`ProbOracleComp.HasQueryBounds.eval_presample`. -/
+theorem interpret_uniform_eq [Fintype H] [Nonempty H] (default : H)
+    (program : OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) α) {size : Query → ℕ} {q maxSize : ℕ}
+    (hq : (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+      program).HasQueryBounds size q maxSize) :
+    interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin q → H)).map fun h =>
+        (runWithAnswers default program (List.ofFn h)).1 := by
+  have hp := hq.eval_presample (ProbComp.uniform H) default
+    (fun v _ s => (pure (v, s) : ProbComp (H × Unit))) ()
+  rw [eval_run_uniform, ProbComp.eval_bind, eval_replicate_uniform] at hp
+  simp only [eval_run_withSampleList, PMF.bind_map, Function.comp_def] at hp
+  have hfst := congrArg (PMF.map Prod.fst) hp
+  simp only [PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def] at hfst
+  rw [show PMF.map (fun x => x) (interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program) =
+    interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) program from PMF.map_id _] at hfst
+  rw [← hfst, PMF.map_bind]
+  simp only [PMF.pure_map]
+  rfl
+
+/-! ### Forking -/
+
+/-- The named position, if it is below `q`. -/
+def indexBelow (q : ℕ) (position : Option ℕ) : Option (Fin q) :=
+  position.bind fun j => if h : j < q then some ⟨j, h⟩ else none
+
+/-- A program with explicit coins as an algorithm on coins and `q` answers, for the general
+forking lemma: the named position below `q`, and the result with the queries. -/
+def forkingAlgorithm {S β : Type} (default : H) (q : ℕ)
+    (program : S → OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)) (s : S) (h : Fin q → H) :
+    Option (Fin q) × ((Option ℕ × β) × List Query) :=
+  (indexBelow q (runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h)).1.1,
+    runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h))
+
+variable {S β : Type} [Fintype H] [Nonempty H] [DecidableEq H]
+
+/-- **The forking lemma for oracle programs** ([BellareNeven2006], Lemma 1): if a program with
+explicit coins asks at most `q` queries, and names a position below `q` with probability `acc`
+when its queries are answered uniformly as they come, then forking it succeeds with probability
+`frk` such that `acc ≤ q / |H| + √(q · frk)`. -/
+theorem le_add_sqrt_fork (first : PMF S)
+    (program : S → OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)) (default : H)
+    {size : Query → ℕ} {q maxSize : ℕ}
+    (hq : ∀ s, (interpret (fun q => ProbOracleComp.query (spec := fun _ : Query => H) q)
+      (program s)).HasQueryBounds size q maxSize) :
+    ((do
+      let s ← first
+      let result ← interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) (program s)
+      return (indexBelow q result.1).isSome : PMF Bool) true).toReal ≤
+      q / Fintype.card H + √(q * ((Forking.fork first (forkingAlgorithm default q program)).map
+        Option.isSome true).toReal) := by
+  have hacc : (do
+      let s ← first
+      let result ← interpret (fun _ => PMF.uniformOfFintype H) (program s)
+      return (indexBelow q result.1).isSome : PMF Bool) =
+      Forking.accept first (forkingAlgorithm default q program) := by
+    simp only [Forking.accept, forkingAlgorithm, Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+      Probability.PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure]
+    refine congrArg _ (funext fun s => ?_)
+    rw [interpret_uniform_eq default (program s) (hq s), PMF.bind_map]
+    rfl
+  rw [hacc]
+  exact Forking.le_add_sqrt_fork first _
+
+/-- A successful fork of a program reruns it on the same coins with answers that agree before the
+named position `j` and differ at it; both runs name `j` and ask the same first `j + 1`
+queries. -/
+theorem mem_support_fork {first : PMF S}
+    {program : S → OracleComp (fun _ : Query => H) (Option ℕ × β)} {default : H} {q : ℕ}
+    {j : Fin q} {out out' : (Option ℕ × β) × List Query}
+    (hfork : some (j, out, out') ∈
+      (Forking.fork first (forkingAlgorithm default q program)).support) :
+    ∃ s ∈ first.support, ∃ h h' : Fin q → H, (∀ i < j, h i = h' i) ∧ h j ≠ h' j ∧
+      out = runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h) ∧
+      out' = runWithAnswers default (program s) (List.ofFn h') ∧
+      out.1.1 = some j.val ∧ out'.1.1 = some j.val ∧ out.2.take (j + 1) = out'.2.take (j + 1) := by

+/-

+
+import Complexity.Foundations.BooleanAnalysis.HadamardTester
+import Complexity.Foundations.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Derivative
+import Complexity.Foundations.BooleanAnalysis.MirrorSets
+import Complexity.Foundations.BooleanAnalysis.MultilinearExtension
+import Complexity.Foundations.BooleanAnalysis.Noise
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.Finset.Expect
+
+/-! # Boolean analysis on small cubes
+
+Concrete instances of the Boolean analysis API, mostly on the cube `Fin 2 → Bool`. The
+conjunction of two bits has BLR acceptance `5 / 8`, so linearity testing certifies a parity at
+distance at most one, and that bound is attained. Its noise sensitivity `δ - δ ^ 2 / 2`, total
+influence `1`, influence `1 / 2`, Fourier coefficient `-1 / 2` and multilinear extension
+`z₀ z₁` are computed. Korten's mirror-set and light-patterns lemmas are applied to sets that
+satisfy their hypotheses, and the Hadamard tester to honest tables at positive error. The
+examples show that the hypotheses of these results are satisfiable and that the definitions
+compute the values their docstrings describe.
+-/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.BooleanAnalysisExamples
+
+open Cslib Cslib.BitString Finset
+
+/-- The conjunction of two bits. -/
+def and₂ (x : Fin 2 → Bool) : Bool :=
+  x 0 && x 1
+
+/-! ### Fourier coefficients -/
+
+-- The coefficient of a character is one on its own set and zero on any other.
+example : fourierCoeff (chi ℝ ({0, 1} : Finset (Fin 2))) {0, 1} = 1 ∧
+    fourierCoeff (chi ℝ ({0, 1} : Finset (Fin 2))) {1} = 0 := by
+  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
+  · rw [fourierCoeff, expect_chi_mul_chi, ite_eq_left rfl]
+  · rw [fourierCoeff, expect_chi_mul_chi, ite_eq_right (by decide)]
+
+-- The coefficient of the conjunction, read as signs, on both coordinates, from the definition.
+example : fourierCoeff (fun x => signVal (and₂ x)) {0, 1} = -1 / 2 := by
+  simp only [fourierCoeff, Fin.expect_univ_cons, Fintype.expect_bool, Fintype.expect_unique]
+  simp [chi, and₂]
+
+/-! ### Linearity testing -/
+
+/-- The BLR test accepts the conjunction of two bits on `10` of the `16` pairs. -/
+theorem blrAcceptance_and₂ : blrAcceptance and₂ = 5 / 8 := by
+  simp only [blrAcceptance, Fin.expect_univ_cons, Fintype.expect_bool, Fintype.expect_unique]
+  simp [and₂, Bool.add_eq_xor]

+reduction on a path, the ball bound on the 5-cycle, the central binomial and tail bounds at
+explicit sizes, and the expander mixing lemma, simple rotation maps, homomorphisms and connected
+components on small rotation maps. This shows that the hypotheses are satisfiable and pins down
+the counting conventions (for instance that `interedges` counts darts).
+-/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.CombinatoricsExamples
+
+open Cslib Finset SimpleGraph
+
+/-! ### Sunflowers -/
+
+-- Three edges through a common vertex are a sunflower whose core is that vertex.
+private theorem isSunflower_star :
+    IsSunflower ({{0, 1}, {0, 2}, {0, 3}} : Finset (Finset (Fin 5))) {0} := by
+  unfold IsSunflower Set.Pairwise
+  simp only [mem_coe]
+  decide
+
+-- The edges of `K₅` contain that sunflower directly.
+example : ContainsSunflower 3 ((univ : Finset (Fin 5)).powersetCard 2) :=
+  ⟨{{0, 1}, {0, 2}, {0, 3}}, by decide, by decide, {0}, isSunflower_star⟩
+
+-- The sunflower lemma finds it too: `K₅` has `10 > (3 - 1) ^ 2 * 2! = 8` edges. Compare
+-- `Sunflower.not_containsSunflower_twoTriangles`, six edges and no such sunflower.
+example : ContainsSunflower 3 ((univ : Finset (Fin 5)).powersetCard 2) :=
+  containsSunflower_of_forall_card_le 3 2 _ (fun _ hs => (mem_powersetCard.1 hs).2.le)
+    (by decide)
+
+-- Plucking the singletons `{0}, {1}, {2}` with two petals must end at `{∅}`: the normal form has
+-- at most `sunflowerBound 2 1 = 1` set, and that set lies inside both `{0}` and `{1}`.
+example : pluckNormalForm 2 ({{0}, {1}, {2}} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))) = {∅} := by
+  set F : Finset (Finset (Fin 3)) := {{0}, {1}, {2}}
+  have hcard : (pluckNormalForm 2 F).card ≤ 1 :=
+    card_pluckNormalForm_le (w := 1) le_rfl (by decide)
+  obtain ⟨t, ht, ht0⟩ := exists_subset_of_mem_pluckNormalForm (p := 2) (s := {0})
+    (show {0} ∈ F by decide)
+  obtain ⟨u, hu, hu1⟩ := exists_subset_of_mem_pluckNormalForm (p := 2) (s := {1})
+    (show {1} ∈ F by decide)
+  obtain rfl : t = u := card_le_one.1 hcard t ht u hu
+  obtain rfl : t = ∅ := eq_empty_of_forall_notMem fun x hx => by
+    have h0 := mem_singleton.1 (ht0 hx)
+    have h1 := mem_singleton.1 (hu1 hx)
+    exact absurd (h0.symm.trans h1) (by decide)
+  exact eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.2 ⟨ht, fun x hx => card_le_one.1 hcard x hx ∅ ht⟩
+
+-- Plucking the edges of `K₅` with three petals leaves at most eight sets and no such sunflower.
+example : (pluckNormalForm 3 ((univ : Finset (Fin 5)).powersetCard 2)).card ≤ 8 ∧
+    ¬ ContainsSunflower 3 (pluckNormalForm 3 ((univ : Finset (Fin 5)).powersetCard 2)) :=
+  ⟨card_pluckNormalForm_le (w := 2) (by decide) fun _ hs => (mem_powersetCard.1 hs).2.le,
+    not_containsSunflower_pluckNormalForm (by decide) _⟩
+
+/-! ### Valiant's depth reduction -/
+
+/-- The directed path `0 → 1 → 2 → 3`. -/
+private def pathEdges : Finset (Fin 4 × Fin 4) := {(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)}
+
+-- Numbering the vertices grades the path with `2 ^ 2` levels.
+private theorem isGrading_pathEdges : IsGrading pathEdges (2 ^ 2) fun v => v.val :=
+  ⟨fun v => v.isLt, by decide⟩
+
+-- The whole path has no grading with two levels.
+private theorem not_isGrading_pathEdges (g : Fin 4 → ℕ) : ¬ IsGrading pathEdges 2 g := by
+  rintro ⟨hlt, hE⟩
+  have h01 := hE (0, 1) (by decide)
+  have h12 := hE (1, 2) (by decide)
+  have := hlt 2
+  simp only at h01 h12
+  omega
+
+-- One round of depth reduction (`k = 2`, `r = 1`) removes at most `3 / 2` of the edges; since the
+-- path has no two-level grading, it removes exactly one.
+example : ∃ F ⊆ pathEdges, #F = 1 ∧ ∃ g : Fin 4 → ℕ, IsGrading (pathEdges \ F) 2 g := by
+  obtain ⟨F, hF, hcard, g, hg⟩ := isGrading_pathEdges.exists_sdiff (r := 1) (by norm_num)
+  refine ⟨F, hF, ?_, g, hg⟩
+  have h3 : #pathEdges = 3 := by decide
+  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos #F with h | h
+  · rw [card_eq_zero.1 h, sdiff_empty] at hg
+    exact absurd hg (not_isGrading_pathEdges g)
+  · omega
+
+/-! ### Balls in graphs of bounded degree -/
+
+-- In the 5-cycle, of maximum degree `2`, the closed ball of radius `1` has at most
+-- `(2 + 1) ^ 1 = 3` vertices, and the ball `{4, 0, 1}` around `0` attains the bound.
+example : #{v | (cycleGraph 5).edist 0 v ≤ (1 : ℕ)} = 3 := by
+  refine le_antisymm (card_edist_le_le (fun _ => cycleGraph_degree_three_le.le) 0 1) ?_
+  have hsub : ({0, 1, 4} : Finset (Fin 5)) ⊆
+      ({v | (cycleGraph 5).edist 0 v ≤ (1 : ℕ)} : Finset (Fin 5)) := by
+    intro v hv
+    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hv
+    rw [mem_filter]
+    refine ⟨mem_univ v, ?_⟩
+    rcases hv with rfl | rfl | rfl
+    · simp
+    · rw [edist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 (by decide)]
+      simp
+    · rw [edist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 (by decide)]
+      simp
+  exact le_trans (by decide : 3 ≤ #({0, 1, 4} : Finset (Fin 5))) (card_le_card hsub)
+
+/-! ### Central binomial coefficients -/
+
+-- At `m = 3`: `C(6, 3) = 20` and `20 ^ 2 * 7 = 2800 ≤ 16 ^ 3 = 4096`.
+example : Nat.centralBinom 3 = 20 ∧ Nat.centralBinom 3 ^ 2 * 7 ≤ 16 ^ 3 :=
+  ⟨by decide, centralBinom_sq_mul_le 3⟩
+
+-- At `n = 5`: `C(5, 2) = 10` and `10 ^ 2 * 6 = 600 ≤ 4 ^ 5 = 1024`.
+example : Nat.choose 5 2 = 10 ∧ Nat.choose 5 2 ^ 2 * 6 ≤ 4 ^ 5 :=
+  ⟨by decide, choose_half_sq_mul_le 5⟩
+
+-- For `m ≥ 12` the bound gives `5 * C(2m, m) ≤ 4 ^ m`, since then `2m + 1 ≥ 25`.
+example (m : ℕ) (hm : 12 ≤ m) : 5 * m.centralBinom ≤ 4 ^ m := by
+  refine (Nat.pow_le_pow_iff_left (n := 2) (by norm_num)).1 ?_
+  calc (5 * m.centralBinom) ^ 2 = m.centralBinom ^ 2 * 25 := by ring
+    _ ≤ m.centralBinom ^ 2 * (2 * m + 1) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
+    _ ≤ 16 ^ m := centralBinom_sq_mul_le m
+    _ = (4 ^ m) ^ 2 := by rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm, pow_mul]; norm_num
+
+-- With `n = 99` and `t = 0` the hypothesis `100 (t + 1) ^ 2 ≤ n + 1` holds with equality: at most
+-- `6 / 10` of the subsets of `Fin 99` have at most `49` elements.
+example : 10 * (univ.filter fun S : Finset (Fin 99) => S.card ≤ 49).card ≤ 6 * 2 ^ 99 := by
+  simpa using ten_mul_card_filter_card_le_le 99 0 (by norm_num)
+
+/-! ### Hypergeometric and binomial tails -/
+
+-- The first moment: over the six `2`-subsets `J` of `{0, 1, 2, 3}`, the sizes of `{0, 1} ∩ J`
+-- sum to `#U * C(#s - 1, ℓ - 1) = 2 * 3 = 6`, as a direct count confirms.
+example : ∑ J ∈ (range 4).powersetCard 2, #(range 2 ∩ J) =
+      #(range 2) * (#(range 4) - 1).choose (2 - 1) ∧
+    ∑ J ∈ (range 4).powersetCard 2, #(range 2 ∩ J) = 6 :=
+  ⟨sum_card_inter_powersetCard (range_subset_range.2 (by norm_num)) (by norm_num), by decide⟩
+
+-- Sixteen points, `U` the first twelve and `12`-subsets: `μ = 12 * 12 / 16 = 9 ≥ 8`, so at most
+-- half of the `12`-subsets meet `U` in fewer than `4 ≤ μ / 2` points.
+example : 2 * #{J ∈ (range 16).powersetCard 12 | #(range 12 ∩ J) < 4} ≤ Nat.choose 16 12 := by
+  simpa using two_mul_card_filter_card_inter_lt_le (s := range 16) (U := range 12) (ℓ := 12)
+    (range_subset_range.2 (by norm_num)) (by simp) (by simp) (m := 4) (by simp)
+
+-- The weighted count with `K = {0, 1, 2} ⊆ S = {0, 1, 2, 3}` and `j = 0`: the two subsets of `S`
+-- missing `K`, `∅` and `{3}`, satisfy `2 ^ 3 * 2 ≤ 3 ^ 3 * 2 ^ 1`.
+example : #{x ∈ (range 4).powerset | #(range 3 ∩ x) ≤ 0} = 2 ∧
+    2 ^ 3 * #{x ∈ (range 4).powerset | #(range 3 ∩ x) ≤ 0} ≤ 3 ^ 3 * 2 ^ 1 :=
+  ⟨by decide, by
+    simpa only [card_range] using
+      two_pow_mul_card_filter_card_inter_le (range_subset_range.2 (by norm_num : 3 ≤ 4)) 0⟩
+
+-- Majority votes: two of the three outcomes in `Fin 3` are good. Five of the nine pairs have at
+-- most one good entry, and the bound gives `9 * 5 ≤ 8 * 3 ^ 2`.
+example : (univ.filter fun ω : Fin (2 * 1) → Fin 3 =>
+      (univ.filter fun i => ω i ∈ ({0, 1} : Finset (Fin 3))).card ≤ 1).card = 5 ∧
+    9 ^ 1 * (univ.filter fun ω : Fin (2 * 1) → Fin 3 =>
+      (univ.filter fun i => ω i ∈ ({0, 1} : Finset (Fin 3))).card ≤ 1).card ≤
+      8 ^ 1 * Fintype.card (Fin 3) ^ (2 * 1) :=
+  ⟨by decide, card_filter_card_filter_le_le {0, 1} (by decide) 1⟩
+
+/-! ### Rotation maps and the expander mixing lemma -/
+
+/-- The 4-cycle as a rotation map: label `true` steps forward and arrives on label `false`. -/
+private def cycleFour : RotationMap (Fin 4) Bool where
+  rot p := if p.2 then (p.1 + 1, false) else (p.1 - 1, true)
+  rot_involutive := by
+    unfold Function.Involutive
+    decide
+
+private theorem isSimple_cycleFour : cycleFour.IsSimple :=
+  ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
+
+-- The simple graph of the 4-cycle is `2`-regular, and one walk step averages over the two
+-- neighbors.
+example : cycleFour.toSimpleGraph.IsRegularOfDegree 2 :=
+  isSimple_cycleFour.isRegularOfDegree
+
+example (f : Fin 4 → ℝ) : cycleFour.walk f 0 = (f 1 + f 3) / 2 := by
+  rw [isSimple_cycleFour.walk_apply_eq_sum_neighborFinset,
+    show cycleFour.toSimpleGraph.neighborFinset 0 = {1, 3} by decide, sum_pair (by decide)]
+  simp
+
+-- The complete graph with loops on four vertices has `λ = 0`, so the mixing lemma counts edges
+-- exactly: `e(S, T) = 4 * |S| * |T| / 4`, which is `2` for `S = {0, 1}` and `T = {2}`.
+example : #((RotationMap.complete (Fin 4)).interedges {0, 1} {2}) = 2 := by
+  have h := (RotationMap.complete (Fin 4)).abs_card_interedges_sub_le {0, 1} {2}
+  rw [RotationMap.spectralExpansion_complete, zero_mul, zero_mul, zero_div,
+    abs_nonpos_iff, sub_eq_zero] at h
+  have h' : (#((RotationMap.complete (Fin 4)).interedges {0, 1} {2}) : ℝ) = 2 := by
+    rw [h]
+    simp
+  exact_mod_cast h'
+
+example : #((RotationMap.complete (Fin 4)).interedges {0, 1} {2}) = 2 := by
+  decide
+
+-- The affine plane over `ZMod 3` (nine vertices, degree three) has `λ ≤ √(1 / 3) < 1`, so every
+-- nonempty set of at most four vertices has an edge leaving it.
+example (S : Finset (ZMod 3 × ZMod 3)) (hS : S.Nonempty) (hS4 : 2 * #S ≤ 9) :
+    0 < #((RotationMap.affinePlane (ZMod 3)).interedges S Sᶜ) := by
+  have hcard : Fintype.card (ZMod 3 × ZMod 3) = 9 := by simp [ZMod.card]
+  have h := (RotationMap.affinePlane (ZMod 3)).le_card_interedges_compl_of_two_mul_card_le
+    (S := S) (hcard ▸ hS4)
+  have hlam : (RotationMap.affinePlane (ZMod 3)).spectralExpansion < 1 := by
+    refine (RotationMap.spectralExpansion_affinePlane_le (K := ZMod 3)).trans_lt ?_
+    rw [Real.sqrt_lt' one_pos]
+    simp [ZMod.card]

body:
`renamed_token` is accepted without checking what the replacement resolves to. Reproduced inside `namespace A; open Turing.MultiTapeTM`, with an existing `A.ComputableInPolyTime`: a reference to imported `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` becomes bare `ComputableInPolyTime`, binding to A's declaration rather than `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`. The scope-aware `written_name` chooses the correct qualified target in this same case. A successful build need not detect this change of mathematical meaning.

Validate each shortened replacement against the intended full target, including shadowing/private aliases/local binders, or emit an unambiguous rooted name. Also reject a span that does not spell the referenced original: the current fallback replaces even `completelyUnrelated` at a stale interval, and rewrite accepts `--no-build-check`. Add shadowing and stale-span regressions.

@@ -0,0 +1,1882 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Plan and apply S2 of #456: remove tidy computability from public statements.
+
+Usage: python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py report [--area AREA]... [--json OUT] [--markdown OUT]
+       python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py rewrite --area AREA [--diff OUT | --verify [--rounds N]]
+       python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py stub-registry [--output FILE]
+Common options: [--registry FILE] [--allowlist FILE] [--build-dir DIR] [--no-build-check]
+
+Tidy computability is a proof device: outside the raw machine constructions of the allowlist
+(`scripts/tidy_allowlist.txt`, from #608), no public statement should mention it. Every public
+declaration outside the allowlist whose statement (its type, or the exposed body of a definition)
+mentions a tidy predicate falls in one case of the S2 design
+(https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/456#issuecomment-6376748411):
+
+1. a theorem with a registered plain twin (`--registry`): proofs that become plain use the twin;
+2. any other theorem: it is renamed `computableTidily…` → `computable…` (the target name must be
+   free) and restated with the plain predicates;
+3. a definition, instance or structure field: it is listed for a hand-written plain redefinition.
+
+A declaration that fits none of these is *unclassifiable*: it mentions a tidy notion without a
+same-bound plain equivalence, is a plain/tidy bridge or a deprecated alias, or its target name is
+taken (a collision). `report` prints the classification with per-area counts (#587's areas) and
+each area's rewrite plan, without writing anything.
+
+`rewrite --area AREA` restates the area's case 2 declarations and rewrites every reference to them
+in the three libraries, at the exact ranges recorded in the `.ilean` files (full names, names
+relative to namespaces and `open`s, dot notation), and in comments and READMEs. A declaration is
+*deferred* (left tidy) when its statement names another tidy declaration, gets a tidy hypothesis
+from a `variable` command, or is written inside a tidy namespace. A restated proof is *translated*
+when every tidy declaration it names has a plain counterpart (a twin or a restated lemma): those
+names are replaced in place. Otherwise it is *wrapped*: the old proof runs on tidy hypotheses
+(`have h := h.tidy`) and its conclusion is converted (`refine .of_tidy ?_`); statements that are
+not a bare predicate are transported with `simpa only [<plain ↔ tidy>]`. A reference from a proof
+that stays tidy keeps its old type: the application becomes `(lemma args).tidy`, with `.of_tidy`
+around tidy arguments, and references to case 1 originals stay. `.of_tidy (x.tidy)` round trips
+are then removed. Whatever cannot be done mechanically is listed as manual work.
+
+With `--verify`, the three libraries are built after the rewrite, repeatedly: a translated proof
+that fails is wrapped instead, and a wrapped proof or a client declaration that fails (typically
+a tidy `fun_prop` that used a restated `@[fun_prop]` lemma) is preceded by
+`attribute [local fun_prop] ComputableInPolyTime.tidy in`. Remaining failures are reported. With
+`--stub-failures` (measurement only, never commit the result), proofs that still fail become
+`sorry`, so that later rounds reach the modules downstream of them. `--diff` writes the plan as a
+patch instead of rewriting files.
+
+The registry is a JSON array of `{"original": name, "plain": name, "module": module}` objects, the
+format of #608's `#mirror_pairs`. Until S1 lands, `scripts/tidy_mirror_registry.json` is a stub,
+written by `stub-registry`: the existing declarations whose name is the plain rename of a tidy
+theorem and whose statement is its plain transport.
+
+Declarations, statements and references come from `scripts/quality_report.py` and
+`scripts/QualityReport.lean`, which read the build outputs of
+`lake build Complexity ComplexityTests ComplexityAbstracts`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from collections import Counter, defaultdict
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
+import quality_report as qr  # noqa: E402
+from proof_lengths import masks  # noqa: E402
+
+ALLOWLIST = ROOT / "scripts/tidy_allowlist.txt"
+REGISTRY = ROOT / "scripts/tidy_mirror_registry.json"
+TM = "Turing.MultiTapeTM."
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Notion:
+    """A tidy predicate with a same-bound plain counterpart and their equivalence."""
+    tidy: str
+    plain: str
+    iff: str  # `plain ↔ tidy`
+
+    @property
+    def to_tidy(self) -> str:
+        return self.plain + ".tidy"
+
+    @property
+    def of_tidy(self) -> str:
+        return self.plain + ".of_tidy"
+
+    @property
+    def dot_of_tidy(self) -> str:
+        """`Tidy.computable…`: `of_tidy` for dot notation on a tidy hypothesis."""
+        last = self.plain.rsplit(".", 1)[1]
+        return self.tidy + "." + last[0].lower() + last[1:]
+
+    @property
+    def bridges(self) -> set[str]:
+        return {self.to_tidy, self.of_tidy, self.iff, self.dot_of_tidy}
+
+
+NOTIONS = (
+    Notion(TM + "ComputableTidilyInPolyTime", TM + "ComputableInPolyTime",
+           TM + "computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime"),
+    Notion(TM + "ComputableTidilyInPolySpace", TM + "ComputableInPolySpace",
+           TM + "computableInPolySpace_iff_computableTidilyInPolySpace"),
+    Notion(TM + "ComputableTidilyInSpace", TM + "ComputableInSpace",
+           TM + "computableInSpace_iff_computableTidilyInSpace"),
+    Notion(TM + "ComputableTidilyInO", TM + "ComputableInO",
+           TM + "computableInO_iff_computableTidilyInO"),
+    Notion("Cslib.Complexity.ComputableTidilyInFPTTime", "Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInFPTTime",
+           "Cslib.Complexity.computableInFPTTime_iff_computableTidilyInFPTTime"),
+)
+BY_TIDY = {n.tidy: n for n in NOTIONS}
+BRIDGES = set().union(*(n.bridges for n in NOTIONS))
+# `computableTidilyInPolyTime_foo` → `computableInPolyTime_foo`, for the supported notions only.
+RENAME = re.compile(r"([cC])omputableTidily(In(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|FPTTime))"
+                    r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])")
+# Name components that still say "tidy" after renaming mark a plain/tidy helper.
+TIDY_WORD = re.compile(r"(?i)tid(?:y|ily)")
+
+
+def plain_name(name: str) -> str:
+    return RENAME.sub(r"\1omputable\2", name)
+
+
+def is_tidy_constant(name: str) -> bool:
+    """Mirror of `isTidy` in `scripts/QualityReport.lean`."""
+    last = name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
+    return last.startswith(("ComputableTidily", "ComputesTidily", "IsTidy"))
+
+
+def load_allowlist(path: Path) -> set[str]:
+    """Library source paths (relative to the repository root), one per line; `#` comments."""
+    return {line.split("#", 1)[0].strip() for line in path.read_text().splitlines()} - {""}
+
+
+def load_registry(path: Path | None) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """original → plain twin, from a JSON array of `{"original", "plain", "module"}` objects (the
+    output of #608's `#mirror_pairs`), or an object holding it under `"pairs"`."""
+    if path is None or not path.exists():
+        return {}
+    data = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    if isinstance(data, dict):
+        data = data.get("pairs", [])
+    registry = {}
+    for row in data:
+        if not (isinstance(row, dict) and isinstance(row.get("original"), str)
+                and isinstance(row.get("plain"), str)):
+            raise ValueError(f"{path}: malformed registry entry {row!r}")
+        registry[row["original"]] = row["plain"]
+    return registry
+
+
+# --- Classification -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Entry:
+    name: str
+    module: str
+    path: str  # relative to `Complexity/`
+    area: str
+    kind: str  # theorem, definition, structure field, constructor, instance
+    case: str  # "1", "2", "3" or "unclassifiable"
+    reason: str = ""
+    target: str = ""  # the twin (case 1) or the new name (case 2)
+    notions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    unsupported: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    body_only: bool = False  # mentions tidy only in its exposed body
+    implicit: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    users: int = 0  # other modules that name it
+    detail: str = ""
+    collision: dict | None = None
+    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+def decl_kind(decl: dict) -> str:
+    if decl["role"] == "member":
+        return "constructor" if decl["kind"] == "ctor" else "structure field"
+    if decl["keyword"] == "instance" or "instance" in decl["attrs"]:
+        return "instance"
+    if decl["kind"] == "thm":
+        return "theorem"
+    return "definition"
+
+
+def classify_decl(decl: dict, const: dict, registry: dict[str, str], constants: dict[str, dict],
+                  private_names: dict[str, set[str]]) -> Entry:
+    """The S2 case of one public declaration whose statement mentions a tidy constant."""
+    name = decl["name"]
+    tidy = sorted(set(const.get("tidy", [])) | set(const.get("tb", [])))
+    entry = Entry(name=name, module=decl["module"], path=decl["path"], area=decl["area"],
+                  kind=decl_kind(decl), case="unclassifiable",
+                  notions=[t for t in tidy if t in BY_TIDY],
+                  unsupported=[t for t in tidy if t not in BY_TIDY],
+                  body_only=not const.get("tidy"), implicit=list(decl.get("implicit", [])),
+                  users=len(decl.get("lib_refs", ())) + len(decl.get("test_refs", ()))
+                  + len(decl.get("abstract_refs", ())))
+    last = name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
+    if "deprecated" in decl["attrs"]:
+        entry.reason, entry.detail = "deprecated alias", "#588: delete, no aliases"
+    elif is_tidy_constant(name) and entry.kind != "theorem":
+        entry.reason = "tidy notion definition"
+    elif name in BRIDGES or (entry.kind == "theorem" and TIDY_WORD.search(plain_name(last))):
+        entry.reason, entry.detail = "bridge", "kept for proofs; S3 stores it internally"
+    elif entry.unsupported:
+        entry.reason = "unsupported notion"
+        entry.detail = "no same-bound plain equivalence: " + ", ".join(
+            f"`{t}`" for t in entry.unsupported)
+    elif entry.kind != "theorem":
+        entry.case = "3"
+    elif name in registry:
+        twin = registry[name]
+        entry.target = twin
+        if twin not in constants:
+            entry.reason, entry.detail = "registered twin missing", f"`{twin}` is not built"
+        else:
+            entry.case = "1"
+            if constants[twin].get("ph") != const.get("ph"):
+                entry.warnings.append("the twin's statement is not the syntactic plain "
+                                      "transport (checked only up to definitional equality "
+                                      "by S1)")
+    else:
+        target = plain_name(name)
+        entry.target = target
+        taken = target in constants or target in private_names.get(decl["module"], set())
+        if target != name and taken:
+            existing = constants.get(target)
+            same = existing is not None and existing.get("ph") == const.get("ph")
+            entry.collision = {
+                "target": target, "module": existing["m"] if existing else decl["module"],
+                "equivalent": same, "private": existing is None or not existing["e"]}
+            entry.reason = "collision"
+            entry.detail = ("the target has the plain statement but is not a registered twin"
+                            if same else "the target exists with another statement")
+        else:
+            entry.case = "2"
+    return entry
+
+
+def private_by_module(constants: dict[str, dict]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
+    """The user-facing names of private constants, by module."""
+    out: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
+    for name, const in constants.items():
+        if name.startswith("_private."):
+            rest = name.removeprefix("_private.").split(".0.", 1)
+            if len(rest) == 2:
+                out[const["m"]].add(rest[1])
+    return out
+
+
+def classify_all(model: "Model", registry: dict[str, str]) -> list[Entry]:
+    entries = []
+    privates = private_by_module(model.constants)
+    for name, decl in sorted(model.decls.items()):
+        const = model.constants.get(name, {})
+        if decl["role"] == "generated" or not (const.get("tidy") or const.get("tb")):
+            continue
+        if "Complexity/" + decl["path"] in model.allowlist:
+            continue
+        entries.append(classify_decl(decl, const, registry, model.constants, privates))
+    targets = Counter(e.target for e in entries if e.case == "2" and e.target != e.name)
+    for e in entries:
+        if e.case == "2" and e.target != e.name and targets[e.target] > 1:
+            e.case, e.reason = "unclassifiable", "collision"
+            e.detail = "another declaration renames to the same target"
+            e.collision = {"target": e.target, "module": e.module, "equivalent": False,
+                           "private": False}
+    return entries
+
+
+def registry_problems(registry: dict[str, str], constants: dict[str, dict]) -> list[str]:
+    out = []
+    for original, twin in sorted(registry.items()):
+        if original not in constants:
+            out.append(f"`{original}` is registered but not in the build")
+        elif twin not in constants:
+            out.append(f"twin `{twin}` of `{original}` is not in the build")
+    return out
+

+# --- Loading ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+class Model:
+    """Declarations, constants and references of the built libraries."""
+
+    def __init__(self, build_dir: Path, allowlist: set[str]):
+        pairs = ",".join(f"{n.tidy}={n.plain}" for n in NOTIONS)
+        self.lib = qr.Library(build_dir, pairs)
+        self.constants = self.lib.constants
+        self.decls, self.owners, _ = qr.collect_declarations(self.lib)
+        qr.annotate_headers(self.lib, self.decls)
+        qr.collect_references(self.lib, self.decls, self.owners)
+        qr.classify(self.decls)
+        self.allowlist = allowlist
+        self._users: dict[str, list[tuple[str, list]]] | None = None
+        self._known: set[str] | None = None
+
+    def users(self, name: str) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:
+        """`(module, usage)` for every reference to `name` in the three libraries."""
+        if self._users is None:
+            self._users = defaultdict(list)
+            for module in self.lib.ileans:
+                for ref, _, info in self.lib.references(module):
+                    for usage in info["usages"]:
+                        self._users[ref].append((module, usage))
+        return self._users.get(name, [])
+
+    @property
+    def known(self) -> set[str]:
+        """Every constant name the build defines or references, for name resolution."""
+        if self._known is None:
+            self._known = set(self.constants)
+            for module in self.lib.ileans:
+                self._known.update(ref for ref, _, _ in self.lib.references(module))
+        return self._known
+

+AREA_ORDER = [name for name, _, _ in qr.AREAS] + [qr.OTHER_AREA]

+
+def summary(entries: list[Entry]) -> dict:
+    by_area: dict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
+    reasons: Counter = Counter()
+    for e in entries:
+        by_area[e.area]["total"] += 1
+        by_area[e.area][e.case] += 1
+        if e.case == "unclassifiable":
+            reasons[e.reason] += 1
+    total = Counter()
+    for counts in by_area.values():
+        total.update(counts)
+    return {"areas": {a: dict(by_area[a]) for a in AREA_ORDER if a in by_area},
+            "total": dict(total), "unclassifiable_reasons": dict(reasons.most_common())}

+def markdown_report(report: dict, limit: int = 40) -> str:
+    s = report["summary"]
+    dirty = " with uncommitted changes" if report["dirty"] else ""
+    out = [f"Revision `{report['revision']}`{dirty}; build outputs {report['outputs']}. "
+           f"Allowlist: {report['allowlist_size']} modules. "
+           f"Registry: {report['registry_size']} pairs (`{report['registry']}`).", "",
+           "### Public declarations whose statement mentions a tidy predicate", "",
+           "| Area | Total | (1) Registered twin | (2) Rename and restate | "
+           "(3) Definition or field | Unclassifiable |", "|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|"]
+    for area, c in list(s["areas"].items()) + [("Total", s["total"])]:
+        out.append(f"| {area} | {c.get('total', 0):,} | {c.get('1', 0):,} | {c.get('2', 0):,} | "
+                   f"{c.get('3', 0):,} | {c.get('unclassifiable', 0):,} |")
+    out += ["", "Unclassifiable, by reason: " + "; ".join(
+        f"{r} ({n})" for r, n in s["unclassifiable_reasons"].items()) + "."]
+    collisions = [e for e in report["entries"] if e["collision"]]
+    if collisions:
+        out += ["", "### Collisions", "",
+                "| Declaration | Target | Target module | Same plain statement |",
+                "|---|---|---|---|"]
+        for e in collisions[:limit]:
+            c = e["collision"]
+            out.append(f"| `{e['name']}` | `{c['target']}` | `{c['module']}` | "
+                       f"{'yes' if c['equivalent'] else 'no'} |")
+        if len(collisions) > limit:
+            out.append(f"| … {len(collisions) - limit} more in the JSON report | | | |")
+    unsupported = Counter(t for e in report["entries"] for t in e["unsupported"])
+    if unsupported:
+        out += ["", "Tidy notions without a same-bound plain equivalence, by declarations "
+                "mentioning them: " + ", ".join(f"`{t}` ({n})" for t, n in
+                                                unsupported.most_common()) + "."]
+    third = [e for e in report["entries"] if e["case"] == "3"]
+    if third:
+        out += ["", "### Case 3: definitions and structure fields", ""]
+        out += [f"* `{e['name']}` ({e['kind']}, {e['area']})" for e in third[:limit]]
+        if len(third) > limit:
+            out.append(f"* … {len(third) - limit} more in the JSON report")
+    if report["registry_problems"]:
+        out += ["", "Registry problems: " + "; ".join(report["registry_problems"][:limit])]
+    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

+# --- Lean source helpers (unit-tested in scripts/test_tidy_sweep.py) ----------------------------
+
+OPENERS, CLOSERS = "([{⦃⟨‹", ")]}⦄⟩›"
+IDENT = re.compile(qr.IDENT.pattern)
+KEYWORDS = {"by", "fun", "λ", "with", "at", "using", "from", "then", "else", "do", "in", "if",
+            "match", "show", "have", "let", "calc", "only", "generalizing", "says", "where",
+            "deriving", "termination_by", "decreasing_by", "obtain", "rcases", "refine", "exact"}
+COMMAND_KEYWORD = re.compile(r"#?[A-Za-z_]+")
+NAME_ONLY_COMMANDS = {"#print", "#check", "#guard_msgs", "attribute", "open", "export", "#eval",
+                      "#reduce", "#synth", "add_decl_doc", "#lint", "#help"}
+LEMMA_LIST_TACTIC = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:simp|simp_all|dsimp|simp_rw|rw|rwa|rewrite|erw|nth_rewrite|nth_rw|simpa|fun_prop|"
+    r"aesop|norm_num|field_simp|grind|polytime|positivity|unfold|delta|gcongr|subst_vars|"
+    r"continuity|measurability|bound|decide|omega|linarith|nlinarith|exact\?|apply\?|"
+    r"rw_mod_cast|push_cast|norm_cast|simp_arith|conv)\b[^\[\]\n]*$")
+
+
+def match_bracket(mask: str, i: int, limit: int | None = None) -> int:
+    """The index of the bracket closing the one at `mask[i]`, or -1."""
+    depth, end = 0, len(mask) if limit is None else limit
+    for j in range(i, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+            if depth == 0:
+                return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def find_top_level(mask: str, start: int, end: int, token: str) -> int:
+    """The first `token` at bracket depth 0 in `mask[start:end]`, or -1. `:` excludes `:=`."""
+    depth = 0
+    for j in range(start, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+        elif depth == 0 and mask.startswith(token, j):
+            if token == ":" and (mask.startswith(":=", j) or mask.startswith("::", j)
+                                 or (j and mask[j - 1] == ":")):
+                continue
+            return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def line_indent(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    start = text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+    return len(text[start:]) - len(text[start:].lstrip(" "))
+
+
+def column(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    return offset - (text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1)
+
+
+def atom_end(mask: str, i: int, limit: int) -> int:
+    """The end of the atom (identifier, number, `?_`, bracket group, `.ident`) at `i` together
+    with directly attached projections (`.field`, `.1`), or `i` when no atom starts there."""
+    if i >= limit:
+        return i
+    char = mask[i]
+    if char in OPENERS:
+        end = match_bracket(mask, i, limit)
+        if end < 0:
+            return i
+        j = end + 1
+    elif char == "." and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char == "?" and mask.startswith("?_", i):
+        j = i + 2
+    elif char == "@" and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char.isdigit():
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and (mask[j].isalnum() or mask[j] == "."):
+            j += 1
+    else:
+        match = IDENT.match(mask, i)
+        if not match or match[0].rstrip(".") in KEYWORDS:
+            return i
+        j = match.end()
+    while j < limit and mask[j] == "." and j + 1 < limit and (
+            mask[j + 1].isdigit() or IDENT.match(mask, j + 1)):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, j + 1).end() if IDENT.match(mask, j + 1) else j + 2
+    return min(j, limit)
+
+
+NAMED_ARG = re.compile(r"\(\s*[^\W\d][\w'₀-₉]*\s*:=")
+
+
+def parse_args(mask: str, pos: int, limit: int, count: int, base_indent: int,
+               named: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    """Up to `count` positional application arguments after `pos`: atoms separated by blanks,
+    continuing onto lines indented more than `base_indent`. Named arguments `(x := e)` are
+    skipped and, when `named` is given, appended to it."""
+    args = []
+    i = pos
+    while len(args) < count and i < limit:
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and mask[j] in " \t":
+            j += 1
+        if j < limit and mask[j] == "\n":
+            k = j
+            while k < limit and mask[k] in " \t\n":
+                k += 1
+            if k >= limit or line_indent(mask, k) <= base_indent:
+                break
+            j = k
+        if j == i and args:
+            break  # no blank after the previous argument
+        end = atom_end(mask, j, limit)
+        if end == j:
+            break
+        if NAMED_ARG.match(mask, j):
+            if named is not None:
+                named.append((j, end))
+        else:
+            args.append((j, end))
+        i = end
+    return args
+
+
+def strip_space(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    while start < end and mask[start].isspace():
+        start += 1
+    while end > start and mask[end - 1].isspace():
+        end -= 1
+    return start, end
+
+
+def is_atomic_application(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    """For text `P args` in `mask[start:end]` made of atoms only, the span of `P`; else None."""
+    start, end = strip_space(mask, start, end)
+    head = atom_end(mask, start, end)
+    if head == start:
+        return None
+    args = parse_args(mask, head, end, 10 ** 6, -1)
+    last = args[-1][1] if args else head
+    return (start, head) if strip_space(mask, last, end)[0] == end else None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Binder:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    bracket: str
+    names: list[str]
+    type_start: int
+    type_end: int
+    default: bool
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DeclText:
+    start: int
+    sel_start: int
+    sel_end: int
+    end: int
+    binders: list[Binder]
+    colon: int  # the `:` before the type, or -1
+    assign: int  # the `:=` before the body, or -1
+    problems: list[str]
+
+
+def parse_decl(mask: str, start: int, sel_start: int, sel_end: int, end: int) -> DeclText:
+    """Binders, type and body of the declaration whose name ends at `sel_end`."""
+    assign = find_top_level(mask, sel_end, end, ":=")
+    stop = assign if assign >= 0 else end
+    binders, problems, colon = [], [], -1
+    i = sel_end
+    if mask.startswith(".{", i):
+        i = match_bracket(mask, i + 1, stop) + 1
+    while i < stop:
+        char = mask[i]
+        if char.isspace():
+            i += 1
+        elif char in "([{⦃":
+            close = match_bracket(mask, i, stop)
+            if close < 0:
+                problems.append("unbalanced binder")
+                break
+            inner = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":")
+            default = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":=")
+            if inner < 0:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:close].split(), close
+            else:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:inner].split(), inner + 1
+            type_end = default if default >= 0 else close
+            binders.append(Binder(i, close + 1, char, names, type_start, type_end,
+                                  default >= 0))
+            i = close + 1
+        elif char == ":":
+            colon = i
+            break
+        else:
+            problems.append("binder without brackets")
+            break
+    if assign < 0:
+        problems.append("no `:=` (pattern-matching definition)")
+    return DeclText(start, sel_start, sel_end, end, binders, colon, assign, problems)
+
+
+def proof_parts(text: str, assign: int, end: int) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    """The text after `:=` and whether it is a tactic block."""
+    body = text[assign + 2:end]
+    return body, re.match(r"\s*by(?:\s|$)", body) is not None
+
+
+def collapse(text: str) -> str:
+    return " ".join(text.split())
+
+
+# --- Scopes and names ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+SCOPE_COMMAND = re.compile(
+    r"^(?P<mods>(?:@\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:public|private|noncomputable|protected|meta)\s+)*)"
+    r"(?P<kw>namespace|section|end|open|mutual)\b(?P<rest>[^\n]*)", re.M)
+
+
+def namespaces_of(names) -> set[str]:
+    """Every name and every proper prefix of a name, as namespaces."""
+    out = set()
+    for name in names:
+        parts = name.split(".")
+        for i in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+            out.add(".".join(parts[:i]))
+    return out
+
+
+class Scopes:
+    """The current namespace and opened namespaces at each offset of a masked source."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mask: str, namespaces: set[str]):
+        self.points: list[tuple[int, str, tuple[str, ...]]] = [(0, "", ())]
+        self.once: list[tuple[int, int, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
+        stack: list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]] = []
+        starts = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(mask)] + [len(mask)]
+        for match in SCOPE_COMMAND.finditer(mask):
+            kw, rest = match["kw"], match["rest"].split()
+            namespace = ".".join(n for k, n, _ in stack if k == "namespace" and n)
+            opens = [o for _, _, os in stack for o in os]
+            if kw == "namespace" and rest:
+                stack.append(("namespace", rest[0], []))
+            elif kw in ("section", "mutual"):
+                stack.append((kw, rest[0] if rest and kw == "section" else "", []))
+            elif kw == "end":
+                if stack:
+                    stack.pop()
+            elif kw == "open":
+                one_shot = bool(rest) and rest[-1] == "in"
+                words = [w for w in (rest[:-1] if one_shot else rest)
+                         if w not in ("scoped", "hiding", "renaming", "→", "private")
+                         and not w.startswith("(") and IDENT.fullmatch(w)]
+                resolved = []
+                for word in words:
+                    prefixes = [".".join(namespace.split(".")[:i])
+                                for i in range(len(namespace.split(".")), -1, -1)] if namespace \
+                        else [""]
+                    found = [p + "." + word if p else word for p in prefixes + opens + resolved
+                             if (p + "." + word if p else word) in namespaces]
+                    resolved += found or [word]
+                if one_shot:
+                    after = next((s for s in starts if s > match.end()), len(mask))
+                    following = next((s for s in starts if s > after), len(mask))
+                    self.once.append((match.start(), following, tuple(resolved)))
+                    continue
+                if not stack:
+                    stack.append(("file", "", []))
+                stack[-1][2].extend(resolved)
+            namespace = ".".join(n for k, n, _ in stack if k == "namespace" and n)
+            opens = [o for _, _, os in stack for o in os]
+            self.points.append((match.end(), namespace, tuple(opens)))
+
+    def at(self, offset: int) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
+        namespace, opens = "", ()
+        for point, ns, os in self.points:
+            if point > offset:
+                break
+            namespace, opens = ns, os
+        extra = tuple(o for start, end, os in self.once if start <= offset < end for o in os)
+        return namespace, opens + extra
+
+    def prefixes(self, offset: int) -> list[str]:
+        """Namespaces a written name may be relative to, innermost first (`""` is the root)."""
+        namespace, opens = self.at(offset)
+        parts = namespace.split(".") if namespace else []
+        return [".".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1)] + list(opens)
+
+
+def written_name(target: str, prefixes: list[str], known: set[str]) -> str:
+    """The shortest suffix of `target` that resolves to it, and to nothing else, from a position
+    whose namespace prefixes and opened namespaces are `prefixes`."""
+    parts = target.split(".")
+    for k in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+        suffix = ".".join(parts[-k:])
+        hits = {p + "." + suffix if p else suffix for p in prefixes}
+        resolved = {h for h in hits if h in known or h == target}
+        if resolved == {target}:
+            return suffix
+    return target
+
+
+def renamed_token(token: str, old: str, new: str) -> str | None:
+    """`token` (a written form of `old`) with the renamed part, when the written prefix still
+    resolves the same way (`old = P.token` and `new = P.result`); otherwise None."""
+    at = "@" if token.startswith("@") else ""
+    bare = token[len(at):]
+    root = "_root_." if bare.startswith("_root_.") else ""
+    bare = bare[len(root):]
+    if not (old == bare or old.endswith("." + bare)):
+        return None
+    prefix = old[:len(old) - len(bare)]
+    if not new.startswith(prefix):
+        return None
+    result = new[len(prefix):]
+    if not result or (prefix and result.startswith(".")):
+        return None
+    return at + root + result
+
+
+# --- Edits --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Replace:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    text: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Wrap:
+    """Text inserted before `open` and after `close`; `site` orders wraps with equal spans (the
+    wrap of the site that starts first is outermost)."""
+    open: int
+    close: int
+    before: str
+    after: str
+    site: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Region:
+    """A span whose edited text is then transformed by `build`."""
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    build: object
+    decl: str
+
+
+def render(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap], lo: int, hi: int) -> str:
+    """`text[lo:hi]` with the replacements and wraps inside it applied. At one position, wraps
+    close (innermost first) before others open (outermost first), then a replacement starts."""
+    reps = sorted((r for r in replaces if lo <= r.start and r.end <= hi),
+                  key=lambda r: (r.start, r.end))
+    ws = [w for w in wraps if lo <= w.open and w.close <= hi]
+    points = sorted({r.start for r in reps} | {w.open for w in ws} | {w.close for w in ws})
+    starting = defaultdict(list)
+    for r in reps:
+        starting[r.start].append(r)
+    out, cur = [], lo
+    for p in points:
+        if p < cur:
+            continue  # inside a replaced span
+        out.append(text[cur:p])
+        out += [w.after for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.close == p),
+                                        key=lambda w: (-w.open, -w.site))]
+        out += [w.before for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.open == p),
+                                         key=lambda w: (-w.close, w.site))]
+        cur = p
+        for r in starting.get(p, []):
+            out.append(r.text)
+            cur = max(cur, r.end)
+    out.append(text[cur:hi])
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def apply_edits(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap],
+                regions: list[Region]) -> str:
+    out, cur = [], 0
+    for region in sorted(regions, key=lambda r: r.start):
+        out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, region.start))
+        out.append(region.build(render(text, replaces, wraps, region.start, region.end)))
+        cur = region.end
+    out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, len(text)))
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Round trips --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+OF_TIDY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.'])(?:(?:[\w.']*\.)?Computable(?:In(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|"
+                     r"FPTTime))\.|\.)of_tidy\b")
+DOT_ROUND_TRIP = re.compile(r"\.tidy\.computableIn(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|FPTTime)\b")
+
+
+def cancel_round_trips(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """Remove `of_tidy (x.tidy)`, `of_tidy <| x.tidy` and `x.tidy.computableIn…` round trips,
+    where `x` is an atom. Returns the new text and the number of removals."""
+    count = 0
+    while True:
+        mask = masks(text)[1]
+        change = None
+        for match in DOT_ROUND_TRIP.finditer(mask):
+            change = (match.start(), match.end(), "")
+            break
+        if change is None:
+            for match in OF_TIDY.finditer(mask):
+                i = match.end()
+                while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                    i += 1
+                pipe = mask.startswith("<|", i)
+                if pipe:
+                    i += 2
+                    while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                        i += 1
+                end = atom_end(mask, i, len(mask))
+                if end == i:
+                    continue
+                inner = (i, end)
+                if mask[i] == "(" and match_bracket(mask, i) == end - 1:
+                    inner = strip_space(mask, i + 1, end - 1)
+                start, stop = inner
+                if not mask[start:stop].endswith(".tidy") or atom_end(mask, start, stop) != stop:
+                    continue
+                core_end = stop - len(".tidy")
+                if atom_end(mask, start, core_end) != core_end:
+                    continue
+                if pipe:
+                    after = end
+                    while after < len(mask) and mask[after] in " \t":
+                        after += 1
+                    if after < len(mask) and mask[after] not in CLOSERS + "\n,":
+                        continue
+                change = (match.start(), end, text[start:core_end])
+                break
+        if change is None:
+            return text, count
+        start, end, new = change
+        new_mask = masks(new)[1]
+        if (start > 0 and text[start - 1] == "(" and end < len(text) and text[end] == ")"
+                and atom_end(new_mask, 0, len(new)) == len(new) and not new.startswith("@")):
+            start, end = start - 1, end + 1
+        text = text[:start] + new + text[end:]
+        count += 1
+
+
+# --- Wrapping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Hyp:
+    names: list[str]
+    old_type: str  # one line
+    simple: bool
+
+
+def reindent(lines: list[str], delta: int) -> list[str] | None:
+    """Shift lines by `delta` columns; None when that would remove non-blank text."""
+    out = []
+    for line in lines:
+        if not line.strip():
+            out.append("")
+        elif delta >= 0:
+            out.append(" " * delta + line)
+        elif len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" ")) >= -delta:
+            out.append(line[-delta:])
+        else:
+            return None
+    return out
+
+
+def wrap_proof(body: str, body_column: int, decl_indent: int, hyps: list[Hyp],
+               conclusion: str | None, simple_conclusion: bool, iffs: str) -> str | None:
+    """The new text after `:=` for a proof `body` of the old (tidy) statement, now stated plainly:
+    tidy hypotheses are recovered, and the old conclusion converted. `body_column` is the column
+    of the first character of `body`. None when the layout cannot be preserved."""
+    stripped = body.lstrip()
+    lead = body[:len(body) - len(stripped)]
+    first_col = body_column + len(lead) if "\n" not in lead else len(lead.rsplit("\n", 1)[1])
+    stripped = stripped.rstrip()
+    tactic = re.match(r"by(?=\s|$)", stripped) is not None
+    if not hyps and simple_conclusion and not tactic:
+        return f"{lead}.of_tidy ({stripped})"
+    k = decl_indent + 2
+    rebind = []
+    for hyp in hyps:
+        for name in hyp.names:
+            rebind.append(f"have {name} := {name}.tidy" if hyp.simple else
+                          f"have {name} : {hyp.old_type} := by simpa only [{iffs}] using {name}")
+    if tactic:
+        rest = stripped[2:]
+        if rest.lstrip(" \t").startswith("\n") or not rest.strip():
+            lines = rest.lstrip(" \t")[1:].split("\n")
+            nonblank = [ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()]
+            if not nonblank:
+                return None
+            k = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        else:
+            first_line, _, tail = rest.lstrip(" \t").partition("\n")
+            tactic_col = first_col + 2 + (len(rest) - len(rest.lstrip(" \t")))
+            shifted = reindent(tail.split("\n"), k - tactic_col) if tail else []
+            if shifted is None:
+                return None
+            lines = [" " * k + first_line] + shifted
+        pad = " " * k
+        out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+        if conclusion is None:
+            out += lines
+        elif simple_conclusion:
+            out += [pad + "refine .of_tidy ?_"] + lines
+        else:
+            inner = reindent(lines, 2)
+            out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} := by"] + inner + \
+                [pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+        return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+    first, _, tail = stripped.partition("\n")
+    tail_lines = tail.split("\n") if tail else []
+    nonblank = [ln for ln in tail_lines if ln.strip()]
+    shift = 0
+    if nonblank:
+        least = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        shift = max(0, k + 2 - least)
+    tail_lines = reindent(tail_lines, shift) or tail_lines
+    pad = " " * k
+    out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+    term = "\n".join([first] + tail_lines)
+    if conclusion is None:
+        out.append(pad + "exact " + term)
+    elif simple_conclusion:
+        out.append(pad + "exact .of_tidy (" + term + ")")
+    else:
+        out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} :=", pad + "  " + term,
+                pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+    return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Planning -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Manual:
+    path: str
+    line: int
+    decl: str
+    kind: str
+    detail: str = ""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Ref:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    decl: str | None
+
+
+class SourceFile:
+    def __init__(self, path: Path, namespaces: set[str]):
+        self.path = path
+        self.text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.code, self.mask = masks(self.text) if path.suffix == ".lean" else (self.text,) * 2
+        self.lines = self.text.split("\n")
+        self.starts = [0]
+        for line in self.lines:
+            self.starts.append(self.starts[-1] + len(line) + 1)
+        self.commands = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(self.mask)]
+        self._namespaces = namespaces
+        self._scopes: Scopes | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def scopes(self) -> Scopes:
+        if self._scopes is None:
+            self._scopes = Scopes(self.mask, self._namespaces)
+        return self._scopes
+
+    def at(self, line: int, column16: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 0-based line and UTF-16 column (`.ilean` positions)."""
+        return self.starts[line] + qr.utf16_index(self.lines[line], column16)
+
+    def at_range(self, line: int, column: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 1-based line and code-point column (declaration ranges)."""
+        return self.starts[line - 1] + column
+
+    def line_of(self, offset: int) -> int:
+        """The 1-based line of an offset."""
+        return self.text.count("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+
+    def command_keyword(self, offset: int) -> str:
+        starts = [s for s in self.commands if s <= offset]
+        if not starts:
+            return ""
+        match = COMMAND_KEYWORD.match(self.mask, starts[-1])
+        return match[0] if match else ""
+
+    def comment_spans(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+        if self.path.suffix != ".lean":
+            return [(0, len(self.text))]
+        spans, i = [], 0
+        while i < len(self.text):
+            if self.code[i] != self.text[i]:
+                j = i
+                while j < len(self.text) and self.code[j] != self.text[j] or (
+                        j < len(self.text) and self.text[j] == "\n" and j + 1 < len(self.text)
+                        and self.code[j + 1] != self.text[j + 1]):
+                    j += 1
+                spans.append((i, j))
+                i = j
+            else:
+                i += 1
+        return spans
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileEdits:
+    replaces: list[Replace] = field(default_factory=list)
+    wraps: list[Wrap] = field(default_factory=list)
+    regions: list[Region] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class Planner:
+    """The edits of one area's batch: case 2 declarations restated and renamed, their clients
+    converted, and case 1 twins used in translated proofs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model: Model, entries: list[Entry], registry: dict[str, str], area: str,
+                 force_wrap: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+                 force_bridge: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset(),
+                 stub: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset()):
+        self.model, self.area, self.force_wrap = model, area, force_wrap
+        self.force_bridge, self.stub = force_bridge, stub
+        self.entries = {e.name: e for e in entries}
+        self.batch = {e.name: e for e in entries if e.area == area and e.case == "2"}
+        self.renames = {name: e.target for name, e in self.batch.items()}
+        self.twins = {o: p for o, p in registry.items() if p in model.constants}
+        self.files: dict[Path, FileEdits] = defaultdict(FileEdits)
+        self.sources: dict[Path, SourceFile] = {}
+        self.manual: list[Manual] = []
+        self.decls: dict[str, dict] = {}
+        self.spans: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.needs: dict[str, dict[str, bool]] = defaultdict(dict)
+        self.sites = Counter()
+        self.imports: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
+        self.known = model.known | set(self.renames.values())
+        self.namespaces = namespaces_of(self.known)
+        self.round_trips = 0
+        self.deferred: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        self.bridged: list[str] = []
+        self.stubbed: list[str] = []
+
+    # Sources and references.
+
+    def source(self, path: Path) -> SourceFile:
+        if path not in self.sources:
+            self.sources[path] = SourceFile(path, self.namespaces)
+        return self.sources[path]
+
+    def refs(self, module: str) -> list[Ref]:
+        src = self.source(qr.source_path(module))
+        out = []
+        for name, _, info in self.model.lib.references(module):
+            for u in info["usages"]:
+                out.append(Ref(name, src.at(u[0], u[1]), src.at(u[2], u[3]),
+                               u[4] if len(u) == 5 else None))
+        return out
+
+    def ref_kind(self, name: str) -> str:
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return "pred"
+        if owner in self.renames:
+            return "renamed"
+        if name in self.twins:
+            return "twin"
+        if name in BRIDGES:
+            return "bridge"
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        if const.get("tidy") or const.get("tb") or is_tidy_constant(name):
+            return "tidy"
+        return "plain"
+
+    def new_name(self, name: str) -> str:
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return BY_TIDY[name].plain
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if owner in self.renames and (name == owner or name.startswith(owner + ".")):
+            return self.renames[owner] + name[len(owner):]
+        return self.twins.get(name, name)
+
+    def note(self, path: Path, offset: int, decl: str | None, kind: str, detail: str = ""):
+        src = self.source(path)
+        self.manual.append(Manual(str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), src.line_of(offset), decl or "",
+                                  kind, detail))
+
+    def need(self, module: str, constant: str, public: bool) -> None:
+        defining = self.model.constants.get(constant, {}).get("m")
+        if defining and defining != module:
+            self.needs[module][defining] = self.needs[module].get(defining, False) or public
+
+    def notions_of(self, name: str) -> list[Notion]:
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        return [BY_TIDY[t] for t in const.get("tidy", []) if t in BY_TIDY]
+
+    # Names.
+
+    def rename_at(self, src: SourceFile, start: int, end: int, old: str, new: str) -> str | None:
+        """The written form of `new` replacing the reference to `old` at `start`."""
+        token = src.text[start:end]
+        if old == new:
+            return token
+        if start and src.text[start - 1] == ".":  # field or leading-dot notation
+            if old.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] == new.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]:
+                return token
+            if old.rsplit(".", 1)[0] == new.rsplit(".", 1)[0] and "." not in token:
+                return new.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
+            return None
+        candidate = renamed_token(token, old, new)
+        if candidate is not None and not candidate.lstrip("@").startswith("_root_."):
+            return candidate

body:
Measurement stubs are written into ordinary source files by `plan_stubs`/`rewrite`, without quarantine or rollback. `lake_build` uses non-strict `lake build`, so a test-only `sorry` warning can leave code 0; `check_build` then returns `status: passed` with a nonempty `stubbed` list. Reproduced with a stubbed `theorem probe : True`; Markdown omits the taint, and `main` at line 1878 returns 0 even for failed verification.

Please isolate measurement output from the ordinary source checkout (or remove the stub mode), mark any stubbed result visibly incomplete rather than passed, and return nonzero for failed/stubbed `--verify`. Normal verification should use strict build checks. Test the complete write/report/exit boundary, including a test-only stub. Full strict CI/hygiene catches the resulting `sorry`, but that does not make this local measurement flow safe.
