+# --- Lean source helpers (unit-tested in scripts/test_tidy_sweep.py) ----------------------------
+
+OPENERS, CLOSERS = "([{⦃⟨‹", ")]}⦄⟩›"
+IDENT = re.compile(qr.IDENT.pattern)
+KEYWORDS = {"by", "fun", "λ", "with", "at", "using", "from", "then", "else", "do", "in", "if",
+            "match", "show", "have", "let", "calc", "only", "generalizing", "says", "where",
+            "deriving", "termination_by", "decreasing_by", "obtain", "rcases", "refine", "exact"}
+COMMAND_KEYWORD = re.compile(r"#?[A-Za-z_]+")
+NAME_ONLY_COMMANDS = {"#print", "#check", "#guard_msgs", "attribute", "open", "export", "#eval",
+                      "#reduce", "#synth", "add_decl_doc", "#lint", "#help"}
+LEMMA_LIST_TACTIC = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:simp|simp_all|dsimp|simp_rw|rw|rwa|rewrite|erw|nth_rewrite|nth_rw|simpa|fun_prop|"
+    r"aesop|norm_num|field_simp|grind|polytime|positivity|unfold|delta|gcongr|subst_vars|"
+    r"continuity|measurability|bound|decide|omega|linarith|nlinarith|exact\?|apply\?|"
+    r"rw_mod_cast|push_cast|norm_cast|simp_arith|conv)\b[^\[\]\n]*$")
+
+
+def match_bracket(mask: str, i: int, limit: int | None = None) -> int:
+    """The index of the bracket closing the one at `mask[i]`, or -1."""
+    depth, end = 0, len(mask) if limit is None else limit
+    for j in range(i, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+            if depth == 0:
+                return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def find_top_level(mask: str, start: int, end: int, token: str) -> int:
+    """The first `token` at bracket depth 0 in `mask[start:end]`, or -1. `:` excludes `:=`."""
+    depth = 0
+    for j in range(start, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+        elif depth == 0 and mask.startswith(token, j):
+            if token == ":" and (mask.startswith(":=", j) or mask.startswith("::", j)
+                                 or (j and mask[j - 1] == ":")):
+                continue
+            return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def line_indent(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    start = text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+    return len(text[start:]) - len(text[start:].lstrip(" "))
+
+
+def column(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    return offset - (text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1)
+
+
+def atom_end(mask: str, i: int, limit: int) -> int:
+    """The end of the atom (identifier, number, `?_`, bracket group, `.ident`) at `i` together
+    with directly attached projections (`.field`, `.1`), or `i` when no atom starts there."""
+    if i >= limit:
+        return i
+    char = mask[i]
+    if char in OPENERS:
+        end = match_bracket(mask, i, limit)
+        if end < 0:
+            return i
+        j = end + 1
+    elif char == "." and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char == "?" and mask.startswith("?_", i):
+        j = i + 2
+    elif char == "@" and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char.isdigit():
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and (mask[j].isalnum() or mask[j] == "."):
+            j += 1
+    else:
+        match = IDENT.match(mask, i)
+        if not match or match[0].rstrip(".") in KEYWORDS:
+            return i
+        j = match.end()
+    while j < limit and mask[j] == "." and j + 1 < limit and (
+            mask[j + 1].isdigit() or IDENT.match(mask, j + 1)):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, j + 1).end() if IDENT.match(mask, j + 1) else j + 2
+    return min(j, limit)
+
+
+NAMED_ARG = re.compile(r"\(\s*[^\W\d][\w'₀-₉]*\s*:=")
+
+
+def parse_args(mask: str, pos: int, limit: int, count: int, base_indent: int,
+               named: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    """Up to `count` positional application arguments after `pos`: atoms separated by blanks,
+    continuing onto lines indented more than `base_indent`. Named arguments `(x := e)` are
+    skipped and, when `named` is given, appended to it."""
+    args = []
+    i = pos
+    while len(args) < count and i < limit:
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and mask[j] in " \t":
+            j += 1
+        if j < limit and mask[j] == "\n":
+            k = j
+            while k < limit and mask[k] in " \t\n":
+                k += 1
+            if k >= limit or line_indent(mask, k) <= base_indent:
+                break
+            j = k
+        if j == i and args:
+            break  # no blank after the previous argument
+        end = atom_end(mask, j, limit)
+        if end == j:
+            break
+        if NAMED_ARG.match(mask, j):
+            if named is not None:
+                named.append((j, end))
+        else:
+            args.append((j, end))
+        i = end
+    return args
+
+
+def strip_space(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    while start < end and mask[start].isspace():
+        start += 1
+    while end > start and mask[end - 1].isspace():
+        end -= 1
+    return start, end
+
+
+def is_atomic_application(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    """For text `P args` in `mask[start:end]` made of atoms only, the span of `P`; else None."""
+    start, end = strip_space(mask, start, end)
+    head = atom_end(mask, start, end)
+    if head == start:
+        return None
+    args = parse_args(mask, head, end, 10 ** 6, -1)
+    last = args[-1][1] if args else head
+    return (start, head) if strip_space(mask, last, end)[0] == end else None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Binder:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    bracket: str
+    names: list[str]
+    type_start: int
+    type_end: int
+    default: bool
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DeclText:
+    start: int
+    sel_start: int
+    sel_end: int
+    end: int
+    binders: list[Binder]
+    colon: int  # the `:` before the type, or -1
+    assign: int  # the `:=` before the body, or -1
+    problems: list[str]
+
+
+def parse_decl(mask: str, start: int, sel_start: int, sel_end: int, end: int) -> DeclText:
+    """Binders, type and body of the declaration whose name ends at `sel_end`."""
+    assign = find_top_level(mask, sel_end, end, ":=")
+    stop = assign if assign >= 0 else end
+    binders, problems, colon = [], [], -1
+    i = sel_end
+    if mask.startswith(".{", i):
+        i = match_bracket(mask, i + 1, stop) + 1
+    while i < stop:
+        char = mask[i]
+        if char.isspace():
+            i += 1
+        elif char in "([{⦃":
+            close = match_bracket(mask, i, stop)
+            if close < 0:
+                problems.append("unbalanced binder")
+                break
+            inner = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":")
+            default = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":=")
+            if inner < 0:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:close].split(), close
+            else:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:inner].split(), inner + 1
+            type_end = default if default >= 0 else close
+            binders.append(Binder(i, close + 1, char, names, type_start, type_end,
+                                  default >= 0))
+            i = close + 1
+        elif char == ":":
+            colon = i
+            break
+        else:
+            problems.append("binder without brackets")
+            break
+    if assign < 0:
+        problems.append("no `:=` (pattern-matching definition)")
+    return DeclText(start, sel_start, sel_end, end, binders, colon, assign, problems)
+
+
+def proof_parts(text: str, assign: int, end: int) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    """The text after `:=` and whether it is a tactic block."""
+    body = text[assign + 2:end]
+    return body, re.match(r"\s*by(?:\s|$)", body) is not None
+
+
+def collapse(text: str) -> str:
+    return " ".join(text.split())
+
+
+# --- Scopes and names ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+SCOPE_COMMAND = re.compile(
+    r"^(?P<mods>(?:@\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:public|private|noncomputable|protected|meta)\s+)*)"
+    r"(?P<kw>namespace|section|end|open|mutual)\b(?P<rest>[^\n]*)", re.M)
+
+
+def namespaces_of(names) -> set[str]:
+    """Every name and every proper prefix of a name, as namespaces."""
+    out = set()
+    for name in names:
+        parts = name.split(".")
+        for i in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+            out.add(".".join(parts[:i]))
+    return out
+
+
+class Scopes:
+    """The current namespace and opened namespaces at each offset of a masked source."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mask: str, namespaces: set[str]):
+        self.points: list[tuple[int, str, tuple[str, ...]]] = [(0, "", ())]
+        self.once: list[tuple[int, int, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
+        stack: list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]] = []
+        starts = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(mask)] + [len(mask)]
+        for match in SCOPE_COMMAND.finditer(mask):
+            kw, rest = match["kw"], match["rest"].split()
+            namespace = ".".join(n for k, n, _ in stack if k == "namespace" and n)
+            opens = [o for _, _, os in stack for o in os]
+            if kw == "namespace" and rest:
+                stack.append(("namespace", rest[0], []))
+            elif kw in ("section", "mutual"):
+                stack.append((kw, rest[0] if rest and kw == "section" else "", []))
+            elif kw == "end":
+                if stack:
+                    stack.pop()
+            elif kw == "open":
+                one_shot = bool(rest) and rest[-1] == "in"
+                words = [w for w in (rest[:-1] if one_shot else rest)
+                         if w not in ("scoped", "hiding", "renaming", "→", "private")
+                         and not w.startswith("(") and IDENT.fullmatch(w)]
+                resolved = []
+                for word in words:
+                    prefixes = [".".join(namespace.split(".")[:i])
+                                for i in range(len(namespace.split(".")), -1, -1)] if namespace \
+                        else [""]
+                    found = [p + "." + word if p else word for p in prefixes + opens + resolved
+                             if (p + "." + word if p else word) in namespaces]
+                    resolved += found or [word]
+                if one_shot:
+                    after = next((s for s in starts if s > match.end()), len(mask))
+                    following = next((s for s in starts if s > after), len(mask))
+                    self.once.append((match.start(), following, tuple(resolved)))
+                    continue
+                if not stack:
+                    stack.append(("file", "", []))
+                stack[-1][2].extend(resolved)
+            namespace = ".".join(n for k, n, _ in stack if k == "namespace" and n)
+            opens = [o for _, _, os in stack for o in os]
+            self.points.append((match.end(), namespace, tuple(opens)))
+
+    def at(self, offset: int) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
+        namespace, opens = "", ()
+        for point, ns, os in self.points:
+            if point > offset:
+                break
+            namespace, opens = ns, os
+        extra = tuple(o for start, end, os in self.once if start <= offset < end for o in os)
+        return namespace, opens + extra
+
+    def prefixes(self, offset: int) -> list[str]:
+        """Namespaces a written name may be relative to, innermost first (`""` is the root)."""
+        namespace, opens = self.at(offset)
+        parts = namespace.split(".") if namespace else []
+        return [".".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1)] + list(opens)
+
+
+def written_name(target: str, prefixes: list[str], known: set[str]) -> str:
+    """The shortest suffix of `target` that resolves to it, and to nothing else, from a position
+    whose namespace prefixes and opened namespaces are `prefixes`."""
+    parts = target.split(".")
+    for k in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+        suffix = ".".join(parts[-k:])
+        hits = {p + "." + suffix if p else suffix for p in prefixes}
+        resolved = {h for h in hits if h in known or h == target}
+        if resolved == {target}:
+            return suffix
+    return target
+
+
+def renamed_token(token: str, old: str, new: str) -> str | None:
+    """`token` (a written form of `old`) with the renamed part, when the written prefix still
+    resolves the same way (`old = P.token` and `new = P.result`); otherwise None."""
+    at = "@" if token.startswith("@") else ""
+    bare = token[len(at):]
+    root = "_root_." if bare.startswith("_root_.") else ""
+    bare = bare[len(root):]
+    if not (old == bare or old.endswith("." + bare)):
+        return None
+    prefix = old[:len(old) - len(bare)]
+    if not new.startswith(prefix):
+        return None
+    result = new[len(prefix):]
+    if not result or (prefix and result.startswith(".")):
+        return None
+    return at + root + result
+
+
+# --- Edits --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Replace:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    text: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Wrap:
+    """Text inserted before `open` and after `close`; `site` orders wraps with equal spans (the
+    wrap of the site that starts first is outermost)."""
+    open: int
+    close: int
+    before: str
+    after: str
+    site: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Region:
+    """A span whose edited text is then transformed by `build`."""
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    build: object
+    decl: str
+
+
+def render(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap], lo: int, hi: int) -> str:
+    """`text[lo:hi]` with the replacements and wraps inside it applied. At one position, wraps
+    close (innermost first) before others open (outermost first), then a replacement starts."""
+    reps = sorted((r for r in replaces if lo <= r.start and r.end <= hi),
+                  key=lambda r: (r.start, r.end))
+    ws = [w for w in wraps if lo <= w.open and w.close <= hi]
+    points = sorted({r.start for r in reps} | {w.open for w in ws} | {w.close for w in ws})
+    starting = defaultdict(list)
+    for r in reps:
+        starting[r.start].append(r)
+    out, cur = [], lo
+    for p in points:
+        if p < cur:
+            continue  # inside a replaced span
+        out.append(text[cur:p])
+        out += [w.after for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.close == p),
+                                        key=lambda w: (-w.open, -w.site))]
+        out += [w.before for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.open == p),
+                                         key=lambda w: (-w.close, w.site))]
+        cur = p
+        for r in starting.get(p, []):
+            out.append(r.text)
+            cur = max(cur, r.end)
+    out.append(text[cur:hi])
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def apply_edits(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap],
+                regions: list[Region]) -> str:
+    out, cur = [], 0
+    for region in sorted(regions, key=lambda r: r.start):
+        out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, region.start))
+        out.append(region.build(render(text, replaces, wraps, region.start, region.end)))
+        cur = region.end
+    out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, len(text)))
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Round trips --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+OF_TIDY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.'])(?:(?:[\w.']*\.)?Computable(?:In(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|"
+                     r"FPTTime))\.|\.)of_tidy\b")
+DOT_ROUND_TRIP = re.compile(r"\.tidy\.computableIn(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|FPTTime)\b")
+
+
+def cancel_round_trips(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """Remove `of_tidy (x.tidy)`, `of_tidy <| x.tidy` and `x.tidy.computableIn…` round trips,
+    where `x` is an atom. Returns the new text and the number of removals."""
+    count = 0
+    while True:
+        mask = masks(text)[1]
+        change = None
+        for match in DOT_ROUND_TRIP.finditer(mask):
+            change = (match.start(), match.end(), "")
+            break
+        if change is None:
+            for match in OF_TIDY.finditer(mask):
+                i = match.end()
+                while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                    i += 1
+                pipe = mask.startswith("<|", i)
+                if pipe:
+                    i += 2
+                    while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                        i += 1
+                end = atom_end(mask, i, len(mask))
+                if end == i:
+                    continue
+                inner = (i, end)
+                if mask[i] == "(" and match_bracket(mask, i) == end - 1:
+                    inner = strip_space(mask, i + 1, end - 1)
+                start, stop = inner
+                if not mask[start:stop].endswith(".tidy") or atom_end(mask, start, stop) != stop:
+                    continue
+                core_end = stop - len(".tidy")
+                if atom_end(mask, start, core_end) != core_end:
+                    continue
+                if pipe:
+                    after = end
+                    while after < len(mask) and mask[after] in " \t":
+                        after += 1
+                    if after < len(mask) and mask[after] not in CLOSERS + "\n,":
+                        continue
+                change = (match.start(), end, text[start:core_end])
+                break
+        if change is None:
+            return text, count
+        start, end, new = change
+        new_mask = masks(new)[1]
+        if (start > 0 and text[start - 1] == "(" and end < len(text) and text[end] == ")"
+                and atom_end(new_mask, 0, len(new)) == len(new) and not new.startswith("@")):
+            start, end = start - 1, end + 1
+        text = text[:start] + new + text[end:]
+        count += 1
+
+
+# --- Wrapping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Hyp:
+    names: list[str]
+    old_type: str  # one line
+    simple: bool
+
+
+def reindent(lines: list[str], delta: int) -> list[str] | None:
+    """Shift lines by `delta` columns; None when that would remove non-blank text."""
+    out = []
+    for line in lines:
+        if not line.strip():
+            out.append("")
+        elif delta >= 0:
+            out.append(" " * delta + line)
+        elif len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" ")) >= -delta:
+            out.append(line[-delta:])
+        else:
+            return None
+    return out
+
+
+def wrap_proof(body: str, body_column: int, decl_indent: int, hyps: list[Hyp],
+               conclusion: str | None, simple_conclusion: bool, iffs: str) -> str | None:
+    """The new text after `:=` for a proof `body` of the old (tidy) statement, now stated plainly:
+    tidy hypotheses are recovered, and the old conclusion converted. `body_column` is the column
+    of the first character of `body`. None when the layout cannot be preserved."""
+    stripped = body.lstrip()
+    lead = body[:len(body) - len(stripped)]
+    first_col = body_column + len(lead) if "\n" not in lead else len(lead.rsplit("\n", 1)[1])
+    stripped = stripped.rstrip()
+    tactic = re.match(r"by(?=\s|$)", stripped) is not None
+    if not hyps and simple_conclusion and not tactic:
+        return f"{lead}.of_tidy ({stripped})"
+    k = decl_indent + 2
+    rebind = []
+    for hyp in hyps:
+        for name in hyp.names:
+            rebind.append(f"have {name} := {name}.tidy" if hyp.simple else
+                          f"have {name} : {hyp.old_type} := by simpa only [{iffs}] using {name}")
+    if tactic:
+        rest = stripped[2:]
+        if rest.lstrip(" \t").startswith("\n") or not rest.strip():
+            lines = rest.lstrip(" \t")[1:].split("\n")
+            nonblank = [ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()]
+            if not nonblank:
+                return None
+            k = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        else:
+            first_line, _, tail = rest.lstrip(" \t").partition("\n")
+            tactic_col = first_col + 2 + (len(rest) - len(rest.lstrip(" \t")))
+            shifted = reindent(tail.split("\n"), k - tactic_col) if tail else []
+            if shifted is None:
+                return None
+            lines = [" " * k + first_line] + shifted
+        pad = " " * k
+        out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+        if conclusion is None:
+            out += lines
+        elif simple_conclusion:
+            out += [pad + "refine .of_tidy ?_"] + lines
+        else:
+            inner = reindent(lines, 2)
+            out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} := by"] + inner + \
+                [pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+        return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+    first, _, tail = stripped.partition("\n")
+    tail_lines = tail.split("\n") if tail else []
+    nonblank = [ln for ln in tail_lines if ln.strip()]
+    shift = 0
+    if nonblank:
+        least = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        shift = max(0, k + 2 - least)
+    tail_lines = reindent(tail_lines, shift) or tail_lines
+    pad = " " * k
+    out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+    term = "\n".join([first] + tail_lines)
+    if conclusion is None:
+        out.append(pad + "exact " + term)
+    elif simple_conclusion:
+        out.append(pad + "exact .of_tidy (" + term + ")")
+    else:
+        out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} :=", pad + "  " + term,
+                pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+    return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Planning -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Manual:
+    path: str
+    line: int
+    decl: str
+    kind: str
+    detail: str = ""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Ref:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    decl: str | None
+
+
+class SourceFile:
+    def __init__(self, path: Path, namespaces: set[str]):
+        self.path = path
+        self.text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.code, self.mask = masks(self.text) if path.suffix == ".lean" else (self.text,) * 2
+        self.lines = self.text.split("\n")
+        self.starts = [0]
+        for line in self.lines:
+            self.starts.append(self.starts[-1] + len(line) + 1)
+        self.commands = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(self.mask)]
+        self._namespaces = namespaces
+        self._scopes: Scopes | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def scopes(self) -> Scopes:
+        if self._scopes is None:
+            self._scopes = Scopes(self.mask, self._namespaces)
+        return self._scopes
+
+    def at(self, line: int, column16: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 0-based line and UTF-16 column (`.ilean` positions)."""
+        return self.starts[line] + qr.utf16_index(self.lines[line], column16)
+
+    def at_range(self, line: int, column: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 1-based line and code-point column (declaration ranges)."""
+        return self.starts[line - 1] + column
+
+    def line_of(self, offset: int) -> int:
+        """The 1-based line of an offset."""
+        return self.text.count("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+
+    def command_keyword(self, offset: int) -> str:
+        starts = [s for s in self.commands if s <= offset]
+        if not starts:
+            return ""
+        match = COMMAND_KEYWORD.match(self.mask, starts[-1])
+        return match[0] if match else ""
+
+    def comment_spans(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+        if self.path.suffix != ".lean":
+            return [(0, len(self.text))]
+        spans, i = [], 0
+        while i < len(self.text):
+            if self.code[i] != self.text[i]:
+                j = i
+                while j < len(self.text) and self.code[j] != self.text[j] or (
+                        j < len(self.text) and self.text[j] == "\n" and j + 1 < len(self.text)
+                        and self.code[j + 1] != self.text[j + 1]):
+                    j += 1
+                spans.append((i, j))
+                i = j
+            else:
+                i += 1
+        return spans
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileEdits:
+    replaces: list[Replace] = field(default_factory=list)
+    wraps: list[Wrap] = field(default_factory=list)
+    regions: list[Region] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class Planner:
+    """The edits of one area's batch: case 2 declarations restated and renamed, their clients
+    converted, and case 1 twins used in translated proofs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model: Model, entries: list[Entry], registry: dict[str, str], area: str,
+                 force_wrap: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+                 force_bridge: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset(),
+                 stub: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset()):
+        self.model, self.area, self.force_wrap = model, area, force_wrap
+        self.force_bridge, self.stub = force_bridge, stub
+        self.entries = {e.name: e for e in entries}
+        self.batch = {e.name: e for e in entries if e.area == area and e.case == "2"}
+        self.renames = {name: e.target for name, e in self.batch.items()}
+        self.twins = {o: p for o, p in registry.items() if p in model.constants}
+        self.files: dict[Path, FileEdits] = defaultdict(FileEdits)
+        self.sources: dict[Path, SourceFile] = {}
+        self.manual: list[Manual] = []
+        self.decls: dict[str, dict] = {}
+        self.spans: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.needs: dict[str, dict[str, bool]] = defaultdict(dict)
+        self.sites = Counter()
+        self.imports: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
+        self.known = model.known | set(self.renames.values())
+        self.namespaces = namespaces_of(self.known)
+        self.round_trips = 0
+        self.deferred: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        self.bridged: list[str] = []
+        self.stubbed: list[str] = []
+
+    # Sources and references.
+
+    def source(self, path: Path) -> SourceFile:
+        if path not in self.sources:
+            self.sources[path] = SourceFile(path, self.namespaces)
+        return self.sources[path]
+
+    def refs(self, module: str) -> list[Ref]:
+        src = self.source(qr.source_path(module))
+        out = []
+        for name, _, info in self.model.lib.references(module):
+            for u in info["usages"]:
+                out.append(Ref(name, src.at(u[0], u[1]), src.at(u[2], u[3]),
+                               u[4] if len(u) == 5 else None))
+        return out
+
+    def ref_kind(self, name: str) -> str:
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return "pred"
+        if owner in self.renames:
+            return "renamed"
+        if name in self.twins:
+            return "twin"
+        if name in BRIDGES:
+            return "bridge"
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        if const.get("tidy") or const.get("tb") or is_tidy_constant(name):
+            return "tidy"
+        return "plain"
+
+    def new_name(self, name: str) -> str:
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return BY_TIDY[name].plain
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if owner in self.renames and (name == owner or name.startswith(owner + ".")):
+            return self.renames[owner] + name[len(owner):]
+        return self.twins.get(name, name)
+
+    def note(self, path: Path, offset: int, decl: str | None, kind: str, detail: str = ""):
+        src = self.source(path)
+        self.manual.append(Manual(str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), src.line_of(offset), decl or "",
+                                  kind, detail))
+
+    def need(self, module: str, constant: str, public: bool) -> None:
+        defining = self.model.constants.get(constant, {}).get("m")
+        if defining and defining != module:
+            self.needs[module][defining] = self.needs[module].get(defining, False) or public
+
+    def notions_of(self, name: str) -> list[Notion]:
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        return [BY_TIDY[t] for t in const.get("tidy", []) if t in BY_TIDY]
+
+    # Names.
+
+    def rename_at(self, src: SourceFile, start: int, end: int, old: str, new: str) -> str | None:
+        """The written form of `new` replacing the reference to `old` at `start`."""
+        token = src.text[start:end]
+        if old == new:
+            return token
+        if start and src.text[start - 1] == ".":  # field or leading-dot notation
+            if old.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] == new.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]:
+                return token
+            if old.rsplit(".", 1)[0] == new.rsplit(".", 1)[0] and "." not in token:
+                return new.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
+            return None
+        candidate = renamed_token(token, old, new)
+        if candidate is not None and not candidate.lstrip("@").startswith("_root_."):
+            return candidate
+        at = "@" if token.startswith("@") else ""
+        return at + written_name(new, src.scopes.prefixes(start), self.known)
+
+    # Declarations.
+
+    def plan(self) -> "Planner":
+        analyses = {name: self.analyse_decl(self.batch[name]) for name in sorted(self.batch)}
+        changed = True
+        while changed:  # a statement naming a deferred declaration is deferred too
+            changed = False
+            for name, a in analyses.items():
+                if name in self.deferred or a is None:
+                    continue
+                reasons = list(a["defer"]) + [
+                    f"statement names deferred `{x.name}`" for x in a["sig_refs"]
+                    if (qr.owner_of(x.name, self.model.owners) or x.name) in self.deferred]
+                if reasons:
+                    self.deferred[name] = reasons
+                    changed = True
+        for name, a in analyses.items():
+            if a is None:
+                self.deferred.setdefault(name, ["declaration range missing"])
+        for name in self.deferred:
+            self.renames.pop(name, None)
+        for name in sorted(self.batch):
+            if name in self.deferred:
+                self.defer(name, analyses[name])
+            else:
+                self.plan_decl(self.batch[name], analyses[name])
+        for name in sorted(self.renames):
+            self.plan_clients(name)
+        self.plan_bridges()
+        self.plan_stubs()
+        self.plan_comments()
+        self.plan_imports()
+        return self
+
+    def analyse_decl(self, entry: Entry) -> dict | None:
+        """Parse a declaration and find what prevents restating it."""
+        decl = self.model.decls[entry.name]
+        module, path = decl["module"], qr.source_path(decl["module"])
+        if not decl["range"]:
+            return None
+        src = self.source(path)
+        r = decl["range"]
+        start, end = src.at_range(r[0], r[1]), src.at_range(r[2], r[3])
+        sel_start, sel_end = src.at_range(r[4], r[5]), src.at_range(r[6], r[7])
+        dt = parse_decl(src.mask, start, sel_start, sel_end, end)
+        refs = [x for x in self.refs(module) if start <= x.start < end]
+        split = dt.assign if dt.assign >= 0 else end
+        a = {"module": module, "path": path, "src": src, "dt": dt, "start": start, "end": end,
+             "sig_refs": [x for x in refs if x.start < split],
+             "proof_refs": [x for x in refs if x.start >= split], "defer": []}
+        if entry.target != entry.name and renamed_token(
+                src.text[sel_start:sel_end], entry.name, entry.target) is None:
+            a["defer"].append("name written inside a tidy namespace")
+        for x in a["sig_refs"]:
+            if self.ref_kind(x.name) in ("bridge", "tidy"):
+                a["defer"].append(f"statement names tidy `{x.name}`")
+        written = sum(1 for x in a["sig_refs"] if x.name in BY_TIDY)
+        if not written or self.hidden_tidy(entry.name, src, dt, a["sig_refs"]):
+            a["defer"].append("tidy predicate from a `variable` command or notation")
+        return a
+
+    def plan_bridges(self) -> None:
+        """Let the tidy `fun_prop` calls of the declarations in `force_bridge` use the restated
+        (plain) certificates: `attribute [local fun_prop] ComputableInPolyTime.tidy in`."""
+        notions = {n for name in self.renames for n in self.notions_of(name)}
+        for module, name in sorted(self.force_bridge):
+            ranges = self.model.lib.ileans.get(module, {}).get("decls", {})
+            path = qr.source_path(module)
+            src = self.source(path)
+            if name.startswith("line:"):
+                start = src.starts[command_start_line(src, int(name[5:]))]
+            elif name in ranges:
+                start = src.at(ranges[name][0], ranges[name][1])
+            else:
+                continue
+            if name in self.batch:
+                own = set(self.notions_of(name))
+            else:
+                own = notions
+            lines = "".join(
+                f"attribute [local fun_prop] "
+                f"{written_name(n.to_tidy, src.scopes.prefixes(start), self.known)} in\n"
+                for n in sorted(own, key=lambda n: n.tidy))
+            self.files[path].replaces.append(Replace(start, start, lines))
+            for n in own:
+                self.need(module, n.to_tidy, False)
+            self.bridged.append(name)
+
+    def plan_stubs(self) -> None:
+        """Measurement only (`--stub-failures`): replace the proofs of `stub` by `sorry`, so that
+        a build reaches the modules downstream of them."""
+        for module, name in sorted(self.stub):
+            ranges = self.model.lib.ileans.get(module, {}).get("decls", {})
+            if name not in ranges:
+                continue
+            path = qr.source_path(module)
+            src, r = self.source(path), ranges[name]
+            start, end = src.at(r[0], r[1]), src.at(r[2], r[3])
+            assign = find_top_level(src.mask, src.at(r[6], r[7]), end, ":=")
+            if assign < 0:
+                continue
+            fe = self.files[path]
+            fe.regions = [g for g in fe.regions if not (g.start >= start and g.end <= end)]
+            fe.regions.append(Region(assign + 2, end, lambda _: " by\n  sorry", name))
+            self.stubbed.append(name)
+
+    def defer(self, name: str, a: dict | None) -> None:
+        """A declaration left tidy in this batch; references to it stay unchanged."""
+        decl = self.model.decls[name]
+        path = qr.source_path(decl["module"])
+        self.decls[name] = {"name": name, "target": self.batch[name].target,
+                            "path": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)),
+                            "line": decl["range"][0] if decl["range"] else 0,
+                            "mode": "deferred", "blocking": [],
+                            "issues": self.deferred[name]}
+        for reason in self.deferred[name]:
+            self.note(path, a["start"] if a else 0, name, "deferred", reason)
+
+    def plan_decl(self, entry: Entry, a: dict) -> None:
+        module, path, src, dt = a["module"], a["path"], a["src"], a["dt"]
+        start, end, sig_refs, proof_refs = a["start"], a["end"], a["sig_refs"], a["proof_refs"]
+        fe = self.files[path]
+        info = {"name": entry.name, "target": entry.target, "path": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)),
+                "line": src.line_of(start), "mode": "manual", "blocking": [], "issues": []}
+        self.decls[entry.name] = info
+        self.spans[module].append((start, end, entry.name))
+
+        def issue(kind: str, detail: str = "", offset: int = start) -> None:
+            info["issues"].append(kind)
+            self.note(path, offset, entry.name, kind, detail)
+
+        if entry.target != entry.name:
+            token = src.text[dt.sel_start:dt.sel_end]
+            fe.replaces.append(Replace(dt.sel_start, dt.sel_end,
+                                       renamed_token(token, entry.name, entry.target)))
+        for x in sig_refs:
+            if self.ref_kind(x.name) in ("pred", "renamed", "twin"):
+                new = self.rename_at(src, x.start, x.end, x.name, self.new_name(x.name))
+                if new is None:
+                    issue("statement reference in dot notation", x.name, x.start)
+                    continue
+                fe.replaces.append(Replace(x.start, x.end, new))
+                self.need(module, self.new_name(x.name), True)
+        doc = src.text[start:dt.sel_start]
+        if TIDY_WORD.search(doc.split("-/")[0] if "/--" in doc else ""):
+            issue("docstring mentions tidiness (review wording)")
+        info["blocking"] = sorted({x.name for x in proof_refs
+                                   if self.ref_kind(x.name) in ("bridge", "tidy")
+                                   and x.name != entry.name})
+        wrap, problems = self.wrap_plan(entry, src, dt, sig_refs)
+        if not info["blocking"] and entry.name not in self.force_wrap and dt.assign >= 0:
+            info["mode"] = "translate"
+        elif wrap is not None:
+            info["mode"] = "wrap"
+        else:
+            for problem in problems:
+                issue("cannot wrap the proof", problem)
+            if not info["blocking"] and dt.assign >= 0:
+                info["mode"] = "translate"
+            return
+        for x in proof_refs:
+            kind = self.ref_kind(x.name)
+            if info["mode"] == "translate" and kind in ("pred", "renamed", "twin"):
+                new = self.rename_at(src, x.start, x.end, x.name, self.new_name(x.name))
+                if new is None:
+                    issue("proof reference in dot notation to a renamed twin", x.name, x.start)
+                elif new != src.text[x.start:x.end]:
+                    fe.replaces.append(Replace(x.start, x.end, new))
+                if kind == "twin":
+                    self.need(module, self.new_name(x.name), False)
+            elif info["mode"] == "wrap" and kind == "renamed" and x.name != entry.name:
+                if x.name in self.renames:
+                    self.convert(path, module, x.start, x.end, x.name, entry.name, "tidy")
+                else:
+                    issue("generated constant of a restated declaration", x.name, x.start)
+        if info["mode"] == "wrap":
+            fe.regions.append(Region(dt.assign + 2, end, wrap, entry.name))
+            for notion in self.notions_of(entry.name):
+                self.need(module, notion.of_tidy, False)
+                self.need(module, notion.iff, False)
+
+    def hidden_tidy(self, name: str, src: SourceFile, dt: DeclText, sig_refs: list[Ref]) -> bool:
+        """Whether the statement has more tidy binders or conclusions than are written."""
+        sg = self.model.constants.get(name, {}).get("sg")
+        if not sg:
+            return False
+        lean = sum(1 for _, flag in sg[0] if flag) + (sg[1] != 0)
+        written = 0
+        for b in dt.binders:
+            if any(b.type_start <= x.start < b.type_end and x.name in BY_TIDY for x in sig_refs):
+                written += max(1, len(b.names))
+        if dt.colon >= 0:
+            written += sum(1 for x in sig_refs if x.start > dt.colon and x.name in BY_TIDY)
+        return lean > written
+
+    def wrap_plan(self, entry: Entry, src: SourceFile, dt: DeclText, sig_refs: list[Ref]):
+        """The proof transformation of a wrapped declaration, or None and the problems."""
+        problems = [p for p in dt.problems]
+        preds = [x for x in sig_refs if x.name in BY_TIDY]
+        hyps = []
+        for b in dt.binders:
+            inside = [x for x in preds if b.type_start <= x.start < b.type_end]
+            if not inside:
+                continue
+            if b.bracket == "[" or not b.names or "_" in b.names:
+                problems.append("unnamed or instance tidy hypothesis")
+            if b.default:
+                problems.append("tidy hypothesis with a default value")
+            if src.mask[b.type_start:b.type_end] != src.text[b.type_start:b.type_end]:
+                problems.append("comment inside a tidy hypothesis")
+            head = is_atomic_application(src.mask, b.type_start, b.type_end)
+            simple = head is not None and any(x.start == head[0] for x in inside)
+            hyps.append(Hyp(b.names, collapse(src.text[b.type_start:b.type_end]), simple))
+        conclusion, simple = None, False
+        if dt.colon >= 0 and dt.assign >= 0:
+            inside = [x for x in preds if x.start > dt.colon]
+            if inside:
+                conclusion = collapse(src.text[dt.colon + 1:dt.assign])
+                head = is_atomic_application(src.mask, dt.colon + 1, dt.assign)
+                simple = head is not None and any(x.start == head[0] for x in inside)
+                if src.mask[dt.colon + 1:dt.assign] != src.text[dt.colon + 1:dt.assign]:
+                    problems.append("comment inside the statement")
+        if dt.assign >= 0 and re.search(r"(?m)^\s*(?:termination_by|decreasing_by|where)\b",
+                                        src.mask[dt.assign:dt.end]):
+            problems.append("termination or `where` clauses")
+        if self.hidden_tidy(entry.name, src, dt, sig_refs):
+            problems.append("tidy hypothesis from a `variable` command or notation")
+        if problems:
+            return None, problems
+        prefixes = src.scopes.prefixes(dt.start)
+        iffs = ", ".join(written_name(n.iff, prefixes, self.known)
+                         for n in self.notions_of(entry.name))
+        body_column = column(src.text, dt.assign + 2)
+        indent = line_indent(src.text, dt.sel_start)
+        args = (body_column, indent, hyps, conclusion, simple, iffs)
+        if wrap_proof(src.text[dt.assign + 2:dt.end], *args) is None:
+            return None, ["proof layout"]
+        return (lambda body: wrap_proof(body, *args)), []
+
+    # Clients.
+
+    def in_batch_decl(self, module: str, offset: int) -> str | None:
+        for start, end, name in self.spans.get(module, ()):
+            if start <= offset < end:
+                return name
+        return None
+
+    def plan_clients(self, name: str) -> None:
+        for module, u in self.model.users(name):
+            path = qr.source_path(module)
+            src = self.source(path)
+            start, end = src.at(u[0], u[1]), src.at(u[2], u[3])
+            if self.in_batch_decl(module, start):
+                continue
+            context = "name" if src.command_keyword(start) in NAME_ONLY_COMMANDS else "tidy"
+            self.convert(path, module, start, end, name, u[4] if len(u) == 5 else None, context)
+
+    def convert(self, path: Path, module: str, start: int, end: int, old: str,
+                decl: str | None, context: str) -> None:
+        """Rename a reference to a restated declaration; in a proof that stays tidy, keep the
+        site's old type with `.tidy` around the application and `.of_tidy` around tidy
+        arguments."""
+        src, fe = self.source(path), self.files[path]
+        new = self.renames[old]
+        token = src.text[start:end]
+        written = self.rename_at(src, start, end, old, new)
+        self.sites[context] += 1
+        if written is None:
+            self.note(path, start, decl, "reference in dot notation", f"`{token}`")
+            return
+        if written != token:
+            fe.replaces.append(Replace(start, end, written))
+        if context != "tidy":
+            return
+        problem = self.convert_site(src, fe, start, end, old)
+        if problem:
+            self.note(path, start, decl, "reference kept tidy", f"`{token}`: {problem}")
+        else:
+            for notion in self.notions_of(old):
+                self.need(module, notion.of_tidy, False)
+
+    def convert_site(self, src: SourceFile, fe: FileEdits, start: int, end: int,
+                     old: str) -> str | None:
+        sg = self.model.constants.get(old, {}).get("sg")
+        if not sg:
+            return None
+        binders, conclusion = sg
+        mask = src.mask
+        opener = enclosing_opener(mask, start)
+        if opener >= 0 and mask[opener] == "[" and LEMMA_LIST_TACTIC.search(

body:
`f` is required to be computable without A, in both new WPP/LWPP oracle definitions. Conventional WPP^A/LWPP^A allows an FP^A target. The [authors’ FFK manuscript](https://lance.fortnow.com/papers/files/gaps.pdf), discussion following Definition5.13, explicitly distinguishes this issue and explains why eliminating the relativized gap does not eliminate the oracle from that target.

These Lean results can remain useful, but please distinguish the fixed-target classes in their names/API documentation, qualify every WPP/LWPP oracle identity (including the self-lowness and SPP-oracle claims), and remove the unqualified conventional identities from the PR description. ROADMAP must retain the target-relativized objective as remaining, rather than deleting it. Record #670 as a bounded milestone if that is the intended scope. Also verify the Lemma5.5/Theorem5.6 attributions against the cited edition; the author copies place this caveat after Definition5.13. A documentation/model-scope correction is sufficient; this review does not demand proving a broader theorem.

This definition rejects every previously queried message, whereas [Boneh–Shoup v0.6, Attack Game6.1 / Definition6.2](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf#page=234) forbids only previously returned (message,tag) pairs. Those notions differ for randomized MACScheme signing. Please explicitly call this the fresh-message EUF-CMA variant and distinguish it from the book’s stronger fresh-pair notion in the module/game/security docs and PR description. The deterministic prfMAC construction has a unique valid tag and is unaffected.

Also correct the PRF-to-MAC references throughout source/PR/task text: the bound is [Theorem6.2](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf#page=240), and the construction is in Section6.3. Theorem6.1 concerns verification queries; “Construction6.1” is not this construction. These are scope/attribution corrections, not a request to broaden the implementation.

+/-!
+# Uniform message authentication codes and PRF-based MACs
+
+A uniform symmetric message authentication code (`MACScheme`) consists of a strict probabilistic
+polynomial-time key generator `keyGen`, a strict probabilistic polynomial-time tag generator `sign`,
+and a deterministic polynomial-time tag verifier `verify` that accepts every tag produced by `sign`
+on an `n`-bit message under a secret key sampled at security parameter `n`. Unlike digital
+signatures (`SignatureScheme`), verification uses the same secret key as tag generation, and the
+adversary receives no public key.
+
+We formalize existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (`eufCmaGame`,
+`EUFCMA`) and under one-time adaptive chosen-message attack (`eufOneTimeGame`, `OneTimeEUFCMA`)
+against uniform strict oracle-PPT forgers (`IsOraclePPT`), and prove that any uniform
+`PseudorandomFunction` yields an `EUFCMA`-secure deterministic MAC (`prfMAC`,
+`PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC`), with the quantitative security reduction of
+[Boneh and Shoup, Theorem 6.1][BonehShoup2023]:
+$$\Pr[\text{Forge}] \le \mathrm{Adv}_{\mathrm{PRF}}(B(\mathcal{A}), n) + 2^{-n}.$$
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme`: uniform symmetric message authentication code on `n`-bit messages.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.signingOracle`, `eufCmaGame`, `EUFCMA`: full adaptive EUF-CMA experiment
+  and security predicate.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.oneTimeSigningOracle`, `eufOneTimeGame`, `OneTimeEUFCMA`: one-time
+  adaptive EUF-CMA experiment and security predicate.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.prfMAC`: canonical deterministic MAC constructed from a keyed function family.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.macLogHandler`, `Cslib.Crypto.macToPrfDistinguisher`: oracle logging handler and

+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.isPPTOn_eufCmaGame`, `isPPT_eufCmaGame`: strict PPT certificates for the
+  MAC EUF-CMA experiment.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.isPPTOn_eufOneTimeGame`, `isPPT_eufOneTimeGame`: strict PPT certificates
+  for the one-time MAC EUF-CMA experiment.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.EUFCMA.oneTimeEUFCMA`: full EUF-CMA security implies one-time EUF-CMA
+  security.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isOraclePPT_macToPrfDistinguisher`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.eval_prfRealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.succProbability_prfIdealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher_le`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.succProbability_eufCmaGame_prfMAC_le`: quantitative PRF-to-MAC forgery reduction
+  (Boneh–Shoup, Theorem 6.1).
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.oneTimeEUFCMA_prfMAC`: any secure uniform
+  `PseudorandomFunction` yields an `EUFCMA`-secure (and `OneTimeEUFCMA`-secure) `MACScheme`.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023], Chapter 6,
+  Sections 6.1–6.4 (Definitions 6.1–6.2, Construction 6.1, and Theorem 6.1).
+* [O. Goldreich, S. Goldwasser, S. Micali, *How to Construct Random Functions*][GGM1986].
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto
+
+open Probability Turing.MultiTapeTM
+open scoped NNReal ENNReal
+
+/-- A uniform symmetric message authentication code (MAC) on `n`-bit messages at security parameter
+`n`, with strict polynomial-time key generation and tag generation, deterministic polynomial-time
+verification, and perfect completeness on supported keys, `n`-bit messages, and tags
+[Boneh and Shoup, Definition 6.1][BonehShoup2023]. -/
+structure MACScheme where
+  /-- Sample a secret MAC key `sk` at unary security parameter `n`. -/
+  keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  /-- Compute a MAC tag on message `msg` using the secret key `sk`. -/
+  sign : List Bool → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  /-- Deterministically verify a candidate `tag` on `msg` under secret key `sk`. -/
+  verify : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → Bool
+  /-- Key generation is uniformly strict PPT in the unary security parameter. -/
+  keyGen_ppt : IsPPTOn encUnary encBits keyGen
+  /-- Tag generation is uniformly strict PPT in the encoded secret key and message. -/
+  sign_ppt : IsPPTOn (encPair encBits encBits) encBits (fun p => sign p.1 p.2)
+  /-- Verification is computable in plain polynomial time on `(sk, msg, tag)`. -/
+  verify_polyTime : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => verify p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool
+  /-- Every tag produced by `sign` on an `n`-bit message under a supported secret key at security
+  parameter `n` is accepted by `verify`. -/
+  verify_sign : ∀ n sk, sk ∈ (ProbComp.eval (keyGen n)).support →
+    ∀ msg, msg.length = n →
+    ∀ tag, tag ∈ (ProbComp.eval (sign sk msg)).support →
+    verify sk msg tag = true
+
+/-- The equivalent tidy verification certificate used internally by compositional proofs. -/
+private theorem MACScheme.verify_polyTime_tidy (M : MACScheme) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => M.verify p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool := by
+  simpa only [← computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime] using M.verify_polyTime
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_contains {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {list : γ → List (List Bool)} {elem : γ → List Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime list encIn (encList encBits))
+    (helem : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime elem encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).contains (elem a)) encIn encBool := by
+  have heq : (fun a => (list a).contains (elem a)) =
+      (fun a => (list a).any (fun x => elem a == x)) := by
+    funext a
+    rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff, List.contains_iff_mem, List.any_eq_true]
+    simp only [beq_iff_eq]
+    exact ⟨fun h => ⟨elem a, h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨_, h, heq⟩ => heq ▸ h⟩
+  rw [heq]
+  exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.anyWithInput (test := fun a x => elem a == x) hlist (by polytime)
+
+namespace MACScheme
+
+attribute [program_certificate] keyGen_ppt sign_ppt verify_polyTime
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem isPPTOn_keyGen_comp (M : MACScheme) {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {n : γ → ℕ} (hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime n encIn encUnary) :
+    IsPPTOn encIn encBits (fun a => M.keyGen (n a)) :=
+  M.keyGen_ppt.preprocess hn
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem isPPTOn_sign_comp (M : MACScheme) {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {sk msg : γ → List Bool}
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encBits)
+    (hmsg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime msg encIn encBits) :
+    IsPPTOn encIn encBits (fun a => M.sign (sk a) (msg a)) :=
+  M.sign_ppt.preprocess (hsk.prod hmsg)
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_verify_comp (M : MACScheme)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {sk msg tag : γ → List Bool}
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encBits)
+    (hmsg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime msg encIn encBits)
+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => M.verify (sk a) (msg a) (tag a)) encIn encBool :=
+  M.verify_polyTime.tidy.comp (hsk.prod (hmsg.prod htag))
+
+/-! ### Full adaptive chosen-message security (`EUFCMA`) -/
+
+/-- Stateful MAC tagging oracle that tags the requested message under `sk` and prepends the
+message to the list of queried messages. -/
+noncomputable def signingOracle (M : MACScheme) (sk : List Bool)
+    (request : Unit × List Bool) : StateT (List (List Bool)) ProbComp (List Bool) :=
+  fun queried => do
+    let tag ← M.sign sk request.2
+    return (tag, request.2 :: queried)
+
+/-- The MAC EUF-CMA experiment [Boneh and Shoup, Definition 6.2][BonehShoup2023]: sample
+`sk ← M.keyGen n`, run the adaptive forger on `(n, [])` with oracle access to
+`M.signingOracle sk`, and accept when the forger outputs a valid `(msg, tag)` pair on an `n`-bit
+message `msg` that was never queried to the tagging oracle. -/
+noncomputable def eufCmaGame (M : MACScheme) (adversary : Forger) (n : ℕ) :
+    ProbComp Bool := do
+  let sk ← M.keyGen n
+  let out ← (OracleComp.interpret
+    (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun k => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin k))
+      (M.signingOracle sk)) (adversary n [])).run []
+  return (out.1.1.length == n) && !out.2.contains out.1.1 &&
+    M.verify sk out.1.1 out.1.2
+
+/-- Run the complete MAC EUF-CMA experiment on its unary security parameter for any oracle-PPT
+forger. -/
+@[program_certificate]
+theorem isPPTOn_eufCmaGame (M : MACScheme) {adversary : Forger}
+    (hadversary : IsOraclePPT (encPair encBits encBits) adversary) :
+    IsPPTOn encUnary encBool (M.eufCmaGame adversary) := by
+  obtain ⟨c, d, hlen⟩ := M.sign_ppt.length_le
+  have hhandler : IsPPTOn
+      (encPair (encPair encUnary encBits)
+        (encPair (encPair (encFinite Unit) encBits) (encList encBits)))
+      (encPair encBits (encList encBits))
+      (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ((Unit × List Bool) × List (List Bool)) =>
+        M.signingOracle pair.1.2 pair.2.1 pair.2.2) := by
+    unfold signingOracle
+    ppt
+  have hrun : IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits)
+      (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) (encList encBits))
+      (fun caller : ℕ × List Bool =>
+        (OracleComp.interpret
+          (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun k => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin k))
+            (M.signingOracle caller.2)) (adversary caller.1 [])).run []) := by
+    apply hadversary.run_interpret_preprocess
+      (prepare := fun caller : ℕ × List Bool => (caller.1, ([] : List Bool)))
+      (initial := fun _ => ([] : List (List Bool)))
+      (resources := fun caller query =>
+        c * (2 * caller.2.length + query.length + 2) ^ d + 2 * query.length + 2)
+      (by fun_prop) hhandler (by fun_prop)
+      (fun _ _ => True) (fun _ => trivial) (by fun_prop)
+    intro caller request queried _ result hresult
+    simp only [signingOracle, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+      PMF.mem_support_bind_iff, PMF.mem_support_pure_iff] at hresult
+    obtain ⟨tag, htag, rfl⟩ := hresult
+    have htagLen := hlen (caller.2, request.2) tag htag
+    simp only [encBits_apply, length_encPair] at htagLen
+    refine ⟨trivial, by lia, ?_⟩
+    simp only [encList_cons, List.length_append, length_frame, encBits_apply]
+    lia
+  have hpost : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ((List Bool × List Bool) × List (List Bool)) =>
+        (pair.2.1.1.length == pair.1.1) && !pair.2.2.contains pair.2.1.1 &&
+          M.verify pair.1.2 pair.2.1.1 pair.2.1.2)
+      (encPair (encPair encUnary encBits)
+        (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) (encList encBits))) encBool := by
+    polytime
+  exact M.keyGen_ppt.bind_with (hrun.bind_with hpost.isPPTOn)
+
+/-- The MAC EUF-CMA experiment is uniformly strict PPT, independently of unused auxiliary input. -/
+@[program_certificate]
+theorem isPPT_eufCmaGame (M : MACScheme) {adversary : Forger}
+    (hadversary : IsOraclePPT (encPair encBits encBits) adversary) :
+    IsPPT encBool (fun n _ => M.eufCmaGame adversary n) :=
+  ((M.isPPTOn_eufCmaGame hadversary).preprocess (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst _ _)).isPPT
+
+/-- Existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (EUF-CMA) for a symmetric MAC
+against uniform strict oracle-PPT adversaries [Boneh and Shoup, Definition 6.2][BonehShoup2023]. -/

body:
`@[local fun_prop, program_certificate]` makes only the first attribute local. The `program_certificate` handler in `Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean` uses its global attribute kind for both `certificateExt.add` and `Attribute.add ... fun_prop`; `hasGlobalFunProp` deliberately ignores the local entry. Consequently these private tidy certificates still become global automation after importing the module.

Please make the program-certificate registrations local as well (or remove them from private helpers), preserving the public plain certificates. This occurs in both `CollisionResistant.lean` helpers and seven `MerkleDamgard.lean` helpers. Verify that ordinary importing clients retain the plain API without globally registering those private tidy rules. This applies Samuel’s plain-only global automation direction without changing the mathematical construction.

+/-!
+# The Merkle–Damgård transform
+
+Given a keyed `2n → n` collision-resistant compression family
+`h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, the Merkle–Damgård transform ([BonehShoup2023],
+Section 8.4, Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3) constructs a collision-resistant hash family on
+arbitrary-length messages by iterating `h k` over a sequence of `n`-bit blocks starting from a
+fixed `n`-bit initialization vector `0^n`.
+
+We formalize the transform and its collision-extraction reduction at two levels:
+
+1. **Block-chain level (`merkleDamgardChain`, `extractChainCollision`)**:
+   Iterating `h k` over a list of `n`-bit blocks produces an `n`-bit digest. Whenever two block
+   lists `bs₁` and `bs₂` of `n`-bit blocks produce the same final digest under `merkleDamgardChain`
+   and neither block list is a suffix of the other (`¬ (bs₁ <:+ bs₂) ∧ ¬ (bs₂ <:+ bs₁)`), scanning
+   the compression inputs backward from the final step (`extractChainCollision`) deterministically
+   finds a `2n`-bit collision `(x₁, x₂)` for `h k` in polynomial time. In particular, this covers
+   both cases of the classical length-strengthened Merkle–Damgård proof ([BonehShoup2023],
+   Theorem 8.3):
+   * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`: the final (length-encoding) blocks of
+     `bs₁` and `bs₂` differ;
+   * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: `bs₁` and `bs₂` have the same number of
+     blocks and `bs₁ ≠ bs₂`.
+   Consequently, any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding turns a `CompressionFamily` into a
+   collision-resistant hash family (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`).
+
+2. **Unrestricted bit-string level (`mdBlocks`, `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`)**:
+   Encoding an arbitrary bit string `msg : List Bool` as the initial marker block `0^n` followed by
+   one `n`-bit data block `1 ‖ b ‖ 0^{n-2}` per bit `b` of `msg` produces a suffix-free block
+   encoding of **all** bit strings for every `n ≥ 2`, with no upper bound on message length.
+   Iterating `h` over `mdBlocks k.length msg` yields
+   `merkleDamgard h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, which is collision-resistant on all
+   arbitrary-length bit strings (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+   `CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`).
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.padOrTake`: fixed-width bit-string normalization to exact length `n`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgardChain`: block-level iterated compression
+  `blocks.foldl (fun acc b => h k (acc ++ b)) iv`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.chainTraceStep`, `Cslib.Crypto.chainTrace`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.extractChainCollision`: polynomial-time backward scan extracting a `2n`-bit
+  compression collision from colliding block chains.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdEndBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdDataBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks`: suffix-free
+  `n`-bit block encoding of arbitrary bit strings.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgard`, `Cslib.Crypto.extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: domain-extended
+  keyed hash family and its deterministic collision extractor.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgardChain`, `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgard`: digest length
+  preservation.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_not_suffix`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: fundamental Merkle–Damgård chain
+  collision extraction lemmas.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`: collision resistance
+  for any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks_suffix_iff`: suffix-freeness of `mdBlocks n` for `n ≥ 2`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: deterministic collision extraction for
+  `merkleDamgard`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`: any `2n → n` collision-resistant
+  compression family yields an unrestricted collision-resistant hash family on `List Bool`.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+  Section 8.4 (Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3).
+* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020], Section 5.2.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-! ### Fixed-width normalization -/
+
+/-- Normalize a bit string to exact length `n` by right-padding with `false` or truncating.
+On words already of length `n`, this is the identity. -/
+def padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (w ++ List.replicate n false).take n
+
+@[simp]
+theorem length_padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : (padOrTake n w).length = n := by
+  simp only [padOrTake, List.length_take, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
+  omega
+
+@[simp]
+theorem padOrTake_eq_self {n : ℕ} {w : List Bool} (hw : w.length = n) :
+    padOrTake n w = w := by
+  subst hw
+  simp [padOrTake]
+
+@[local fun_prop, program_certificate]

+      (fun p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => M.verify p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool := by
+  simpa only [← computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime] using M.verify_polyTime
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_contains {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {list : γ → List (List Bool)} {elem : γ → List Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime list encIn (encList encBits))
+    (helem : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime elem encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).contains (elem a)) encIn encBool := by
+  have heq : (fun a => (list a).contains (elem a)) =
+      (fun a => (list a).any (fun x => elem a == x)) := by
+    funext a
+    rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff, List.contains_iff_mem, List.any_eq_true]
+    simp only [beq_iff_eq]
+    exact ⟨fun h => ⟨elem a, h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨_, h, heq⟩ => heq ▸ h⟩
+  rw [heq]
+  exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.anyWithInput (test := fun a x => elem a == x) hlist (by polytime)
+
+namespace MACScheme
+
+attribute [program_certificate] keyGen_ppt sign_ppt verify_polyTime
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem isPPTOn_keyGen_comp (M : MACScheme) {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {n : γ → ℕ} (hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime n encIn encUnary) :
+    IsPPTOn encIn encBits (fun a => M.keyGen (n a)) :=
+  M.keyGen_ppt.preprocess hn
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem isPPTOn_sign_comp (M : MACScheme) {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
+    {sk msg : γ → List Bool}
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encBits)
+    (hmsg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime msg encIn encBits) :
+    IsPPTOn encIn encBits (fun a => M.sign (sk a) (msg a)) :=
+  M.sign_ppt.preprocess (hsk.prod hmsg)
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_verify_comp (M : MACScheme)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {sk msg tag : γ → List Bool}
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encBits)
+    (hmsg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime msg encIn encBits)
+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => M.verify (sk a) (msg a) (tag a)) encIn encBool :=
+  M.verify_polyTime.tidy.comp (hsk.prod (hmsg.prod htag))
+
+/-! ### Full adaptive chosen-message security (`EUFCMA`) -/
+
+/-- Stateful MAC tagging oracle that tags the requested message under `sk` and prepends the
+message to the list of queried messages. -/
+noncomputable def signingOracle (M : MACScheme) (sk : List Bool)
+    (request : Unit × List Bool) : StateT (List (List Bool)) ProbComp (List Bool) :=
+  fun queried => do
+    let tag ← M.sign sk request.2
+    return (tag, request.2 :: queried)
+
+/-- The MAC EUF-CMA experiment [Boneh and Shoup, Definition 6.2][BonehShoup2023]: sample
+`sk ← M.keyGen n`, run the adaptive forger on `(n, [])` with oracle access to
+`M.signingOracle sk`, and accept when the forger outputs a valid `(msg, tag)` pair on an `n`-bit
+message `msg` that was never queried to the tagging oracle. -/
+noncomputable def eufCmaGame (M : MACScheme) (adversary : Forger) (n : ℕ) :
+    ProbComp Bool := do
+  let sk ← M.keyGen n
+  let out ← (OracleComp.interpret
+    (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun k => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin k))
+      (M.signingOracle sk)) (adversary n [])).run []
+  return (out.1.1.length == n) && !out.2.contains out.1.1 &&
+    M.verify sk out.1.1 out.1.2
+
+/-- Run the complete MAC EUF-CMA experiment on its unary security parameter for any oracle-PPT
+forger. -/
+@[program_certificate]
+theorem isPPTOn_eufCmaGame (M : MACScheme) {adversary : Forger}
+    (hadversary : IsOraclePPT (encPair encBits encBits) adversary) :
+    IsPPTOn encUnary encBool (M.eufCmaGame adversary) := by
+  obtain ⟨c, d, hlen⟩ := M.sign_ppt.length_le
+  have hhandler : IsPPTOn
+      (encPair (encPair encUnary encBits)
+        (encPair (encPair (encFinite Unit) encBits) (encList encBits)))
+      (encPair encBits (encList encBits))
+      (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ((Unit × List Bool) × List (List Bool)) =>
+        M.signingOracle pair.1.2 pair.2.1 pair.2.2) := by
+    unfold signingOracle
+    ppt
+  have hrun : IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits)
+      (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) (encList encBits))
+      (fun caller : ℕ × List Bool =>
+        (OracleComp.interpret
+          (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun k => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin k))
+            (M.signingOracle caller.2)) (adversary caller.1 [])).run []) := by
+    apply hadversary.run_interpret_preprocess
+      (prepare := fun caller : ℕ × List Bool => (caller.1, ([] : List Bool)))
+      (initial := fun _ => ([] : List (List Bool)))
+      (resources := fun caller query =>
+        c * (2 * caller.2.length + query.length + 2) ^ d + 2 * query.length + 2)
+      (by fun_prop) hhandler (by fun_prop)
+      (fun _ _ => True) (fun _ => trivial) (by fun_prop)
+    intro caller request queried _ result hresult
+    simp only [signingOracle, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+      PMF.mem_support_bind_iff, PMF.mem_support_pure_iff] at hresult
+    obtain ⟨tag, htag, rfl⟩ := hresult
+    have htagLen := hlen (caller.2, request.2) tag htag
+    simp only [encBits_apply, length_encPair] at htagLen
+    refine ⟨trivial, by lia, ?_⟩
+    simp only [encList_cons, List.length_append, length_frame, encBits_apply]
+    lia
+  have hpost : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ((List Bool × List Bool) × List (List Bool)) =>
+        (pair.2.1.1.length == pair.1.1) && !pair.2.2.contains pair.2.1.1 &&
+          M.verify pair.1.2 pair.2.1.1 pair.2.1.2)
+      (encPair (encPair encUnary encBits)
+        (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) (encList encBits))) encBool := by
+    polytime
+  exact M.keyGen_ppt.bind_with (hrun.bind_with hpost.isPPTOn)
+
+/-- The MAC EUF-CMA experiment is uniformly strict PPT, independently of unused auxiliary input. -/
+@[program_certificate]
+theorem isPPT_eufCmaGame (M : MACScheme) {adversary : Forger}
+    (hadversary : IsOraclePPT (encPair encBits encBits) adversary) :
+    IsPPT encBool (fun n _ => M.eufCmaGame adversary n) :=
+  ((M.isPPTOn_eufCmaGame hadversary).preprocess (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst _ _)).isPPT
+
+/-- Existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (EUF-CMA) for a symmetric MAC
+against uniform strict oracle-PPT adversaries [Boneh and Shoup, Definition 6.2][BonehShoup2023]. -/

@@ -0,0 +1,792 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.CollisionResistant
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.BitString
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+import Complexity.Tactic.PPT
+
+/-!
+# The Merkle–Damgård transform
+
+Given a keyed `2n → n` collision-resistant compression family
+`h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, the Merkle–Damgård transform ([BonehShoup2023],
+Section 8.4, Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3) constructs a collision-resistant hash family on
+arbitrary-length messages by iterating `h k` over a sequence of `n`-bit blocks starting from a
+fixed `n`-bit initialization vector `0^n`.
+
+We formalize the transform and its collision-extraction reduction at two levels:
+
+1. **Block-chain level (`merkleDamgardChain`, `extractChainCollision`)**:
+   Iterating `h k` over a list of `n`-bit blocks produces an `n`-bit digest. Whenever two block
+   lists `bs₁` and `bs₂` of `n`-bit blocks produce the same final digest under `merkleDamgardChain`
+   and neither block list is a suffix of the other (`¬ (bs₁ <:+ bs₂) ∧ ¬ (bs₂ <:+ bs₁)`), scanning
+   the compression inputs backward from the final step (`extractChainCollision`) deterministically
+   finds a `2n`-bit collision `(x₁, x₂)` for `h k` in polynomial time. In particular, this covers
+   both cases of the classical length-strengthened Merkle–Damgård proof ([BonehShoup2023],
+   Theorem 8.3):
+   * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`: the final (length-encoding) blocks of
+     `bs₁` and `bs₂` differ;
+   * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: `bs₁` and `bs₂` have the same number of
+     blocks and `bs₁ ≠ bs₂`.
+   Consequently, any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding turns a `CompressionFamily` into a
+   collision-resistant hash family (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`).
+
+2. **Unrestricted bit-string level (`mdBlocks`, `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`)**:
+   Encoding an arbitrary bit string `msg : List Bool` as the initial marker block `0^n` followed by
+   one `n`-bit data block `1 ‖ b ‖ 0^{n-2}` per bit `b` of `msg` produces a suffix-free block
+   encoding of **all** bit strings for every `n ≥ 2`, with no upper bound on message length.
+   Iterating `h` over `mdBlocks k.length msg` yields
+   `merkleDamgard h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, which is collision-resistant on all
+   arbitrary-length bit strings (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+   `CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`).
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.padOrTake`: fixed-width bit-string normalization to exact length `n`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgardChain`: block-level iterated compression
+  `blocks.foldl (fun acc b => h k (acc ++ b)) iv`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.chainTraceStep`, `Cslib.Crypto.chainTrace`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.extractChainCollision`: polynomial-time backward scan extracting a `2n`-bit
+  compression collision from colliding block chains.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdEndBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdDataBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks`: suffix-free
+  `n`-bit block encoding of arbitrary bit strings.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgard`, `Cslib.Crypto.extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: domain-extended
+  keyed hash family and its deterministic collision extractor.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgardChain`, `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgard`: digest length
+  preservation.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_not_suffix`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: fundamental Merkle–Damgård chain
+  collision extraction lemmas.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`: collision resistance
+  for any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks_suffix_iff`: suffix-freeness of `mdBlocks n` for `n ≥ 2`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: deterministic collision extraction for
+  `merkleDamgard`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`: any `2n → n` collision-resistant
+  compression family yields an unrestricted collision-resistant hash family on `List Bool`.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+  Section 8.4 (Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3).
+* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020], Section 5.2.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-! ### Fixed-width normalization -/
+
+/-- Normalize a bit string to exact length `n` by right-padding with `false` or truncating.
+On words already of length `n`, this is the identity. -/
+def padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (w ++ List.replicate n false).take n
+
+@[simp]
+theorem length_padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : (padOrTake n w).length = n := by
+  simp only [padOrTake, List.length_take, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
+  omega
+
+@[simp]
+theorem padOrTake_eq_self {n : ℕ} {w : List Bool} (hw : w.length = n) :
+    padOrTake n w = w := by
+  subst hw
+  simp [padOrTake]
+
+@[local fun_prop, program_certificate]

body: Fixed in 8b6b1d40. Every replacement is checked by `Planner.resolves`: the written form must denote exactly the target from its position, considering namespaces, `open`s, same-module private names and local binders, with `_root_.` as the last resort. A span that does not spell the referenced constant is never edited (`spells`; leading-dot spans included), and `rewrite` refuses `--no-build-check`. Regressions are in `ResolutionTests`; your `namespace A; open Turing.MultiTapeTM` case now yields `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`.
