+# --- Lean source helpers (unit-tested in scripts/test_tidy_sweep.py) ----------------------------
+
+OPENERS, CLOSERS = "([{⦃⟨‹", ")]}⦄⟩›"
+IDENT = re.compile(qr.IDENT.pattern)
+KEYWORDS = {"by", "fun", "λ", "with", "at", "using", "from", "then", "else", "do", "in", "if",
+            "match", "show", "have", "let", "calc", "only", "generalizing", "says", "where",
+            "deriving", "termination_by", "decreasing_by", "obtain", "rcases", "refine", "exact"}
+COMMAND_KEYWORD = re.compile(r"#?[A-Za-z_]+")
+NAME_ONLY_COMMANDS = {"#print", "#check", "#guard_msgs", "attribute", "open", "export", "#eval",
+                      "#reduce", "#synth", "add_decl_doc", "#lint", "#help"}
+LEMMA_LIST_TACTIC = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:simp|simp_all|dsimp|simp_rw|rw|rwa|rewrite|erw|nth_rewrite|nth_rw|simpa|fun_prop|"
+    r"aesop|norm_num|field_simp|grind|polytime|positivity|unfold|delta|gcongr|subst_vars|"
+    r"continuity|measurability|bound|decide|omega|linarith|nlinarith|exact\?|apply\?|"
+    r"rw_mod_cast|push_cast|norm_cast|simp_arith|conv)\b[^\[\]\n]*$")
+
+
+def match_bracket(mask: str, i: int, limit: int | None = None) -> int:
+    """The index of the bracket closing the one at `mask[i]`, or -1."""
+    depth, end = 0, len(mask) if limit is None else limit
+    for j in range(i, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+            if depth == 0:
+                return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def find_top_level(mask: str, start: int, end: int, token: str) -> int:
+    """The first `token` at bracket depth 0 in `mask[start:end]`, or -1. `:` excludes `:=`."""
+    depth = 0
+    for j in range(start, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+        elif depth == 0 and mask.startswith(token, j):
+            if token == ":" and (mask.startswith(":=", j) or mask.startswith("::", j)
+                                 or (j and mask[j - 1] == ":")):
+                continue
+            return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def line_indent(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    start = text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+    return len(text[start:]) - len(text[start:].lstrip(" "))
+
+
+def column(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    return offset - (text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1)
+
+
+def atom_end(mask: str, i: int, limit: int) -> int:
+    """The end of the atom (identifier, number, `?_`, bracket group, `.ident`) at `i` together
+    with directly attached projections (`.field`, `.1`), or `i` when no atom starts there."""
+    if i >= limit:
+        return i
+    char = mask[i]
+    if char in OPENERS:
+        end = match_bracket(mask, i, limit)
+        if end < 0:
+            return i
+        j = end + 1
+    elif char == "." and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char == "?" and mask.startswith("?_", i):
+        j = i + 2
+    elif char == "@" and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char.isdigit():
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and (mask[j].isalnum() or mask[j] == "."):
+            j += 1
+    else:
+        match = IDENT.match(mask, i)
+        if not match or match[0].rstrip(".") in KEYWORDS:
+            return i
+        j = match.end()
+    while j < limit and mask[j] == "." and j + 1 < limit and (
+            mask[j + 1].isdigit() or IDENT.match(mask, j + 1)):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, j + 1).end() if IDENT.match(mask, j + 1) else j + 2
+    return min(j, limit)
+
+
+NAMED_ARG = re.compile(r"\(\s*[^\W\d][\w'₀-₉]*\s*:=")
+
+
+def parse_args(mask: str, pos: int, limit: int, count: int, base_indent: int,
+               named: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    """Up to `count` positional application arguments after `pos`: atoms separated by blanks,
+    continuing onto lines indented more than `base_indent`. Named arguments `(x := e)` are
+    skipped and, when `named` is given, appended to it."""
+    args = []
+    i = pos
+    while len(args) < count and i < limit:
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and mask[j] in " \t":
+            j += 1
+        if j < limit and mask[j] == "\n":
+            k = j
+            while k < limit and mask[k] in " \t\n":
+                k += 1
+            if k >= limit or line_indent(mask, k) <= base_indent:
+                break
+            j = k
+        if j == i and args:
+            break  # no blank after the previous argument
+        end = atom_end(mask, j, limit)
+        if end == j:
+            break
+        if NAMED_ARG.match(mask, j):
+            if named is not None:
+                named.append((j, end))
+        else:
+            args.append((j, end))
+        i = end
+    return args
+
+
+def strip_space(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    while start < end and mask[start].isspace():
+        start += 1
+    while end > start and mask[end - 1].isspace():
+        end -= 1
+    return start, end
+
+
+def is_atomic_application(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    """For text `P args` in `mask[start:end]` made of atoms only, the span of `P`; else None."""
+    start, end = strip_space(mask, start, end)
+    head = atom_end(mask, start, end)
+    if head == start:
+        return None
+    args = parse_args(mask, head, end, 10 ** 6, -1)
+    last = args[-1][1] if args else head
+    return (start, head) if strip_space(mask, last, end)[0] == end else None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Binder:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    bracket: str
+    names: list[str]
+    type_start: int
+    type_end: int
+    default: bool
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DeclText:
+    start: int
+    sel_start: int
+    sel_end: int
+    end: int
+    binders: list[Binder]
+    colon: int  # the `:` before the type, or -1
+    assign: int  # the `:=` before the body, or -1
+    problems: list[str]
+
+
+def parse_decl(mask: str, start: int, sel_start: int, sel_end: int, end: int) -> DeclText:
+    """Binders, type and body of the declaration whose name ends at `sel_end`."""
+    assign = find_top_level(mask, sel_end, end, ":=")
+    stop = assign if assign >= 0 else end
+    binders, problems, colon = [], [], -1
+    i = sel_end
+    if mask.startswith(".{", i):
+        i = match_bracket(mask, i + 1, stop) + 1
+    while i < stop:
+        char = mask[i]
+        if char.isspace():
+            i += 1
+        elif char in "([{⦃":
+            close = match_bracket(mask, i, stop)
+            if close < 0:
+                problems.append("unbalanced binder")
+                break
+            inner = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":")
+            default = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":=")
+            if inner < 0:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:close].split(), close
+            else:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:inner].split(), inner + 1
+            type_end = default if default >= 0 else close
+            binders.append(Binder(i, close + 1, char, names, type_start, type_end,
+                                  default >= 0))
+            i = close + 1
+        elif char == ":":
+            colon = i
+            break
+        else:
+            problems.append("binder without brackets")
+            break
+    if assign < 0:
+        problems.append("no `:=` (pattern-matching definition)")
+    return DeclText(start, sel_start, sel_end, end, binders, colon, assign, problems)
+
+
+def proof_parts(text: str, assign: int, end: int) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    """The text after `:=` and whether it is a tactic block."""
+    body = text[assign + 2:end]
+    return body, re.match(r"\s*by(?:\s|$)", body) is not None
+
+
+def collapse(text: str) -> str:
+    return " ".join(text.split())
+
+
+# --- Scopes and names ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+SCOPE_COMMAND = re.compile(
+    r"^(?P<mods>(?:@\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:public|private|noncomputable|protected|meta)\s+)*)"
+    r"(?P<kw>namespace|section|end|open|mutual|variable|export)\b", re.M)
+NOTATION_COMMAND = re.compile(
+    r"(?:@\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*)*(?:(?:local|scoped|private|public|meta)\s+)*"
+    r"(?:notation3?|infixl?|infixr|prefix|postfix|syntax|macro|elab|binder_predicate)\b")
+STRING_LITERAL = re.compile(r'"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*)"')
+
+
+def notation_tokens(text: str, mask: str) -> set[str]:
+    """The tokens the notation, syntax and macro commands of a source declare: the string
+    literals of each whole command, across continuation lines."""
+    starts = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(mask)] + [len(mask)]
+    tokens = set()
+    for start, end in zip(starts, starts[1:]):
+        if NOTATION_COMMAND.match(mask, start):
+            tokens.update(t.strip() for t in STRING_LITERAL.findall(text, start, end))
+    return tokens - {""}
+
+
+def token_capture(written: str, following: str, tokens) -> str | None:
+    """A token that Lean's tokenizer reads instead of the identifier `written` followed by
+    `following`: a token wins over an identifier at least as short as it. `tokens` maps first
+    characters to tokens."""
+    text = written + following
+    lexeme = IDENT.match(text)
+    length = lexeme.end() if lexeme else len(written)
+    for token in tokens.get(written[:1], ()):
+        if len(token) >= length and text.startswith(token):
+            return token
+    return None
+
+
+def by_first(tokens) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+    out: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for token in tokens:
+        out[token[:1]].append(token)
+    return out
+
+
+def namespaces_of(names) -> set[str]:
+    """Every name and every proper prefix of a name, as namespaces."""
+    out = set()
+    for name in names:
+        parts = name.split(".")
+        for i in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+            out.add(".".join(parts[:i]))
+    return out
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Open:
+    """An opened namespace: all of it, only the names `only` (`open N (x y)`), or all but the
+    names `hiding`."""
+    namespace: str
+    only: frozenset[str] | None = None
+    hiding: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scope:
+    namespace: str
+    opens: tuple[Open, ...] = ()
+    aliases: frozenset[str] = frozenset()  # short names from `open … renaming` and `export`
+    variables: frozenset[str] = frozenset()  # names bound by `variable` commands
+
+
+def binder_names(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    """The names bound by the top-level binder groups of a `variable` command (masked)."""
+    names, i = set(), 0
+    while i < len(text):
+        if text[i] in "([{⦃":
+            close = match_bracket(text, i)
+            if close < 0:
+                break
+            inner = text[i + 1:close]
+            colon = find_top_level(inner, 0, len(inner), ":")
+            if colon >= 0:
+                names.update(inner[:colon].split())
+            elif text[i] != "[":
+                names.update(inner.split())
+            i = close + 1
+        else:
+            i += 1
+    return {n for n in names if IDENT.fullmatch(n) and n != "_"}
+
+
+class Scopes:
+    """The namespace, opened namespaces, aliases and section variables at each offset of a
+    masked source, and the tokens its notations, syntax and macros declare."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mask: str, namespaces: set[str], text: str | None = None):
+        self.points: list[tuple[int, Scope]] = [(0, Scope(""))]
+        self.once: list[tuple[int, int, tuple[Open, ...], frozenset[str]]] = []
+        # frames: [kind, name, opens, aliases, variables]
+        stack: list[list] = [["file", "", [], set(), set()]]
+        starts = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(mask)] + [len(mask)]
+        self.tokens = by_first(notation_tokens(text if text is not None else mask, mask))
+
+        def namespace() -> str:
+            return ".".join(f[1] for f in stack if f[0] == "namespace" and f[1])
+
+        def resolve(word: str, earlier: list[Open]) -> list[str]:
+            ns = namespace()
+            parts = ns.split(".") if ns else []
+            prefixes = [".".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1)]
+            prefixes += [o.namespace for f in stack for o in f[2]]
+            prefixes += [o.namespace for o in earlier]
+            found = [p + "." + word if p else word for p in prefixes
+                     if (p + "." + word if p else word) in namespaces]
+            return list(dict.fromkeys(found)) or [word]
+
+        for match in SCOPE_COMMAND.finditer(mask):
+            kw = match["kw"]
+            end = next((x for x in starts if x > match.start()), len(mask))
+            rest = mask[match.end():end]
+            words = rest.split()
+            if kw == "namespace" and words:
+                stack.append(["namespace", words[0], [], set(), set()])
+            elif kw in ("section", "mutual"):
+                stack.append([kw, words[0] if words and kw == "section" else "", [], set(),
+                              set()])
+            elif kw == "end":
+                if len(stack) > 1:
+                    stack.pop()
+            elif kw == "variable":
+                stack[-1][4].update(binder_names(rest))
+            elif kw in ("open", "export"):
+                one_shot = bool(words) and words[-1] == "in"
+                body = " ".join(words[:-1] if one_shot else words)
+                opens, aliases = self.parse_open(body, resolve, kw == "export")
+                if one_shot:
+                    following = next((x for x in starts if x > end), len(mask))
+                    self.once.append((match.start(), following, tuple(opens),
+                                      frozenset(aliases)))
+                    continue
+                stack[-1][2].extend(opens)
+                stack[-1][3].update(aliases)
+            self.points.append((match.end(), Scope(
+                namespace(), tuple(o for f in stack for o in f[2]),
+                frozenset().union(*(f[3] for f in stack)),
+                frozenset().union(*(f[4] for f in stack)))))
+        self.offsets = [point for point, _ in self.points]
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def parse_open(body: str, resolve, export: bool) -> tuple[list[Open], set[str]]:
+        """The namespaces an `open` (or `export`) command makes visible, and the short names it
+        introduces as aliases. `open scoped` opens no names."""
+        words = body.replace("(", " ( ").replace(")", " ) ").replace(",", " ").split()
+        if not words or words[0] == "scoped":
+            return [], set()
+        if words[0] == "private":
+            words = words[1:]
+        if "renaming" in words:
+            pairs = words[words.index("renaming") + 1:]
+            return [], {pairs[i + 2] for i in range(len(pairs) - 2) if pairs[i + 1] == "→"}
+        if "hiding" in words:
+            k = words.index("hiding")
+            return [Open(ns, hiding=frozenset(words[k + 1:]))
+                    for w in words[:k] for ns in resolve(w, [])], set()
+        if "(" in words:
+            k = words.index("(")
+            names = frozenset(w for w in words[k + 1:] if w != ")")
+            opens = [Open(ns, only=names) for w in words[:k] for ns in resolve(w, [])]
+            return ([] if export else opens), (set(names) if export else set())
+        opens: list[Open] = []
+        for w in words:  # a later name may be relative to an earlier one
+            opens += [Open(ns) for ns in resolve(w, opens)]
+        return opens, set()
+
+    def at(self, offset: int) -> Scope:
+        i = bisect.bisect_right(self.offsets, offset) - 1
+        scope = self.points[i][1] if i >= 0 else Scope("")
+        for start, end, opens, aliases in self.once:
+            if start <= offset < end:
+                scope = Scope(scope.namespace, scope.opens + opens, scope.aliases | aliases,
+                              scope.variables)
+        return scope
+
+    def chain(self, offset: int) -> list[str]:
+        """The enclosing namespaces, innermost first, ending with the root `""`."""
+        ns = self.at(offset).namespace
+        parts = ns.split(".") if ns else []
+        return [".".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1)]
+
+    def prefixes(self, offset: int) -> list[str]:
+        """Namespaces a written name may be relative to, innermost first (`""` is the root);
+        selective opens count as whole ones (an over-approximation)."""
+        return self.chain(offset) + [o.namespace for o in self.at(offset).opens]
+
+
+def written_name(target: str, prefixes: list[str], known: set[str]) -> str:
+    """The shortest suffix of `target` that resolves to it, and to nothing else, from a position
+    whose namespace prefixes and opened namespaces are `prefixes`."""
+    parts = target.split(".")
+    for k in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+        suffix = ".".join(parts[-k:])
+        hits = {p + "." + suffix if p else suffix for p in prefixes}
+        resolved = {h for h in hits if h in known or h == target}
+        if resolved == {target}:
+            return suffix
+    return target
+
+
+def renamed_token(token: str, old: str, new: str) -> str | None:
+    """`token` (a written form of `old`) with the renamed part, when the written prefix still
+    resolves the same way (`old = P.token` and `new = P.result`); otherwise None."""
+    at = "@" if token.startswith("@") else ""
+    bare = token[len(at):]
+    root = "_root_." if bare.startswith("_root_.") else ""
+    bare = bare[len(root):]
+    if not (old == bare or old.endswith("." + bare)):
+        return None
+    prefix = old[:len(old) - len(bare)]
+    if not new.startswith(prefix):
+        return None
+    result = new[len(prefix):]
+    if not result or (prefix and result.startswith(".")):
+        return None
+    return at + root + result
+
+
+# --- Edits --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Replace:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    text: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Wrap:
+    """Text inserted before `open` and after `close`; `site` orders wraps with equal spans (the
+    wrap of the site that starts first is outermost)."""
+    open: int
+    close: int
+    before: str
+    after: str
+    site: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Region:
+    """A span whose edited text is then transformed by `build`."""
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    build: object
+    decl: str
+
+
+def render(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap], lo: int, hi: int) -> str:
+    """`text[lo:hi]` with the replacements and wraps inside it applied. At one position, wraps
+    close (innermost first) before others open (outermost first), then a replacement starts."""
+    reps = sorted((r for r in replaces if lo <= r.start and r.end <= hi),
+                  key=lambda r: (r.start, r.end))
+    ws = [w for w in wraps if lo <= w.open and w.close <= hi]
+    points = sorted({r.start for r in reps} | {w.open for w in ws} | {w.close for w in ws})
+    starting = defaultdict(list)
+    for r in reps:
+        starting[r.start].append(r)
+    out, cur = [], lo
+    for p in points:
+        if p < cur:
+            continue  # inside a replaced span
+        out.append(text[cur:p])
+        out += [w.after for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.close == p),
+                                        key=lambda w: (-w.open, -w.site))]
+        out += [w.before for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.open == p),
+                                         key=lambda w: (-w.close, w.site))]
+        cur = p
+        for r in starting.get(p, []):
+            out.append(r.text)
+            cur = max(cur, r.end)
+    out.append(text[cur:hi])
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def apply_edits(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap],
+                regions: list[Region]) -> str:
+    out, cur = [], 0
+    for region in sorted(regions, key=lambda r: r.start):
+        out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, region.start))
+        out.append(region.build(render(text, replaces, wraps, region.start, region.end)))
+        cur = region.end
+    out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, len(text)))
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Round trips --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+OF_TIDY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.'])(?:(?:[\w.']*\.)?Computable(?:In(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|"
+                     r"FPTTime))\.|\.)of_tidy\b")
+DOT_ROUND_TRIP = re.compile(r"\.tidy\.computableIn(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|FPTTime)\b")
+
+
+def cancel_round_trips(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """Remove `of_tidy (x.tidy)`, `of_tidy <| x.tidy` and `x.tidy.computableIn…` round trips,
+    where `x` is an atom. Returns the new text and the number of removals."""
+    count = 0
+    while True:
+        mask = masks(text)[1]
+        change = None
+        for match in DOT_ROUND_TRIP.finditer(mask):
+            change = (match.start(), match.end(), "")
+            break
+        if change is None:
+            for match in OF_TIDY.finditer(mask):
+                i = match.end()
+                while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                    i += 1
+                pipe = mask.startswith("<|", i)
+                if pipe:
+                    i += 2
+                    while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                        i += 1
+                end = atom_end(mask, i, len(mask))
+                if end == i:
+                    continue
+                inner = (i, end)
+                if mask[i] == "(" and match_bracket(mask, i) == end - 1:
+                    inner = strip_space(mask, i + 1, end - 1)
+                start, stop = inner
+                if not mask[start:stop].endswith(".tidy") or atom_end(mask, start, stop) != stop:
+                    continue
+                core_end = stop - len(".tidy")
+                if atom_end(mask, start, core_end) != core_end:
+                    continue
+                if pipe:
+                    after = end
+                    while after < len(mask) and mask[after] in " \t":
+                        after += 1
+                    if after < len(mask) and mask[after] not in CLOSERS + "\n,":
+                        continue
+                change = (match.start(), end, text[start:core_end])
+                break
+        if change is None:
+            return text, count
+        start, end, new = change
+        new_mask = masks(new)[1]
+        if (start > 0 and text[start - 1] == "(" and end < len(text) and text[end] == ")"
+                and atom_end(new_mask, 0, len(new)) == len(new) and not new.startswith("@")):
+            start, end = start - 1, end + 1
+        text = text[:start] + new + text[end:]
+        count += 1
+
+
+# --- Wrapping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Hyp:
+    names: list[str]
+    old_type: str  # one line
+    simple: bool
+
+
+def reindent(lines: list[str], delta: int) -> list[str] | None:
+    """Shift lines by `delta` columns; None when that would remove non-blank text."""
+    out = []
+    for line in lines:
+        if not line.strip():
+            out.append("")
+        elif delta >= 0:
+            out.append(" " * delta + line)
+        elif len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" ")) >= -delta:
+            out.append(line[-delta:])
+        else:
+            return None
+    return out
+
+
+def wrap_proof(body: str, body_column: int, decl_indent: int, hyps: list[Hyp],
+               conclusion: str | None, simple_conclusion: bool, iffs: str) -> str | None:
+    """The new text after `:=` for a proof `body` of the old (tidy) statement, now stated plainly:
+    tidy hypotheses are recovered, and the old conclusion converted. `body_column` is the column
+    of the first character of `body`. None when the layout cannot be preserved."""
+    stripped = body.lstrip()
+    lead = body[:len(body) - len(stripped)]
+    first_col = body_column + len(lead) if "\n" not in lead else len(lead.rsplit("\n", 1)[1])
+    stripped = stripped.rstrip()
+    tactic = re.match(r"by(?=\s|$)", stripped) is not None
+    if not hyps and simple_conclusion and not tactic:
+        return f"{lead}.of_tidy ({stripped})"
+    k = decl_indent + 2
+    rebind = []
+    for hyp in hyps:
+        for name in hyp.names:
+            rebind.append(f"have {name} := {name}.tidy" if hyp.simple else
+                          f"have {name} : {hyp.old_type} := by simpa only [{iffs}] using {name}")
+    if tactic:
+        rest = stripped[2:]
+        if rest.lstrip(" \t").startswith("\n") or not rest.strip():
+            lines = rest.lstrip(" \t")[1:].split("\n")
+            nonblank = [ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()]
+            if not nonblank:
+                return None
+            k = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        else:
+            first_line, _, tail = rest.lstrip(" \t").partition("\n")
+            tactic_col = first_col + 2 + (len(rest) - len(rest.lstrip(" \t")))
+            shifted = reindent(tail.split("\n"), k - tactic_col) if tail else []
+            if shifted is None:
+                return None
+            lines = [" " * k + first_line] + shifted
+        pad = " " * k
+        out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+        if conclusion is None:
+            out += lines
+        elif simple_conclusion:
+            out += [pad + "refine .of_tidy ?_"] + lines
+        else:
+            inner = reindent(lines, 2)
+            out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} := by"] + inner + \
+                [pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+        return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+    first, _, tail = stripped.partition("\n")
+    tail_lines = tail.split("\n") if tail else []
+    nonblank = [ln for ln in tail_lines if ln.strip()]
+    shift = 0
+    if nonblank:
+        least = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        shift = max(0, k + 2 - least)
+    tail_lines = reindent(tail_lines, shift) or tail_lines
+    pad = " " * k
+    out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+    term = "\n".join([first] + tail_lines)
+    if conclusion is None:
+        out.append(pad + "exact " + term)
+    elif simple_conclusion:
+        out.append(pad + "exact .of_tidy (" + term + ")")
+    else:
+        out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} :=", pad + "  " + term,
+                pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+    return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Planning -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Manual:
+    path: str
+    line: int
+    decl: str
+    kind: str
+    detail: str = ""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Ref:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    decl: str | None
+
+
+class SourceFile:
+    def __init__(self, path: Path, namespaces: set[str]):
+        self.path = path
+        self.text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.code, self.mask = masks(self.text) if path.suffix == ".lean" else (self.text,) * 2
+        self.lines = self.text.split("\n")
+        self.starts = [0]
+        for line in self.lines:
+            self.starts.append(self.starts[-1] + len(line) + 1)
+        self.commands = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(self.mask)]
+        self._namespaces = namespaces
+        self._scopes: Scopes | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def scopes(self) -> Scopes:
+        if self._scopes is None:
+            self._scopes = Scopes(self.mask, self._namespaces, self.text)
+        return self._scopes
+
+    def at(self, line: int, column16: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 0-based line and UTF-16 column (`.ilean` positions)."""
+        return self.starts[line] + qr.utf16_index(self.lines[line], column16)
+
+    def at_range(self, line: int, column: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 1-based line and code-point column (declaration ranges)."""
+        return self.starts[line - 1] + column
+
+    def line_of(self, offset: int) -> int:
+        """The 1-based line of an offset."""
+        return self.text.count("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+
+    def command_keyword(self, offset: int) -> str:
+        starts = [s for s in self.commands if s <= offset]
+        if not starts:
+            return ""
+        match = COMMAND_KEYWORD.match(self.mask, starts[-1])
+        return match[0] if match else ""
+
+    def comment_spans(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+        if self.path.suffix != ".lean":
+            return [(0, len(self.text))]
+        spans, i = [], 0
+        while i < len(self.text):
+            if self.code[i] != self.text[i]:
+                j = i
+                while j < len(self.text) and self.code[j] != self.text[j] or (
+                        j < len(self.text) and self.text[j] == "\n" and j + 1 < len(self.text)
+                        and self.code[j + 1] != self.text[j + 1]):
+                    j += 1
+                spans.append((i, j))
+                i = j
+            else:
+                i += 1
+        return spans
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileEdits:
+    replaces: list[Replace] = field(default_factory=list)
+    wraps: list[Wrap] = field(default_factory=list)
+    regions: list[Region] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class Planner:
+    """The edits of one area's batch: case 2 declarations restated and renamed, the references
+    to them converted, and case 1 twins used in proofs that become plain.
+
+    No edit is made at a span whose text does not spell the referenced constant, and a
+    replacement is written only when it resolves to its intended target, and nothing else, from
+    its position. A declaration with a reference that cannot be converted completely is deferred
+    (left tidy), so that skipped references stay unchanged."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model: Model, entries: list[Entry], twins: dict[str, str], area: str,
+                 force_wrap: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+                 bridge: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset()):
+        self.model, self.area, self.force_wrap = model, area, force_wrap
+        self.bridge = bridge
+        self.entries = {e.name: e for e in entries}
+        self.batch = {e.name: e for e in entries if e.area == area and e.case == "2"}
+        self.twins = {o: p for o, p in twins.items() if p in model.constants}
+        self.privates = private_by_module(model.constants)
+        self.known = model.known | {e.target for e in self.batch.values()}
+        self.namespaces = namespaces_of(self.known)
+        self.sources: dict[Path, SourceFile] = {}
+        self.deferred: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        self._refs: dict[str, list[Ref]] = {}
+        self._locals: dict[tuple[str, int, int], set[str]] = {}
+        self._decl_spans: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
+        self.tokens = by_first(model.tokens)
+        self.reset()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Forget the edits of a planning pass."""
+        self.renames = {n: e.target for n, e in self.batch.items() if n not in self.deferred}
+        self.files: dict[Path, FileEdits] = defaultdict(FileEdits)
+        self.manual: list[Manual] = []
+        self.decls: dict[str, dict] = {}
+        self.spans: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.needs: dict[str, dict[str, bool]] = defaultdict(dict)
+        self.sites: Counter = Counter()
+        self.twin_refs: Counter = Counter()
+        self.imports: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
+        self.blockers: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.bridged: list[str] = []
+        self.round_trips = 0
+
+    # Sources and references.
+
+    def source(self, path: Path) -> SourceFile:
+        if path not in self.sources:
+            self.sources[path] = SourceFile(path, self.namespaces)
+        return self.sources[path]
+
+    def refs(self, module: str) -> list[Ref]:
+        if module not in self._refs:
+            src = self.source(qr.source_path(module))
+            out = []
+            for name, _, info in self.model.lib.references(module):
+                for u in info["usages"]:
+                    out.append(Ref(name, src.at(u[0], u[1]), src.at(u[2], u[3]),
+                                   u[4] if len(u) == 5 else None))
+            self._refs[module] = sorted(out, key=lambda x: x.start)
+        return self._refs[module]
+
+    def ref_kind(self, name: str) -> str:
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return "pred"
+        if owner in self.renames:
+            return "renamed"
+        if name in self.twins:
+            return "twin"
+        if name in BRIDGES:
+            return "bridge"
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        if const.get("tidy") or const.get("tb") or is_tidy_constant(name):
+            return "tidy"
+        return "plain"
+
+    def new_name(self, name: str) -> str:
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return BY_TIDY[name].plain
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if owner in self.renames and (name == owner or name.startswith(owner + ".")):
+            return self.renames[owner] + name[len(owner):]
+        return self.twins.get(name, name)
+
+    def note(self, path: Path, offset: int, decl: str | None, kind: str, detail: str = ""):
+        src = self.source(path)
+        self.manual.append(Manual(str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), src.line_of(offset), decl or "",
+                                  kind, detail))
+
+    def where(self, path: Path, offset: int) -> str:
+        return f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{self.source(path).line_of(offset)}"
+
+    def need(self, module: str, constant: str, public: bool) -> None:
+        defining = self.model.constants.get(constant, {}).get("m")
+        if defining and defining != module:
+            self.needs[module][defining] = self.needs[module].get(defining, False) or public
+
+    def notions_of(self, name: str) -> list[Notion]:
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        return [BY_TIDY[t] for t in const.get("tidy", []) if t in BY_TIDY]
+
+    # Names.
+
+    def local_names(self, module: str, src: SourceFile, offset: int) -> set[str]:
+        """Identifiers of the declaration (or command) around `offset` that are not references
+        to constants: binders, local hypotheses, tactic names. A written name whose first
+        component is one of them could be captured by a local."""
+        if module not in self._decl_spans:
+            ranges = self.model.lib.ileans.get(module, {}).get("decls", {}).values()
+            self._decl_spans[module] = [(src.at(r[0], r[1]), src.at(r[2], r[3]))
+                                        for r in ranges]
+        span = next(((a, b) for a, b in self._decl_spans[module] if a <= offset < b), None)
+        if span is None:
+            starts = src.commands + [len(src.mask)]
+            start = max([s for s in starts if s <= offset], default=0)
+            span = (start, min(s for s in starts if s > offset) if offset < len(src.mask)
+                    else len(src.mask))
+        key = (module, *span)
+        if key not in self._locals:
+            refs = [(x.start, x.end) for x in self.refs(module)
+                    if span[0] <= x.start < span[1]]
+            names = set()
+            for match in IDENT.finditer(src.mask, *span):
+                if not any(a <= match.start() < b for a, b in refs):
+                    names.add(match[0].split(".")[0])
+            self._locals[key] = names - KEYWORDS
+        return self._locals[key]
+
+    def resolves(self, module: str, src: SourceFile, offset: int, written: str,
+                 following: str = "") -> set[str]:
+        """Everything `written` (without `@`, followed by `following`) might denote at
+        `offset`, over-approximated: constants reached through the enclosing namespaces and
+        every opened namespace (selective and hiding opens counted whole), private constants of
+        the module, `"<local>"` when its first component is a local binder, a section variable
+        or an alias from `open … renaming` or `export`, and `"<token>"` when the tokenizer would
+        read a notation, syntax or macro token there instead (from the import closure, scoped
+        ones included, or from the module's own commands). Names come from the whole import
+        closure, not only the referenced ones."""
+        privates = self.privates.get(module, set())
+
+        def exists(name: str) -> bool:
+            return name in self.known or name in privates
+        if written.startswith("_root_."):

+import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Action.Defs
+import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Enumerative.DoubleCounting
+import Mathlib.Tactic.GCongr
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
+
+/-!
+# Counting partial assignments and random restrictions
+
+Over a finite index type `ι`, the partial assignments extending `ρ₀` with exactly `ℓ` free
+coordinates number `(m choose ℓ) 2 ^ (m - ℓ)` for the `m` free coordinates of `ρ₀`
+(`PartialAssignment.card_extensions`), so `(|ι| choose ℓ) 2 ^ (|ι| - ℓ)` partial assignments leave
+exactly `ℓ` coordinates free (`PartialAssignment.card_withFree`). Drawing such a partial assignment
+uniformly is drawing a set of `ℓ` free coordinates and a word for the others
+(`PartialAssignment.sum_card_filter_outside`), and double counting relates partial assignments
+with different numbers of free coordinates (`PartialAssignment.sum_card_filter_extensions`,
+`PartialAssignment.sum_extensions_update`); these are the random restrictions of Subbotovskaya's
+method and Håstad's switching lemma.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.extensions`: the extensions of `ρ₀` leaving `ℓ` coordinates
+  free.
+* `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.withFree`: the partial assignments leaving `ℓ` coordinates
+  free.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.card_extensions`,
+  `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.card_withFree`,
+  `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.card_filter_extensions_free_subset`,
+  `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.card_extensions_le_two_mul_card_filter_forall_nonempty`:
+  counting partial assignments by their free coordinates and union-bounding block survival.
+* `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.sum_card_filter_outside`,
+  `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.sum_card_filter_extensions`,
+  `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.sum_extensions_update`,
+  `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.mul_card_extensions_sub_one`: drawing random restrictions and
+  double counting extensions.
+* `Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment.mul_card_filter_withFree_le`: two stages of restrictions,
+  counted.
+
+## References
+
+* [S. Jukna, *Boolean Function Complexity: Advances and Frontiers*][Jukna2012]
+* [J. Håstad, *Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits*][Hastad1986]
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.BitString.PartialAssignment
+
+open Function Finset
+
+variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ρ : PartialAssignment ι}

@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Interactive.Security
+import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+
+/-!
+# Interactive reductions in the plain model
+
+In the plain model neither party has oracles, and a run is an ordinary probabilistic program.
+`Interactive.plainLaw` is the law of a prover-side program, and
+`Interactive.World.plain_eval_execute` computes the law of a whole execution from the law of the
+prover's run. The main result is that round-by-round soundness implies soundness with the sum of
+the per-round errors (`Interactive.Verifier.RbrSound.sound`), against arbitrary prover strategies.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Interactive.plainLaw`: the law of a program without oracles.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Interactive.World.plain_eval_execute`: the law of an execution in the plain model.
+* `Interactive.Verifier.RbrSound.sound`: round-by-round soundness implies soundness.
+
+## References
+
+* [R. Canetti, Y. Chen, J. Holmgren, A. Lombardi, G. N. Rothblum, R. D. Rothblum, D. Wichs,
+  *Fiat–Shamir: from practice to theory*][CanettiCHLRRW2019]
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Interactive
+
+open scoped ENNReal
+open Spec
+
+/-- The law of a program without external oracles: its private coins are fair. -/
+noncomputable def plainLaw {α : Type} (p : ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty α) : PMF α :=
+  OracleComp.interpret (ProbOracleComp.handler ProbComp.unifOracle fun e => e.elim) p
+
+/-- The law of a joint program in the plain model. -/
+private noncomputable def runLaw {α : Type}
+    (p : ProbOracleComp (OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ OracleSpec.empty) α) : PMF α :=
+  OracleComp.interpret (ProbOracleComp.handler ProbComp.unifOracle
+    (OracleComp.sumHandler (fun e => e.elim) fun e => e.elim)) p
+
+private theorem plain_eval {α : Type}
+    (p : ProbOracleComp (OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ OracleSpec.empty) α) :
+    World.plain.eval p = runLaw p := by
+  have h := OracleComp.run_interpret_stateless (m := PMF) (State := Unit)
+    (ProbOracleComp.handler ProbComp.unifOracle
+      (OracleComp.sumHandler (fun e => e.elim) fun e => e.elim)) p ()
+  have hh : (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun n => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifOracle n))
+      World.plain.impl) =
+      fun q s => (fun a => (a, s)) <$> ProbOracleComp.handler ProbComp.unifOracle
+        (OracleComp.sumHandler (fun e => e.elim) fun e => e.elim) q := by
+    funext q s
+    rcases q with n | e | e
+    · rfl
+    · exact e.elim
+    · exact e.elim
+  unfold World.eval ProbOracleComp.runWith
+  erw [hh, h]
+  exact (PMF.map_comp _ _ _).trans (PMF.map_id _)
+
+private theorem runLaw_liftProver {α : Type} (p : ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty α) :
+    runLaw (liftProver (oV := OracleSpec.empty) p) = plainLaw p := by
+  rw [runLaw, liftProver, OracleComp.interpret_interpret, plainLaw]
+  congr 1
+  funext q
+  rcases q with n | e
+  · simp [ProbOracleComp.handler]
+  · exact e.elim
+
+
+/-- A returned value has a point law. -/
+@[simp] theorem plainLaw_pure {α : Type} (a : α) :
+    plainLaw (pure a : ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty α) = PMF.pure a := rfl
+
+/-- Sequencing is `PMF.bind`. -/
+@[simp] theorem plainLaw_bind {α β : Type} (p : ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty α)
+    (f : α → ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty β) :
+    plainLaw (p >>= f) = (plainLaw p).bind fun a => plainLaw (f a) :=
+  OracleComp.interpret_bind _ _ _
+
+/-- Postprocessing is `PMF.map`. -/
+@[simp] theorem plainLaw_map {α β : Type} (f : α → β) (p : ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty α) :
+    plainLaw (f <$> p) = (plainLaw p).map f :=
+  OracleComp.interpret_map _ _ _
+
+/-- Embedded sampling has the law of the sampled program. -/
+@[simp] theorem plainLaw_sample {α : Type} (p : ProbComp α) :
+    plainLaw (ProbOracleComp.sample (spec := OracleSpec.empty) p) = ProbComp.eval p :=
+  ProbOracleComp.interpret_sample _ _ _
+
+private theorem runLaw_pure {α : Type} (a : α) :
+    runLaw (pure a : ProbOracleComp (OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ OracleSpec.empty) α) = PMF.pure a := rfl
+
+private theorem runLaw_bind {α β : Type}
+    (p : ProbOracleComp (OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ OracleSpec.empty) α)
+    (f : α → ProbOracleComp (OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ OracleSpec.empty) β) :
+    runLaw (p >>= f) = (runLaw p).bind fun a => runLaw (f a) :=
+  OracleComp.interpret_bind _ _ _
+
+private theorem runLaw_map {α β : Type} (f : α → β)
+    (p : ProbOracleComp (OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ OracleSpec.empty) α) :
+    runLaw (f <$> p) = (runLaw p).map f :=
+  OracleComp.interpret_map _ _ _
+
+/-- A program whose queries are answered deterministically has a point law. -/
+private theorem interpret_pure_handler {ι : Type} {spec : OracleSpec ι} {α : Type}
+    (f : (q : ι) → spec q) (p : OracleComp spec α) :
+    OracleComp.interpret (m := PMF) (fun q => PMF.pure (f q)) p =
+      PMF.pure (OracleComp.interpret (m := Id) f p) := by
+  induction p using PFunctor.FreeM.induction with
+  | pure a => rfl
+  | lift_bind q cont ih =>
+    rw [show (PFunctor.FreeM.lift q).bind cont = OracleComp.query q >>= cont from rfl,
+      OracleComp.interpret_bind, OracleComp.interpret_bind, OracleComp.interpret_query,
+      OracleComp.interpret_query]
+    simp only [Probability.PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind, PMF.pure_bind]
+    exact ih (f q)
+
+private theorem runLaw_output {s : Spec} {StmtIn StmtOut : Type}
+    (V : Verifier OracleSpec.empty s StmtIn StmtOut)
+    (x : StmtIn) (τ : Transcript s) :
+    runLaw (V.output (oP := OracleSpec.empty) x τ) = PMF.pure (V.outputOn x τ) := by
+  rw [runLaw, Verifier.output, OracleComp.interpret_interpret, Verifier.outputOn]
+  rw [← interpret_pure_handler]
+  congr 1
+  funext q
+  rcases q with e | q
+  · exact e.elim
+  · rfl
+
+private theorem toOuterMeasure_bind_le {α β : Type} (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β) (t : Set β)
+    {K : ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∀ a, (f a).toOuterMeasure t ≤ K) : (p.bind f).toOuterMeasure t ≤ K := by
+  rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_apply]
+  exact Probability.PMF.tsum_mul_le_of_forall_le _ h
+
+private theorem toOuterMeasure_bind_pure {α β : Type} (p : PMF α) (g : α → β) (t : Set β) :
+    (p.bind fun a => PMF.pure (g a)).toOuterMeasure t = p.toOuterMeasure (g ⁻¹' t) := by
+  rw [← PMF.toOuterMeasure_map_apply]
+  rfl
+
+/-- **The law of an execution in the plain model**: run the prover's strategy against the
+challenge samplers, then apply the verifier's decision to the transcript. -/
+theorem World.plain_eval_execute {s : Spec} {StmtIn StmtOut α : Type}
+    (V : Verifier OracleSpec.empty s StmtIn StmtOut) (x : StmtIn)
+    (P : ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty (ProverStrategy (ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty) s α)) :
+    World.plain.eval (V.execute (oP := OracleSpec.empty) x P) =
+      (plainLaw (P >>= runStrategy s V.samplers)).map fun r => (r.1, V.outputOn x r.1, r.2) := by
+  rw [plain_eval]
+  simp only [Verifier.execute, runLaw_bind, runLaw_liftProver, runLaw_output, runLaw_pure,
+    PMF.pure_bind, plainLaw_bind, PMF.map_bind]
+  rfl
+
+/-- From a doomed prefix, the rest of a run wins with probability at most the remaining errors. -/
+private theorem rbrFrom_le : ∀ (s : Spec) (smp : PerChallenge ProbComp s)
+    (ε : PerChallenge (fun _ => ℝ≥0∞) s) (S : Prefix s → Prop) (wins : Transcript s → Prop),
+    RbrFrom s smp ε S wins → ¬ S (Prefix.empty s) →
+    ∀ {α : Type} (st : ProverStrategy (ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty) s α),
+      (plainLaw (runStrategy s smp st)).toOuterMeasure {r | wins r.1} ≤ PerChallenge.sum s ε
+  | [], _, _, _, wins, h, hS, _, st => by
+    have hw : ¬ wins () := h hS
+    simp [runStrategy, hw]
+  | .prover M I :: s, smp, ε, S, wins, h, hS, _, st => by
+    simp only [runStrategy, plainLaw_bind]
+    refine toOuterMeasure_bind_le _ _ _ fun p => ?_
+    rcases p with ⟨msg, st'⟩
+    simp only [plainLaw_pure]
+    rw [toOuterMeasure_bind_pure]
+    exact rbrFrom_le s smp ε (fun p => S (some (msg, p))) (fun τ => wins (msg, τ)) (h.2 msg)
+      (h.1 hS msg) st'
+  | .verifier C :: s, smp, ε, S, wins, h, hS, _, st => by
+    simp only [runStrategy, plainLaw_bind, plainLaw_sample]
+    rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_apply]
+    set A : Set C := {c | S (some (c, Prefix.empty s))}
+    have hinner : ∀ c, ((plainLaw (st c)).bind fun st' => (plainLaw (runStrategy s smp.2 st')).bind
+        fun r => plainLaw (pure ((c, r.1), r.2))).toOuterMeasure {r | wins r.1} ≤
+        A.indicator 1 c + PerChallenge.sum s ε.2 := by
+      intro c
+      by_cases hc : c ∈ A
+      · refine le_trans ?_ le_self_add
+        rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hc]
+        exact Probability.PMF.toOuterMeasure_le_one _ _

This file imports the old hub, and the complete fresh-main overlay through Sequential has no path to Uniform. @@ -0,0 +1,332 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Interactive.Sequential
+import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
+public import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Degrees
+public import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Eval.Defs
+
+/-!
+# The sumcheck protocol with a final evaluation check
+
+The index is a polynomial `P` in `n` variables over a finite field `F` with every individual
+degree at most `d`. A claim `(r, c)` at round `i` consists of the challenges `r : Fin i → F` of
+the earlier rounds and a value `c`. It states that the sum of `P` over the Boolean hypercube in
+the coordinates `i, …, n - 1`, with the coordinates below `i` fixed to `r`, is `c`
+(`Sumcheck.rel P i`). At round `0` this is the sumcheck claim `∑_{b ∈ {0,1}ⁿ} P b = c`, and at
+round `n` it is the evaluation claim `P r = c`.
+
+This is the protocol of Lund, Fortnow, Karloff and Nisan [LundFortnowKarloffNisan1992] as a
+composition of one-round reductions, with each challenge uniform on the field. Each round needs
+`i < n`: past the last variable the honest round polynomial is constant, and the round is neither
+complete nor round-by-round sound. The TQBF protocol in
+`Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.IP.TQBF.Protocol` is a separate, unchanged
+development.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Sumcheck.Claim F i`: the claims of round `i`, a point of `F^i` and a value.
+* `Sumcheck.partialSum P r`: the sum of `P` over the Boolean hypercube in the coordinates from
+  `i` on, with the coordinates below `i` fixed to `r : Fin i → F`.
+* `Sumcheck.round d P i` reduces `rel P i` to `rel P (i + 1)` in one prover message (a univariate
+  polynomial) and one uniform challenge `z`, and appends `z` to the point.
+* `Sumcheck.finalCheck P` reduces `rel P n` to acceptance by evaluating `P` without interaction.
+* `Sumcheck.proof d P` is `round 0`, …, `round (n - 1)`, by `Reduction.iterate`, followed by
+  `finalCheck`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Sumcheck.round_complete`, `Sumcheck.round_rbrSound`: each round is perfectly complete and
+  round-by-round sound with error `d / |F|`.
+* `Sumcheck.finalCheck_complete`, `Sumcheck.finalCheck_rbrSound`: the final check is perfectly
+  complete and round-by-round sound without error.
+* `Sumcheck.proof_complete`, `Sumcheck.proof_sound`: the end-to-end theorems, corollaries of the
+  component theorems through the composition theorems. The soundness error `n * (d / |F|)` is the
+  sum of the per-round errors, and no step of the composed protocol is reasoned about directly.
+
+## References
+
+* [C. Lund, L. Fortnow, H. Karloff, N. Nisan, *Algebraic methods for interactive proof
+  systems*][LundFortnowKarloffNisan1992]
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Interactive.Sumcheck
+
+open scoped ENNReal
+open Spec
+
+variable {F : Type} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] {n : ℕ} (d : ℕ)
+  (P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F)
+
+/-- A claim of round `i`: the challenges of the rounds before `i` and the claimed value. -/
+abbrev Claim (F : Type) (i : ℕ) : Type := (Fin i → F) × F
+
+/-- The point of `F^n` equal to `r` on the first `i` coordinates and to the Boolean point `b` on
+the others. -/
+def point {i : ℕ} (r : Fin i → F) (b : Fin (n - i) → Bool) : Fin n → F :=
+  fun j => if h : j.val < i then r ⟨j.val, h⟩ else if b ⟨j.val - i, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0
+
+/-- The sum of `P` over the Boolean hypercube in the coordinates from `i` on, with the coordinates
+below `i` fixed to `r`. -/
+noncomputable def partialSum {i : ℕ} (r : Fin i → F) : F :=
+  ∑ b : Fin (n - i) → Bool, MvPolynomial.eval (point r b) P
+
+/-- The relation of round `i`: the claimed value is the partial sum. There is no witness. -/
+def rel (i : ℕ) : Claim F i → Unit → Prop := fun c _ => partialSum P c.1 = c.2
+
+/-- The honest message of round `i`: the partial sum as a polynomial in coordinate `i`. -/
+noncomputable def roundPoly {i : ℕ} (r : Fin i → F) : Polynomial F :=
+  ∑ b : Fin (n - (i + 1)) → Bool,
+    MvPolynomial.aeval (fun j => if h : j.val < i then Polynomial.C (r ⟨j.val, h⟩)
+      else if h' : j.val = i then Polynomial.X
+      else Polynomial.C (if b ⟨j.val - (i + 1), by omega⟩ then 1 else 0)) P
+
+/-- One round: the prover sends a polynomial, read in full; the verifier sends a field element. -/
+abbrev roundSpec (F : Type) [Semiring F] : Spec :=
+  [.prover (Polynomial F) (OracleInterface.full _), .verifier F]
+
+/-- The verifier's test of a round polynomial `g` against the claimed value `c`. -/
+abbrev accepts (c : F) (g : Polynomial F) : Prop := g.natDegree ≤ d ∧ g.eval 0 + g.eval 1 = c
+
+/-- Round `i` of sumcheck: on the claim `(r, c)` and the challenge `z`, the new claim is
+`(Fin.snoc r z, g.eval z)` for the prover's polynomial `g`. -/
+noncomputable def round (i : ℕ) :
+    Reduction OracleSpec.empty OracleSpec.empty (roundSpec F) (Claim F i) Unit (Claim F (i + 1))
+      Unit where
+  prover x _ :=
+    let g := roundPoly P x.1
+    pure (show ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty
+        (Polynomial F × (F → ProbOracleComp OracleSpec.empty _)) from
+      pure (g, fun z => pure ((Fin.snoc x.1 z, g.eval z), ())))
+  verifier :=
+    { samplers := (ProbComp.uniform F, ())
+      decide := fun x c => do
+        let g ← OracleComp.query (spec := OracleSpec.empty ⊕ₒ msgSpec (roundSpec F))
+          (.inr (.inl ()))
+        return if accepts d x.2 g then some (Fin.snoc x.1 c.1, g.eval c.1) else none }
+
+/-- The final check: evaluate `P` at the claimed point, without interaction. -/
+noncomputable def finalCheck :
+    Reduction OracleSpec.empty OracleSpec.empty [] (Claim F n) Unit Unit Unit where
+  prover _ _ := pure ((), ())
+  verifier :=
+    { samplers := ()
+      decide := fun x _ => pure (if MvPolynomial.eval x.1 P = x.2 then some () else none) }
+
+/-- **Sumcheck followed by the final check**: a proof system for the claim `∑_{b ∈ {0,1}ⁿ} P b = c`
+(`rel P 0`). -/
+noncomputable def proof :
+    Reduction OracleSpec.empty OracleSpec.empty (iterSpec (fun _ => roundSpec F) n ++ [])
+      (Claim F 0) Unit Unit Unit :=
+  (Reduction.iterate (s := fun _ => roundSpec F) (S := Claim F) (W := fun _ => Unit)
+    (round d P) n).append (finalCheck P)
+
+/-! ### The round polynomial -/
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- Substituting the variable at coordinate `k` and constants elsewhere gives a polynomial of
+degree at most the degree of `P` in `k`. -/
+private theorem natDegree_aeval_le (k : Fin n) (φ : Fin n → Polynomial F)
+    (hφ : ∀ j, j ≠ k → (φ j).natDegree = 0) (hk : (φ k).natDegree ≤ 1) :
+    (MvPolynomial.aeval φ P).natDegree ≤ P.degreeOf k := by
+  conv_lhs => rw [P.as_sum, map_sum]
+  refine Polynomial.natDegree_sum_le_of_forall_le _ _ fun m hm => ?_
+  rw [MvPolynomial.aeval_monomial, Polynomial.algebraMap_eq]
+  refine (Polynomial.natDegree_C_mul_le _ _).trans ?_
+  refine (Polynomial.natDegree_prod_le _ _).trans ?_
+  refine le_trans ?_ (MvPolynomial.monomial_le_degreeOf k hm)
+  calc ∑ j ∈ m.support, ((φ j) ^ m j).natDegree
+      ≤ ∑ j ∈ m.support, if k = j then m j else 0 := by
+        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => Polynomial.natDegree_pow_le.trans ?_
+        by_cases hj : k = j
+        · subst hj
+          simpa only [ite_true, mul_one] using Nat.mul_le_mul_left (m k) hk
+        · rw [hφ j (Ne.symm hj), mul_zero]
+          exact Nat.zero_le _
+    _ ≤ m k := by
+        rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq]
+        split_ifs <;> simp
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- The round polynomial has degree at most `d`. -/
+private theorem natDegree_roundPoly_le (hP : ∀ j, P.degreeOf j ≤ d) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < n)
+    (r : Fin i → F) : (roundPoly P r).natDegree ≤ d := by
+  refine Polynomial.natDegree_sum_le_of_forall_le _ _ fun b _ => ?_
+  refine (natDegree_aeval_le P ⟨i, hi⟩ _ (fun j hj => ?_) ?_).trans (hP _)
+  · have : j.val ≠ i := fun h => hj (Fin.ext h)
+    split_ifs <;> exact Polynomial.natDegree_C _
+  · simp
+
+omit [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- The coordinate `j < i + 1` of `Fin.snoc r z`. -/
+private theorem snoc_mk {i : ℕ} (r : Fin i → F) (z : F) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < i + 1) :
+    (Fin.snoc r z : Fin (i + 1) → F) ⟨j, hj⟩ = if h : j < i then r ⟨j, h⟩ else z :=
+  rfl
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- The round polynomial at `z` is the partial sum of the next round at the point extended
+by `z`. -/
+private theorem eval_roundPoly_eq {i : ℕ} (r : Fin i → F) (z : F) :
+    (roundPoly P r).eval z = partialSum P (Fin.snoc r z) := by
+  rw [roundPoly, Polynomial.eval_finsetSum, partialSum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
+  rw [← Polynomial.coe_aeval_eq_eval, MvPolynomial.comp_aeval_apply,
+    MvPolynomial.aeval_eq_eval]
+  congr 2
+  funext j
+  simp only [point, snoc_mk]
+  split_ifs <;> first | omega | simp
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- Split a Boolean point of length `m + 1` into its first coordinate and the others. -/
+private theorem sum_bool_succ {k m : ℕ} (h : k = m + 1) (f : (Fin k → Bool) → F) :
+    ∑ b, f b = ∑ c : Bool, ∑ b' : Fin m → Bool,
+      f (fun j => if h0 : j.val = 0 then c else b' ⟨j.val - 1, by omega⟩) := by
+  subst h
+  rw [← (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Bool).sum_comp, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+  refine Fintype.sum_congr _ _ fun c => Fintype.sum_congr _ _ fun b' => congrArg f ?_
+  funext j
+  refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun j => ?_) j <;> simp
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- Fixing coordinate `i` to the Boolean value `c` is reading `c` as the first of the Boolean
+coordinates of round `i`. -/
+private theorem point_snoc {i : ℕ} (r : Fin i → F) (c : Bool) (b : Fin (n - (i + 1)) → Bool) :
+    point (Fin.snoc r (if c then (1 : F) else 0)) b =
+      point r (fun j => if h0 : j.val = 0 then c else b ⟨j.val - 1, by omega⟩) := by
+  funext j
+  simp only [point, snoc_mk]
+  split_ifs <;> first | omega | simp_all [Nat.sub_sub]
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- The verifier's test passes on the honest round polynomial: its values at `0` and `1` sum to
+the partial sum. -/
+private theorem roundPoly_eval_zero_add_one {i : ℕ} (hi : i < n) (r : Fin i → F) :
+    (roundPoly P r).eval 0 + (roundPoly P r).eval 1 = partialSum P r := by
+  rw [eval_roundPoly_eq, eval_roundPoly_eq, add_comm]
+  conv_rhs => rw [partialSum, sum_bool_succ (show n - i = n - (i + 1) + 1 by omega),
+    Fintype.sum_bool]
+  congr 1
+  · exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => congrArg (MvPolynomial.eval · P) (point_snoc r true b)
+  · exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => congrArg (MvPolynomial.eval · P) (point_snoc r false b)
+
+omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
+/-- At round `n` all coordinates are fixed: the partial sum is the evaluation. -/
+theorem partialSum_self (r : Fin n → F) : partialSum P r = MvPolynomial.eval r P := by
+  rw [partialSum, Finset.sum_eq_single (fun _ => false)]
+  · exact congrArg (MvPolynomial.eval · P) (funext fun j => dite_eq_left j.isLt)
+  · exact fun b _ hb => absurd (funext fun j => absurd j.isLt (by omega)) hb
+  · exact fun h => absurd (Finset.mem_univ _) h
+
+/-- The verifier of round `i` outputs the claim at the challenge if it accepts the message. -/
+private theorem round_outputOn (i : ℕ) (x : Claim F i) (τ : Transcript (roundSpec F)) :
+    (round d P i).verifier.outputOn x τ =
+      if accepts d x.2 τ.1 then some (Fin.snoc x.1 τ.2.1, τ.1.eval τ.2.1) else none :=
+  rfl
+
+/-! ### Component theorems (milestone 2) -/
+
+/-- Each round is perfectly complete. -/
+theorem round_complete (hP : ∀ j, P.degreeOf j ≤ d) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < n) :
+    (round d P i).Complete World.plain (rel P i) (rel P (i + 1)) 0 := by
+  intro x w hxw
+  rw [Reduction.run, World.plain_eval_execute, PMF.toOuterMeasure_map_apply]
+  simp only [round, runStrategy, plainLaw_bind, plainLaw_pure, plainLaw_sample, PMF.pure_bind,
+    PMF.bind_bind]
+  have hacc : accepts d x.2 (roundPoly P x.1) :=
+    ⟨natDegree_roundPoly_le d P hP hi x.1, (roundPoly_eval_zero_add_one P hi x.1).trans hxw⟩
+  rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_apply]
+  refine Probability.PMF.tsum_mul_le_of_forall_le _ fun z => le_of_eq ?_
+  refine (PMF.toOuterMeasure_pure_apply _ _).trans (ite_eq_right fun h => h ⟨?_, ?_⟩)
+  · exact (round_outputOn d P i x _).trans (ite_eq_left hacc)
+  · exact (eval_roundPoly_eq P x.1 z).symm
+
+/-- Each round is round-by-round sound with error `d / |F|` (Schwartz–Zippel for one variable). -/
+theorem round_rbrSound (hP : ∀ j, P.degreeOf j ≤ d) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < n) :
+    (round d P i).verifier.RbrSound (language (rel P i)) (language (rel P (i + 1)))
+      ((d : ℝ≥0∞) / Fintype.card F, ()) := by
+  refine ⟨fun x p => match p with
+    | none => partialSum P x.1 = x.2
+    | some (g, none) => accepts d x.2 g ∧ g = roundPoly P x.1
+    | some (g, some (z, _)) => accepts d x.2 g ∧ g.eval z = (roundPoly P x.1).eval z,
+    fun x hx h => hx ⟨(), h⟩, fun x => ⟨?_, fun g => ⟨?_, fun z => ?_⟩⟩⟩
+  · rintro hS m ⟨hacc, rfl⟩
+    exact hS ((roundPoly_eval_zero_add_one P hi x.1).symm.trans hacc.2)
+  · intro hS
+    change (ProbComp.eval (ProbComp.uniform F)).toOuterMeasure
+      {c | accepts d x.2 g ∧ g.eval c = (roundPoly P x.1).eval c} ≤ (d : ℝ≥0∞) / Fintype.card F
+    by_cases hacc : accepts d x.2 g
+    · have hne : g - roundPoly P x.1 ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr fun h => hS ⟨hacc, h⟩
+      classical
+      rw [ProbComp.eval_uniform, Probability.PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFintype, div_eq_mul_inv]

Resolve against published target mappings or otherwise verify the actual destinations before pruning; remap moved declarations and provide a valid fallback for unavailable ones. body:
[P2] Distinguish the old local-only inventory before treating it as published data

The previous head writes `external-doc-targets.json` with these same `pages`/`anchors` keys, but they describe locally generated dependencies. This branch accepts that file as published authority and never fetches the official index. In an isolated repro using the actual old `trim_output()`, followed by this head's `trim_output()` and `check_output()` on the same tree, `published_fetch_calls` is 0, the legacy file is unchanged, and `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Defs.html#Matrix.ofArray` remains accepted even though the supplied public inventory places it in `Matrix/Array.html`.

Use a distinct filename or marker for published inventories and regenerate/reject the legacy local-only cache once. Add an old-trim → new-checker regression so this case cannot silently certify the broken link. A clear rebuild error is sufficient if the old pruned tree cannot be repaired; no broader cache policy is needed.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
[P2] Preserve universe polymorphism of the existing deterministic API

This shared context changed from `{α β γ : Type*}` to `{α β γ : Type}`. Consequently the pre-existing `PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`, reflexivity, composition and related deterministic interfaces now accept only `Type 0`. A generic `universe u; example {α : Type u} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (X : PromiseProblem α) : PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible enc enc X X := .refl enc X` passes against the prior module and fails against this exact head with `PromiseProblem.{u}` versus `PromiseProblem.{0}`.

Retain the original `Type*` context for existing deterministic declarations and localize the `Type` restriction to new PPT-dependent declarations. This does not require generalizing the PPT framework.
