 @[expose] public section
 
 namespace Cslib.Complexity
 
-open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM Probability PromiseProblem
+
+/-! ### Promise-BPP, promise-RP and promise-coRP -/
 
 namespace PromiseProblem
 
-variable {α β γ : Type*} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool}
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+  {Q : PromiseProblem α} {A : Set α}
+
+/-- `V` solves the promise problem `Q` with bounded error, using random strings whose length is `p`
+evaluated at the length of the encoded instance: for every yes-instance at least two thirds of the
+random strings are accepted, and for every no-instance at least two thirds are rejected
+[Goldreich, Definition 1.2][Goldreich2006]. Nothing is required on instances outside the
+promise. -/
+def SolvesWithBoundedError (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (Q : PromiseProblem α) : Prop :=
+  (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+    3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+      V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).card) ∧
+  ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+    3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+      V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card
+
+/-- `V` solves the promise problem `Q` with one-sided error, using random strings whose length is
+`p` evaluated at the length of the encoded instance: for every yes-instance at least half of the
+random strings are accepted, and for every no-instance none is
+[Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]. Nothing is required on instances outside the promise. -/
+def SolvesWithOneSidedError (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (Q : PromiseProblem α) : Prop :=
+  (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+    2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+      V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).card) ∧
+  ∀ a ∈ Q.no, ∀ r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (a, List.ofFn r) = false
+
+@[simp]
+theorem solvesWithBoundedError_ofSet_iff :
+    (ofSet A).SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V ↔ DecidesWithBoundedError enc p V A := by
+  simp only [SolvesWithBoundedError, DecidesWithBoundedError, yes_ofSet, no_ofSet,
+    Set.mem_compl_iff]
+  exact ⟨fun h a => ⟨h.1 a, h.2 a⟩, fun h => ⟨fun a => (h a).1, fun a => (h a).2⟩⟩
+
+@[simp]
+theorem solvesWithOneSidedError_ofSet_iff :
+    (ofSet A).SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V ↔ DecidesWithOneSidedError enc p V A := by
+  simp only [SolvesWithOneSidedError, DecidesWithOneSidedError, yes_ofSet, no_ofSet,
+    Set.mem_compl_iff]
+  exact ⟨fun h a => ⟨h.1 a, h.2 a⟩, fun h => ⟨fun a => (h a).1, fun a => (h a).2⟩⟩
+
+/-- Negating the verifier solves the complement promise problem with bounded error. -/
+theorem SolvesWithBoundedError.compl (h : Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V) :
+    Qᶜ.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p (fun x => !V x) := by
+  refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+  · simpa using h.2 a ha
+  · simpa using h.1 a ha
+
+/-- A one-sided-error solver for a promise problem is a polynomial-time verifier on the promise. -/
+theorem SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate (h : Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V) :
+    (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ V (a, w) = true) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval (enc a).length → V (a, w) = false := by
+  refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha w hw => ?_⟩
+  · have hpos := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := p.eval (enc a).length)
+    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ : (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+        V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).Nonempty := by
+      rw [← Finset.card_pos]
+      have := h.1 a ha
+      omega
+    exact ⟨List.ofFn r, List.length_ofFn, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hr).2⟩
+  · have hno := h.2 a ha fun i => w[i.val]'(by omega)
+    rwa [show (List.ofFn fun i : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) => w[i.val]'(by omega)) = w from
+      List.ext_getElem (by simp [hw]) fun i _ _ => by simp] at hno
+
+end PromiseProblem
+
+section PromiseProbabilistic
+
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {Q : PromiseProblem α} {A : Set α}
+
+/-- The promise problems solved with bounded error by polynomial-time algorithms reading
+polynomially long random strings, with respect to the encoding `enc` of instances
+[Goldreich, Definition 1.2][Goldreich2006]. -/
+def PromiseBPP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (PromiseProblem α) :=
+  {Q | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V}
+
+/-- The promise problems solved with one-sided error (no false positives on no-instances) by
+polynomial-time algorithms reading polynomially long random strings
+[Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]. -/
+def PromiseRP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (PromiseProblem α) :=
+  {Q | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V}
+
+/-- The promise problems solved with one-sided error (no false negatives on yes-instances) by
+polynomial-time algorithms reading polynomially long random strings: those whose complements are
+in `PromiseRP` [Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]. -/
+def PromiseCoRP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (PromiseProblem α) :=
+  {Q | Qᶜ ∈ PromiseRP enc}
+
+theorem mem_PromiseBPP_iff : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+private theorem mem_PromiseBPP_iff_tidy : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V := by
+  simp only [mem_PromiseBPP_iff, computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime]
+
+theorem mem_PromiseRP_iff : Q ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+private theorem mem_PromiseRP_iff_tidy : Q ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V := by
+  simp only [mem_PromiseRP_iff, computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime]
+
+/-- A promise problem is in `PromiseCoRP` when a polynomial-time verifier accepts every random
+string on every yes-instance and rejects at least half on every no-instance. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseCoRP_iff : Q ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, ∀ r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (a, List.ofFn r) = true) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+        2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+          V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨p, fun x => !V x, .of_tidy (by have := hV.tidy; fun_prop),
+      fun a ha r => by simp [hno a ha r], fun a ha => by simpa using hyes a ha⟩
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨p, fun x => !V x, .of_tidy (by have := hV.tidy; fun_prop),
+      fun a ha => by simpa using hno a ha, fun a ha r => by simp [hyes a ha r]⟩
+
+@[simp]
+theorem ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP : ofSet A ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔ A ∈ BPP enc := by
+  simp only [PromiseBPP, BPP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, solvesWithBoundedError_ofSet_iff]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem ofSet_mem_PromiseRP : ofSet A ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔ A ∈ RP enc := by
+  simp only [PromiseRP, RP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, solvesWithOneSidedError_ofSet_iff]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem ofSet_mem_PromiseCoRP : ofSet A ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔ A ∈ coRP enc := by
+  rw [PromiseCoRP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, ← ofSet_compl, ofSet_mem_PromiseRP, mem_coRP]
+
+/-- Every promise problem separated by a language in `BPP` is in `PromiseBPP`. -/
+theorem promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP : promiseClass (BPP enc) ⊆ PromiseBPP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨B, ⟨p, V, hV, hB⟩, hyes, hno⟩
+  exact ⟨p, V, hV, fun a ha => (hB a).1 (hyes ha),
+    fun a ha => (hB a).2 (Set.disjoint_right.1 hno ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every promise problem separated by a language in `RP` is in `PromiseRP`. -/
+theorem promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP : promiseClass (RP enc) ⊆ PromiseRP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨B, ⟨p, V, hV, hB⟩, hyes, hno⟩
+  exact ⟨p, V, hV, fun a ha => (hB a).1 (hyes ha),
+    fun a ha => (hB a).2 (Set.disjoint_right.1 hno ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every promise problem separated by a language in `coRP` is in `PromiseCoRP`. -/
+theorem promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP : promiseClass (coRP enc) ⊆ PromiseCoRP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨B, hB, hyes, hno⟩
+  exact promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP ⟨Bᶜ, hB,
+    Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_left.2 hno, Set.disjoint_compl_left_iff_subset.2 hyes⟩
+
+/-- `PromiseBPP` is closed under complement. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PromiseBPP (hQ : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc) : Qᶜ ∈ PromiseBPP enc :=
+  let ⟨p, V, hV, h⟩ := hQ
+  ⟨p, fun x => !V x, by have := hV.tidy; exact .of_tidy (by fun_prop), h.compl⟩
+
+/-- A promise problem's complement is in `PromiseRP` exactly when the problem is in
+`PromiseCoRP`. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PromiseRP_iff : Qᶜ ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔ Q ∈ PromiseCoRP enc :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A promise problem's complement is in `PromiseCoRP` exactly when the problem is in
+`PromiseRP`. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PromiseCoRP_iff : Qᶜ ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔ Q ∈ PromiseRP enc := by
+  rw [← compl_mem_PromiseRP_iff, compl_compl]
+
+theorem PromiseP_subset_PromiseRP : PromiseP enc ⊆ PromiseRP enc :=
+  (promiseClass_mono P_subset_RP).trans promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP
+
+theorem PromiseP_subset_PromiseCoRP : PromiseP enc ⊆ PromiseCoRP enc :=
+  (promiseClass_mono P_subset_coRP).trans promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP
+
+theorem PromiseP_subset_PromiseBPP : PromiseP enc ⊆ PromiseBPP enc :=
+  (promiseClass_mono P_subset_BPP).trans promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP
+
+theorem PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP : PromiseRP enc ⊆ PromiseNP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨p, V, hV, h⟩
+  exact mem_PromiseNP_iff.2 ⟨p, V, hV.tidy, h.exists_certificate⟩
+
+/-- A counted verifier's uniform rejection probability is its rejected fraction of all words. -/
+private theorem uniformList_rejectCount_toReal (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map (fun word => V (a, word))) false).toReal =
+      ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin n → Bool => V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card : ℝ) /
+        2 ^ n := by
+  rw [BitString.uniformList_map_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- Converting a polynomial-time seeded verifier into a uniform strict PPT Boolean program. -/
+private theorem isPPTOn_sampleList_verifier {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    IsPPTOn enc encBool (fun a => (fun w => V (a, w)) <$>
+      BitString.sampleList (p.eval (enc a).length)) :=
+  have hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p).comp
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encoding_length enc)
+  hcount.sampleList.map_with hV
+
+/-- **Probabilistic-program characterization of `PromiseBPP`**: a promise problem is in
+`PromiseBPP` exactly when a uniform strict PPT Boolean program accepts every yes-instance with
+probability at least `2 / 3` and rejects every no-instance with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔
+    ∃ M : α → ProbComp Bool, IsPPTOn enc encBool M ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 2 / 3 ≤ Pr[M a]) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 2 / 3 ≤ (ProbComp.eval (M a) false).toReal := by
+  rw [mem_PromiseBPP_iff_tidy]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => (fun w => V (a, w)) <$> BitString.sampleList (p.eval (enc a).length),
+      isPPTOn_sampleList_verifier hV, fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [uniformList_acceptCount_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+          3 * (acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hyes a ha
+      linarith
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [uniformList_rejectCount_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+          3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+            V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hno a ha
+      linarith
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    obtain ⟨c, d, evalM, hevalM, hlaw⟩ := hM.exists_seeded_evaluator
+    refine ⟨Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d, fun x => evalM x.1 x.2, hevalM,
+      fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (enc a).length =
+          c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+      rw [hp]
+      have hprob := hyes a ha
+      rw [hlaw a, uniformList_acceptCount_toReal (V := fun x => evalM x.1 x.2),
+        le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+      have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+          3 * (acceptCount (fun x => evalM x.1 x.2) a (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) : ℝ) := by
+        linarith
+      exact_mod_cast h3
+    · have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (enc a).length =
+          c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+      rw [hp]
+      have hprob := hno a ha
+      rw [hlaw a, uniformList_rejectCount_toReal (V := fun x => evalM x.1 x.2),
+        le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+      have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+          3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) → Bool =>
+            evalM a (List.ofFn r) = false).card : ℝ) := by
+        linarith
+      exact_mod_cast h3
+
+/-- **Probabilistic-program characterization of `PromiseRP`**: a promise problem is in `PromiseRP`
+exactly when a uniform strict PPT Boolean program accepts every yes-instance with probability at
+least `1 / 2` and never accepts a no-instance. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn : Q ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔
+    ∃ M : α → ProbComp Bool, IsPPTOn enc encBool M ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 1 / 2 ≤ Pr[M a]) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, true ∉ (ProbComp.eval (M a)).support := by
+  rw [mem_PromiseRP_iff_tidy]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => (fun w => V (a, w)) <$> BitString.sampleList (p.eval (enc a).length),
+      isPPTOn_sampleList_verifier hV, fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha hmem => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [uniformList_acceptCount_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h : (2 : ℝ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+          2 * (acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hyes a ha
+      linarith
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList,
+        PMF.mem_support_map_iff, BitString.mem_support_uniformList_iff] at hmem
+      obtain ⟨w, hw, hVw⟩ := hmem
+      have := (SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate ⟨hyes, hno⟩).2 a ha w hw
+      rw [this] at hVw
+      exact Bool.noConfusion hVw
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    obtain ⟨c, d, evalM, hevalM, hsupp, hlaw⟩ := hM.exists_total_seeded_evaluator
+    refine ⟨Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d, fun x => evalM x.1 x.2, hevalM,
+      fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha r => ?_⟩
+    · have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (enc a).length =
+          c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+      rw [hp]
+      have hprob := hyes a ha
+      rw [hlaw a _ le_rfl, uniformList_acceptCount_toReal (V := fun x => evalM x.1 x.2),
+        le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+      have h2 : (2 : ℝ) ^ (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+          2 * (acceptCount (fun x => evalM x.1 x.2) a (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) : ℝ) := by
+        linarith
+      exact_mod_cast h2
+    · rw [← Bool.not_eq_true]
+      intro htrue
+      exact hno a ha (htrue ▸ hsupp a (List.ofFn r))
+
+/-- **Probabilistic-program characterization of `PromiseCoRP`**: a promise problem is in
+`PromiseCoRP` exactly when a uniform strict PPT Boolean program never rejects a yes-instance and
+rejects every no-instance with probability at least `1 / 2`. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn : Q ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔
+    ∃ M : α → ProbComp Bool, IsPPTOn enc encBool M ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, false ∉ (ProbComp.eval (M a)).support) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 1 / 2 ≤ (ProbComp.eval (M a) false).toReal := by
+  rw [PromiseCoRP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => Bool.not <$> M a, hM.map (by fun_prop), fun a ha hmem => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.mem_support_map_iff,
+        Bool.not_eq_false'] at hmem
+      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := hmem
+      exact hno a ha hb
+    · have h : (ProbComp.eval (Bool.not <$> M a) false).toReal = Pr[M a] := by
+        simp [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_apply]
+      rw [h]
+      exact hyes a ha
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => Bool.not <$> M a, hM.map (by fun_prop), fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha hmem => ?_⟩
+    · have h : Pr[Bool.not <$> M a] = (ProbComp.eval (M a) false).toReal := by
+        simp [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_apply]
+      rw [h]
+      exact hno a ha
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.mem_support_map_iff,
+        Bool.not_eq_true'] at hmem
+      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := hmem
+      exact hyes a ha hb
+
+theorem PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP : PromiseRP enc ⊆ PromiseBPP enc := by
+  intro Q hQ
+  obtain ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩ := mem_PromiseRP_iff_tidy.mp hQ
+  have hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p).comp
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encoding_length enc)
+  refine ⟨p + p, orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V,
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_orVerifier hk hV hV), fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+  · change 2 * 2 ^ (p + p).eval (enc a).length ≤
+      3 * acceptCount (orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V) a
+        ((p + p).eval (enc a).length)
+    rw [Polynomial.eval_add]
+    generalize hk₀ : p.eval (enc a).length = k
+    have hc := acceptCount_orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V a k
+    simp only [hk₀] at hc ⊢
+    have n₁ := acceptCount_add_acceptCount_not V a k
+    have hhalf : 2 ^ k ≤ 2 * acceptCount V a k := hk₀ ▸ hyes a ha
+    have hrej : 2 * acceptCount (fun x => !V x) a k ≤ 2 ^ k := by omega
+    have hprod : 4 * (acceptCount (fun x => !V x) a k * acceptCount (fun x => !V x) a k) ≤
+        2 ^ (k + k) := by
+      rw [pow_add]
+      nlinarith [Nat.mul_le_mul hrej hrej]
+    omega
+  · rw [Polynomial.eval_add]
+    have hall (r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length + p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+        orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V (a, List.ofFn r) = false := by
+      simp only [orVerifier, Bool.or_eq_false_iff]
+      have hcert := (SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate ⟨hyes, hno⟩).2 a ha
+      exact ⟨hcert _ (by simp), hcert _ (by simp)⟩
+    rw [Finset.filter_true_of_mem fun r _ => hall r]
+    simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin]
+    omega
+
+theorem PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP : PromiseCoRP enc ⊆ PromiseBPP enc := fun Q hQ => by
+  simpa using compl_mem_PromiseBPP (PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP hQ)
+
+end PromiseProbabilistic
+
+namespace PromiseProblem
+
+variable {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool}

body:
[P2] Reuse the existing support/probability-one equivalence

Pinned Mathlib already has `PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff` and `ENNReal.toReal_eq_one_iff`. I checked the exact proposed equivalence with pinned Lean and warnings as errors using:

```lean
by
  rw [ENNReal.toReal_eq_one_iff, PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff]
  rfl
```

Remove this newly introduced 22-line public duplicate and use those existing facts at its callers. No compatibility alias is needed for a declaration introduced in this unmerged PR.

+/-- **`PromiseNP` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseNP (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y)
+    (hY : Y ∈ PromiseNP encB) : X ∈ PromiseNP encA := by
+  obtain ⟨B, hB, hyes, hno⟩ := hY
+  obtain ⟨A, hAyes, hAno, hAB⟩ := h.exists_polyTimeReducible hyes hno
+  exact ⟨A, _root_.Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.mem_NP hAB hB, hAyes, hAno⟩
+
+/-- **`PromiseBPP` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseBPP (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y)
+    (hY : Y ∈ PromiseBPP encB) : X ∈ PromiseBPP encA := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfyes, hfno⟩ := polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy.mp h
+  obtain ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩ := mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn.mp hY
+  exact mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn.mpr
+    ⟨fun a => M (f a), hM.preprocess hf, fun a ha => hyes (f a) (hfyes ha),
+      fun a ha => hno (f a) (hfno ha)⟩
+
+/-- **`PromiseRP` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseRP (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y)
+    (hY : Y ∈ PromiseRP encB) : X ∈ PromiseRP encA := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfyes, hfno⟩ := polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy.mp h
+  obtain ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩ := mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn.mp hY
+  exact mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn.mpr
+    ⟨fun a => M (f a), hM.preprocess hf, fun a ha => hyes (f a) (hfyes ha),
+      fun a ha => hno (f a) (hfno ha)⟩
+
+/-- **`PromiseCoRP` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y)
+    (hY : Y ∈ PromiseCoRP encB) : X ∈ PromiseCoRP encA := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfyes, hfno⟩ := polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy.mp h
+  obtain ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩ := mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn.mp hY
+  exact mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn.mpr
+    ⟨fun a => M (f a), hM.preprocess hf, fun a ha => hyes (f a) (hfyes ha),
+      fun a ha => hno (f a) (hfno ha)⟩
+
+/-! ### Randomized reductions with one-sided error -/
+
+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** and soundness
+threshold `s : α → ℝ` from a promise problem `X` to a promise problem `Y`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform strict PPT program
+`R : α → ProbComp β` such that:
+
+* **Completeness (no false negatives on `X.yes`):** for every `a ∈ X.yes`, every supported output
+  of `R a` lies in `Y.yes`;
+* **Soundness (`s a` on `X.no`):** for every `a ∈ X.no`, `R a` outputs an instance in `Y.no` with
+  probability at least `s a`.
+
+Instances outside `X.yes ∪ X.no` are unconstrained. -/
+def RPReducibleWithError (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (s : α → ℝ)
+    (X : PromiseProblem α) (Y : PromiseProblem β) : Prop :=
+  ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+    (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** from a promise problem
+`X` to a promise problem `Y`, with the standard soundness threshold `2 / 3`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform
+strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` mapping every yes-instance of `X` exclusively into `Y.yes`
+and mapping every no-instance of `X` into `Y.no` with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/
+def RPReducible (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool)
+    (X : PromiseProblem α) (Y : PromiseProblem β) : Prop :=
+  ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+    (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- `RPReducible` is `RPReducibleWithError` at the constant soundness threshold `2 / 3`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_rpReducibleWithError :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔ RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 2 / 3) X Y :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducibleWithError` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_probability {s : α → ℝ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducible` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_probability [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducible, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- For a discrete distribution `p`, every supported outcome lies in `S` if and only if `S` has
+real probability `1`. This bridges the support-based completeness condition
+`∀ b ∈ support, b ∈ Y.yes` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] and the probability-one condition
+`Pr[R(x) ∈ Y.yes] = 1` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],

[P2] Put the reused generic event bound in its shared home

`toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul` is a statement about arbitrary PMFs, events and a restricted-event lower bound, with no promise-problem dependency. It is already reused by composition and both randomized class pullbacks (lines 915, 1062 and 1125). Move this small lemma to the existing `Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean` API and consume it here. Existing Event/Bind and pinned upstream were checked; no equivalent with these restricted-event premises was found. Keep the same premises and proof; no new probability model or hierarchy is needed.

+/-- **`PromiseNP` is closed under polynomial-time reductions.** -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseNP (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y)

+/-! ### Randomized reductions with one-sided error -/
+
+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** and soundness
+threshold `s : α → ℝ` from a promise problem `X` to a promise problem `Y`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform strict PPT program
+`R : α → ProbComp β` such that:
+
+* **Completeness (no false negatives on `X.yes`):** for every `a ∈ X.yes`, every supported output
+  of `R a` lies in `Y.yes`;
+* **Soundness (`s a` on `X.no`):** for every `a ∈ X.no`, `R a` outputs an instance in `Y.no` with
+  probability at least `s a`.
+
+Instances outside `X.yes ∪ X.no` are unconstrained. -/
+def RPReducibleWithError (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (s : α → ℝ)
+    (X : PromiseProblem α) (Y : PromiseProblem β) : Prop :=
+  ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+    (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** from a promise problem
+`X` to a promise problem `Y`, with the standard soundness threshold `2 / 3`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform
+strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` mapping every yes-instance of `X` exclusively into `Y.yes`
+and mapping every no-instance of `X` into `Y.no` with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/
+def RPReducible (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool)
+    (X : PromiseProblem α) (Y : PromiseProblem β) : Prop :=
+  ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+    (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- `RPReducible` is `RPReducibleWithError` at the constant soundness threshold `2 / 3`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_rpReducibleWithError :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔ RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 2 / 3) X Y :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducibleWithError` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_probability {s : α → ℝ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducible` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_probability [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducible, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- For a discrete distribution `p`, every supported outcome lies in `S` if and only if `S` has
+real probability `1`. This bridges the support-based completeness condition
+`∀ b ∈ support, b ∈ Y.yes` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] and the probability-one condition
+`Pr[R(x) ∈ Y.yes] = 1` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one (p : _root_.PMF β) (S : Set β) :
+    (∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S) ↔ (p.toOuterMeasure S).toReal = 1 := by
+  have hadd := PMF.toOuterMeasure_toReal_add_compl p S
+  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+  have hzero : (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal = 0 ↔ ∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S := by
+    rw [← not_iff_not]
+    have hpos := PMF.toOuterMeasure_toReal_pos_iff p Sᶜ
+    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff] at hpos
+    constructor
+    · intro h hforall
+      obtain ⟨b, hbS, hbs⟩ := hpos.mp (lt_of_le_of_ne hnonneg (Ne.symm h))
+      exact hbS (hforall b hbs)
+    · intro h
+      have ⟨b, hbs, hbS⟩ : ∃ b ∈ p.support, b ∉ S := by
+        by_contra! hc
+        exact h hc
+      exact ne_of_gt (hpos.mpr ⟨b, hbS, hbs⟩)
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    linarith [hzero.mpr h]
+  · intro h
+    exact hzero.mp (by linarith)
+
+/-- Equivalence of support-based completeness and probability-one completeness for
+`RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one {s : α → ℝ} :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one]
+
+/-- Equivalence of support-based completeness and probability-one completeness for
+`RPReducible` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal :=
+  rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one
+
+/-- Lowering the soundness threshold preserves `RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.mono {s₁ s₂ : α → ℝ}
+    (h : RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₁ X Y) (hs : ∀ a ∈ X.no, s₂ a ≤ s₁ a) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₂ X Y :=
+  let ⟨R, hR, hyes, hno⟩ := h
+  ⟨R, hR, hyes, fun a ha => (hs a ha).trans (hno a ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every `RPReducible` reduction with soundness `2 / 3` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] is also
+an `RPReducibleWithError` reduction with soundness `1 / 2` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira,
+Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]. -/
+theorem RPReducible.rpReducibleWithError_half (h : RPReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 1 / 2) X Y :=
+  RPReducibleWithError.mono h fun _ _ => by norm_num
+
+/-- **Valiant–Vazirani dual convention bridge** [Valiant and Vazirani][ValiantVazirani1986],
+[Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]: a randomized reduction from `X` to `Y` in the dual
+one-sided error convention (mapping yes-instances into `Y.yes` with probability at least `2 / 3`
+and mapping no-instances exclusively into `Y.no`) is `RPReducible` between the complement promise
+problems `Xᶜ` and `Yᶜ`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_compl_iff :
+    RPReducible encA encB Xᶜ Yᶜ ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.no, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.no) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.yes, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+open Classical in
+/-- The real probability that a function of a uniform bit string of length `n` lands in `S` is the
+fraction of `n`-bit strings mapping into `S`. -/
+private theorem toOuterMeasure_map_uniformList_toReal (f : List Bool → β) (n : ℕ) (S : Set β) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map f).toOuterMeasure S).toReal =
+      ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin n → Bool => f (List.ofFn r) ∈ S).card : ℝ) / 2 ^ n := by
+  rw [BitString.uniformList, PMF.map_comp, PMF.toOuterMeasure_map_apply,
+    PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFintype_toReal]
+  simp [Function.comp_def, Set.mem_preimage]
+
+open Classical in
+/-- **Seeded-function characterization of `RPReducible`** [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020],
+[Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]: `X` is `RPReducible` to `Y`
+if and only if there are a polynomial `p` and a function `f : α × List Bool → β`, computable in
+polynomial time with respect to `encPair encA encBits` and `encB`, such that for every `a ∈ X.yes`
+and every random string `r` of length `p(|a|)` we have `f(a, r) ∈ Y.yes`, and for every `a ∈ X.no`
+at least two thirds of the random strings `r` of length `p(|a|)` satisfy `f(a, r) ∈ Y.no`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_exists_seeded :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (f : α × List Bool → β),
+        ComputableInPolyTime f (encPair encA encBits) encB ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ r : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) → Bool, f (a, List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (encA a).length ≤
+          3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) → Bool =>
+            f (a, List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.no).card := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨R, hR, hyes, hno⟩
+    obtain ⟨c, d, evalR, hevalR, hsupp, hlaw⟩ := hR.exists_total_seeded_evaluator
+    refine ⟨Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d, fun x => evalR x.1 x.2, .of_tidy hevalR,
+      fun a ha r => hyes a ha _ (hsupp a (List.ofFn r)), fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (encA a).length =
+        c * ((encA a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+    rw [hp]
+    have hprob := hno a ha
+    rw [hlaw a _ le_rfl, toOuterMeasure_map_uniformList_toReal,
+      le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+    have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ (c * ((encA a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+        3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (c * ((encA a).length + 1) ^ d) → Bool =>
+          evalR a (List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.no).card : ℝ) := by
+      linarith
+    exact_mod_cast h3
+  · rintro ⟨p, f, hf, hyes, hno⟩
+    have hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (encA a).length) encA encUnary :=
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p).comp
+        (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encoding_length encA)
+    let R (a : α) : ProbComp β :=
+      (fun w => f (a, w)) <$> BitString.sampleList (p.eval (encA a).length)
+    have hR : IsPPTOn encA encB R := hcount.sampleList.map_with hf.tidy
+    refine ⟨R, hR, fun a ha b hb => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [R, ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList,
+        PMF.mem_support_map_iff, BitString.mem_support_uniformList_iff] at hb
+      obtain ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩ := hb
+      have hr := hyes a ha fun i => w[i.val]'(by omega)
+      rwa [show (List.ofFn fun i : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) => w[i.val]'(by omega)) = w from
+        List.ext_getElem (by simp [hw]) fun i _ _ => by simp] at hr
+    · simp only [R, ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [toOuterMeasure_map_uniformList_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ p.eval (encA a).length ≤
+          3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) → Bool =>
+            f (a, List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.no).card : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hno a ha
+      linarith
+
+/-! ### Lifting deterministic reductions and structural closure -/
+
+/-- Every deterministic polynomial-time reduction of promise problems lifts to a randomized
+reduction with soundness `1` (zero error). -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.rpReducibleWithError (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 1) X Y := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hyes, hno⟩ := polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy.mp h
+  refine ⟨fun a => pure (f a), hf.isPPTOn, fun a ha b hb => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+  · simp only [ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.support_pure, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hb
+    exact hb ▸ hyes ha
+  · have hmem : f a ∈ Y.no := hno ha
+    simp [ProbComp.eval_pure, hmem]
+
+/-- Every deterministic polynomial-time reduction of promise problems is a randomized one-sided
+reduction (`RPReducible`). -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y :=
+  h.rpReducibleWithError.mono fun _ _ => by norm_num
+
+/-- Every deterministic polynomial-time reduction between decision problems gives an `RPReducible`
+reduction between their promise problems. -/
+theorem _root_.Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible_ofSet {A : Set α} {B : Set β}
+    (h : Complexity.PolyTimeReducible encA encB A B) :
+    RPReducible encA encB (ofSet A) (ofSet B) :=
+  (polyTimeReducible_ofSet_iff.mpr h).rpReducible
+
+/-- Every promise problem reduces to itself by a zero-error randomized reduction. -/
+@[refl]
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.refl (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (X : PromiseProblem α) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encA (fun _ => 1) X X :=
+  (PolyTimeReducible.refl encA X).rpReducibleWithError
+
+/-- Every promise problem is `RPReducible` to itself. -/
+@[refl]
+theorem RPReducible.refl (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (X : PromiseProblem α) :
+    RPReducible encA encA X X :=
+  (PolyTimeReducible.refl encA X).rpReducible
+
+/-- Enlarging the target promise preserves `RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.of_subset {s : α → ℝ}
+    (h : RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y) (hyes : Y.yes ⊆ Y'.yes) (hno : Y.no ⊆ Y'.no) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y' := by
+  obtain ⟨R, hR, hRyes, hRno⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨R, hR, fun a ha b hb => hyes (hRyes a ha b hb), fun a ha => (hRno a ha).trans ?_⟩
+  exact ENNReal.toReal_mono (PMF.toOuterMeasure_ne_top _ _)
+    ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure.mono hno)
+
+/-- Enlarging the target promise preserves `RPReducible`. -/
+theorem RPReducible.of_subset (h : RPReducible encA encB X Y) (hyes : Y.yes ⊆ Y'.yes)
+    (hno : Y.no ⊆ Y'.no) : RPReducible encA encB X Y' :=
+  RPReducibleWithError.of_subset h hyes hno
+
+/-- If `p` lands in `S` with probability at least `s₁` and for every supported `b ∈ S` the
+continuation `k b` lands in `T` with probability at least `s₂`, then `p.bind k` lands in `T` with
+probability at least `s₁ * s₂`. -/
+private theorem toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul (p : _root_.PMF β) (k : β → _root_.PMF γ)

body:
[P2] Distinguish complement duality from the Valiant–Vazirani success bound

[Valiant–Vazirani](https://ics.uci.edu/~vazirani/ValVaz.pdf), printed pp. 86–87, uses inverse-polynomial YES success (the isolation bound is `1/(4n)`). This `rfl` bridge complements a constant `2/3` convention; it does not normalize that source reduction. Under #798's faithfulness rule, label this as an original library complement-duality identity and explicitly state the quantitative difference, rather than a proved Valiant–Vazirani equivalence. A threshold-parametric `RPReducibleWithError` complement identity could expose the inverse-polynomial convention directly. No implementation of amplification or of the paper's reduction is requested.

+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** and soundness
+threshold `s : α → ℝ` from a promise problem `X` to a promise problem `Y`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform strict PPT program
+`R : α → ProbComp β` such that:
+

+  of `R a` lies in `Y.yes`;
+* **Soundness (`s a` on `X.no`):** for every `a ∈ X.no`, `R a` outputs an instance in `Y.no` with
+  probability at least `s a`.
+
+Instances outside `X.yes ∪ X.no` are unconstrained. -/
+def RPReducibleWithError (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool) (s : α → ℝ)
+    (X : PromiseProblem α) (Y : PromiseProblem β) : Prop :=
+  ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+    (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** from a promise problem
+`X` to a promise problem `Y`, with the standard soundness threshold `2 / 3`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform
+strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` mapping every yes-instance of `X` exclusively into `Y.yes`
+and mapping every no-instance of `X` into `Y.no` with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/
+def RPReducible (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (encB : β ↪ List Bool)
+    (X : PromiseProblem α) (Y : PromiseProblem β) : Prop :=
+  ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+    (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- `RPReducible` is `RPReducibleWithError` at the constant soundness threshold `2 / 3`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_rpReducibleWithError :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔ RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 2 / 3) X Y :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducibleWithError` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_probability {s : α → ℝ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducible` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_probability [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducible, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- For a discrete distribution `p`, every supported outcome lies in `S` if and only if `S` has
+real probability `1`. This bridges the support-based completeness condition
+`∀ b ∈ support, b ∈ Y.yes` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] and the probability-one condition
+`Pr[R(x) ∈ Y.yes] = 1` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one (p : _root_.PMF β) (S : Set β) :
+    (∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S) ↔ (p.toOuterMeasure S).toReal = 1 := by
+  have hadd := PMF.toOuterMeasure_toReal_add_compl p S
+  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+  have hzero : (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal = 0 ↔ ∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S := by
+    rw [← not_iff_not]
+    have hpos := PMF.toOuterMeasure_toReal_pos_iff p Sᶜ
+    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff] at hpos
+    constructor
+    · intro h hforall
+      obtain ⟨b, hbS, hbs⟩ := hpos.mp (lt_of_le_of_ne hnonneg (Ne.symm h))
+      exact hbS (hforall b hbs)
+    · intro h
+      have ⟨b, hbs, hbS⟩ : ∃ b ∈ p.support, b ∉ S := by
+        by_contra! hc
+        exact h hc
+      exact ne_of_gt (hpos.mpr ⟨b, hbS, hbs⟩)
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    linarith [hzero.mpr h]
+  · intro h
+    exact hzero.mp (by linarith)
+

+`RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one {s : α → ℝ} :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one]
+
+/-- Equivalence of support-based completeness and probability-one completeness for
+`RPReducible` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal :=
+  rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one
+
+/-- Lowering the soundness threshold preserves `RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.mono {s₁ s₂ : α → ℝ}
+    (h : RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₁ X Y) (hs : ∀ a ∈ X.no, s₂ a ≤ s₁ a) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₂ X Y :=
+  let ⟨R, hR, hyes, hno⟩ := h
+  ⟨R, hR, hyes, fun a ha => (hs a ha).trans (hno a ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every `RPReducible` reduction with soundness `2 / 3` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] is also
+an `RPReducibleWithError` reduction with soundness `1 / 2` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira,
+Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]. -/
+theorem RPReducible.rpReducibleWithError_half (h : RPReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 1 / 2) X Y :=
+  RPReducibleWithError.mono h fun _ _ => by norm_num
+
+/-- **Valiant–Vazirani dual convention bridge** [Valiant and Vazirani][ValiantVazirani1986],

body:
[P2] Correct the source locators and distinguish library generalizations

Please correct these module citations and the PR faithfulness table:

- [Ilango ITCS 2020](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/11719/pdf/LIPIcs-ITCS-2020-34.pdf), §2 p.34:11, matches the perfect-YES/NO-`2/3` convention. Corollary 3.4 p.34:16 is a randomized reduction to **MOCSP**, not the body's MCSP* or claimed collapse theorem; label the generic collapse consequences as library results.
- [ILO CCC 2020](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol169-ccc2020/LIPIcs.CCC.2020.22/LIPIcs.CCC.2020.22.pdf): §3.2 is MDCP. Multi-MCSP is §4.2, Lemmas 15–16, pp.22:20–22:23, from **gap/approximate bounded Set Cover**, with high-probability soundness. The table drops that gap and calls `1/2` the exact source parameter. The parametric API can represent a weakened half bound; `2/3 ⇒ 1/2` is only weakening, not normalization in the other direction.
- [Hirahara TR22-119](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2022/119/download), Lemma 8.3 p.26 and Theorem 8.5 pp.30–31, supports the one-sided orientation with soundness `1-o(1)`. Arbitrary threshold functions and composition accounting here are library generalizations, not that paper's tunable-δ theorem.
- In [Goldreich's July 2005 author version](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/PSX/prpr-r.pdf), BPP is Definition 1.2 p.4; RP/coRP are §6.2 p.18, rather than §5.1. Identify the version used.

Also add the missing bibliography entries for the newly used `Ilango2020`, `IlangoLoffOliveira2020` and `Hirahara2022` keys; exact-head `references.bib` contains none of them.

[P2] Classify reducible raw-premise aliases before allowing transitions

The `.find?` scan checks literal constant names in binder types. Pinned FunProp recognizes reducible aliases, so a full-arity abbreviation hides the raw premise here and is subsequently searched as a raw property. The following ordinary-import reproducer passes at this exact head: the first goal rejects `polytime`, but after the aliased transition is registered the identical goal succeeds. +/-- Restate known local certificates in the goal's family. This introduces proof facts only;
+it never changes the goal or searches the other calculus. -/

+private meta def polytimeKnownFacts : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
+  let mut goal ← getMainGoal
+  let predicate ← polytimePredicate (← goal.getType)
+  let (source, conversion) := if predicate == ``ComputableInPolyTime then
+      (``ComputableTidilyInPolyTime, ``ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy)
+    else (``ComputableInPolyTime, ``ComputableInPolyTime.tidy)
+  let mut added := false
+  for h in ← getLCtx do
+    unless h.isImplementationDetail do
+      let type := (← whnfR (← instantiateMVars h.type)).consumeMData
+      if type.isAppOf source && !type.hasExprMVar then
+        let proof ← mkAppM conversion #[h.toExpr]

+        let found ← (← getLCtx).anyM fun other => isDefEq other.type type

+          let (_, next) ← goal.note (← mkFreshUserName `knownCertificate) proof

+open Lean Meta in
+/-- Inspect proposition aliases with the same reducible transparency used by `fun_prop`.
+`Meta.transform` maintains binder context, including dependent and quantified premises; data and
+proof implementations are not unfolded merely to classify a transition's proposition. -/
+private meta def rawTransitionPremise (type : Expr) : MetaM Bool := do
+  let rawName := fun n : Name =>
+    n.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidily" ||
+      n.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidily"

+      | .const n _ => rawName n
+      | _ => false).isSome then

+    discard <| Meta.transform type (pre := fun e => do
+      if ← get then return .done e
+      let reduced ← if ← isProp e then whnfR e else pure e
+      if let .const name _ := reduced.getAppFn then
+        if rawName name then

+/-- Retain ordinary transitions while excluding those that require raw construction predicates.

+private meta def plainTransitions (thms : GeneralTheorems) : MetaM GeneralTheorems := do
+  let mut names : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for node in thms.theorems.tries do
+    for rule in node.values do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+    for (_, rule) in node.pending do names := names.insert rule.thmName

+    tries := thms.theorems.tries.map fun node =>

+/-- Shared compositional backend with a fresh alias-aware transition boundary. The standard

+  let target ← goal.getType
+  let disch : Expr → MetaM (Option Expr) := fun e => do
+    tacticToDischarge (← `(tactic| first | with_reducible assumption | infer_param)) e
+  let ctx : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Context := { config := { maxSteps }, disch }
+  let env ← getEnv
+  let state : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.State := {
+    morTheorems := morTheoremsExt.getState env
+    transitionTheorems := ← plainTransitions (transitionTheoremsExt.getState env) }

+/-!
+# Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity (`K^t`) and Levin's `Kt`
+
+This module defines the universal multi-tape Turing machine description method
+`Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTM` for binary strings, the corresponding plain and
+time-bounded Kolmogorov complexities `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain` (`K`) and
+`Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded` (`K^t`), and Levin's time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity
+`Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKt` (`Kt`).
+
+## Modeling conventions (#798 Decisions D1–D3)
+
+* **D1 (clock counts steps of the described machine):**
+  A binary program `p : List Bool` is parsed into a multi-tape Turing machine description
+  `decodeDesc (unframe p)` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.decodeDesc`) and an input bit string
+  `dropFrame p` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.dropFrame`). At step bound `t`, `universalTM` runs the
+  described machine on `(dropFrame p).map eBit` for `t` steps (`Universal.Desc.runFor`).
+  In [Liu and Pass, Section 2.2][LiuPass2020], $U(\Pi, 1^t)$ denotes the output of $M(w)$ when
+  emulated for $t$ steps (whose proof of Theorem 5.2 requires counting steps of the described
+  machine $M$, or a constant-overhead universal simulator). Counting the steps of the described
+  multi-tape machine directly in `universalTM` makes $K^t$ exact at linear time scales while the
+  polynomial overhead of the universal simulator `Universal.universal` appears only in algorithmic
+  membership results such as `MINKT ∈ NP`.
+* **D2 (global output):**
+  When the described machine halts within `t` steps, the entire output tape contents are mapped back
+  to `List Bool` via `(· != 0)`, matching the global "print $x$" convention of
+  [Ko][Ko1986], [Liu and Pass, Section 2.2][LiuPass2020], and [Hirahara][Hirahara2018], as well as
+  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFor_eq_simulate`.
+* **D3 (values in `ℕ∞` with finite-form bridges):**
+  `plain`, `timeBounded`, and `levinKt` take values in `ℕ∞` via
+  `DescriptionMethod.ecomplexity` and `DescriptionMethod.etimeBoundedComplexity`, accompanied by
+  `ℕ`-valued wrappers (`plainNat`, `timeBoundedNat`, `levinKtNat`) and proved equivalence bridges
+  (`timeBounded_le_natCast_iff`, `timeBoundedNat_le_iff`, `timeBoundedNat_eq_sInf`,
+  `levinKt_le_natCast_iff`) showing agreement with the literature's `min` over `ℕ` whenever a
+  witness exists.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTMRunFor`: clocked evaluation of a binary program
+  `p` for `t` steps of the described multi-tape machine.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTM`: the universal multi-tape description method on
+  `List Bool`.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plainNat`: plain Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ under
+  `universalTM` in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ`.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBoundedNat`: time-bounded Kolmogorov
+  complexity $K^t(x)$ for a time bound $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ`.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKt`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKtNat`: Levin's time-bounded complexity
+  $\mathrm{Kt}(x) = \inf_{s \ge 1} (K^s(x) + \lceil \log_2 s \rceil)$, in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTMSimulation`,
+  `Cslib.Kolmogorov.simulation_ofMultiTapeTM`: every finite-state binary `MultiTapeTM` is simulated
+  by `universalTM` with constant program overhead and zero time overhead.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded_anti`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded_mono_of_le`: monotonicity in
+  the time bound $t$.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded_le`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_timeBounded_le`:
+  $K^t(x) \le |x| + c$ whenever $t(|x|) \ge |x| + 1$ ([Liu and Pass, Fact 2.1][LiuPass2020] under
+  the multi-tape output convention).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain_le_timeBounded`,
+  `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded`: $K(x) \le K^t(x)$ against both
+  `plain` (`universalTM.ecomplexity`) and `DescriptionMethod.universal.ecomplexity`.

+/-!
+# The Partial Minimum Circuit Size Problem (`MCSP*`)
+
+The *Partial Minimum Circuit Size Problem* (`MCSP*` or `PartialMCSP`) asks, given the truth table
+of a partial Boolean function $f^* : \{0, 1\}^n \to \{0, 1, *\}$ on `arity = n` inputs and a size
+threshold `s`, whether there exists a total Boolean function $f : \{0, 1\}^n \to \{0, 1\}$ that
+extends $f^*$ (agreeing with $f^*$ on every input where $f^*(x) \ne *$) and has a circuit of size
+at most `s` [Ilango2020FOCS, Section 2.2; Hirahara2022, Definition 8.4].
+
+In `PartialMCSP.Instance`, the truth table has $2^n$ entries in `Option Bool`, where `some b`
+requires the circuit to output `b` and `none` represents the "don't care" symbol `*` (also written
+`?` in [Hirahara2022]).
+
+Following Decision D5 on issue #798, `Cslib.PartialMCSP` uses the standard De Morgan all-gates size
+measure `Circuit.size` (`complexityOn interpretation x.definedInputs (single x.completion)`),
+matching `Cslib.MCSP` and `Cslib.SuccinctMCSP`. We also define `Cslib.PartialMCSP.BinaryGate` using
+the AND/OR-only gate count `c.program.cost binaryCost` from [Ilango2020FOCS, Section 2.2] (where NOT
+and constant gates are free), and prove the fan-in and threshold-$n-1$ bridge theorems relating the
+two measures:
+* Every De Morgan circuit `c : Circuit signature n m` depends on at most
+  `m + c.program.cost binaryCost` inputs (`Circuit.card_inputSupport_le_cost_binaryCost`), because
+  only binary AND and OR gates increase the number of supporting inputs in the backward cone.
+* A program has `p.cost binaryCost = g` if and only if every gate is a binary AND or OR gate
+  (`Program.cost_binaryCost_eq_iff_forall_isBinary`).
+* Every yes-instance of `PartialMCSP` is a yes-instance of `PartialMCSP.BinaryGate`
+  (`PartialMCSP.mem_binaryGate_of_mem`).
+* When all `n` input coordinates are essential for the partial function, no circuit with fewer than
+  `n - 1` binary gates can agree with it (`PartialMCSP.not_mem_binaryGate_of_threshold_lt`), and at
+  threshold `n - 1` any all-gates circuit agreeing with it must have size `n - 1`, binary cost
+  `n - 1`, and consist solely of binary AND/OR gates
+  (`PartialMCSP.isBinary_of_mem_of_threshold_le`).
+
+String encodings of `PartialMCSP.Instance`, membership in `NP`, and the polynomial-time many-one
+reduction from `MCSP` to `PartialMCSP` are in `Complexity.Computability.MCSP.PartialNP`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.PartialMCSP.Instance`: an instance of partial-function MCSP (`arity`, `table` of length
+  $2^{\text{arity}}$ over `Option Bool`, and `threshold`).
+* `Cslib.PartialMCSP.Instance.AgreesWith`: a total Boolean function extends the partial truth table.
+* `Cslib.PartialMCSP`: yes-instances under the all-gates De Morgan circuit size measure.
+* `Cslib.PartialMCSP.BinaryGate`: yes-instances under Ilango's AND/OR-only gate measure
+  (`binaryCost`).
+* `Cslib.PartialMCSP.Instance.ofTotal`, `Cslib.PartialMCSP.Instance.toSuccinct`: embeddings into
+  `PartialMCSP` from `MCSP` and from `PartialMCSP` into `SuccinctMCSP`.
+

+  outputs depends on at most `m + c.program.cost binaryCost` inputs.
+* `Cslib.Circuits.Program.cost_binaryCost_eq_iff_forall_isBinary`: `p.cost binaryCost = g` iff every

+open Lean Meta Elab Tactic in
+/-- Restate known local certificates in the goal's family. This introduces proof facts only;
+it never changes the goal or searches the other calculus. -/
+@[aesop safe -30 tactic (rule_sets := [PolyTime])]
+private meta def polytimeKnownFacts : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
+  let mut goal ← getMainGoal
+  let predicate ← polytimePredicate (← goal.getType)
+  let (source, conversion) := if predicate == ``ComputableInPolyTime then
+      (``ComputableTidilyInPolyTime, ``ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy)
+    else (``ComputableInPolyTime, ``ComputableInPolyTime.tidy)
+  let mut added := false
+  for h in ← getLCtx do
+    unless h.isImplementationDetail do
+      let type := (← whnfR (← instantiateMVars h.type)).consumeMData
+      if type.isAppOf source && !type.hasExprMVar then
+        let proof ← mkAppM conversion #[h.toExpr]
+        let type ← inferType proof
+        let found ← (← getLCtx).anyM fun other => isDefEq other.type type
+        unless found do
+          let (_, next) ← goal.note (← mkFreshUserName `knownCertificate) proof
+          goal := next
+          added := true
+  unless added do throwError "no new known certificate"
+  replaceMainGoal [goal]

+open Lean Meta in
+/-- Inspect proposition aliases with the same reducible transparency used by `fun_prop`.
+`Meta.transform` maintains binder context, including dependent and quantified premises; data and
+proof implementations are not unfolded merely to classify a transition's proposition. -/
+private meta def rawTransitionPremise (type : Expr) : MetaM Bool := do
+  let rawName := fun n : Name =>
+    n.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidily" ||
+      n.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidily"
+  if (type.find? fun e => match e with
+      | .const n _ => rawName n
+      | _ => false).isSome then
+    return true
+  let inspect : StateRefT Bool MetaM Unit := do
+    discard <| Meta.transform type (pre := fun e => do
+      if ← get then return .done e
+      let reduced ← if ← isProp e then whnfR e else pure e
+      if let .const name _ := reduced.getAppFn then
+        if rawName name then
+          set true
+          return .done reduced
+      return .continue (some reduced))
+  return (← inspect.run false).2
+
+open Lean in
+private meta initialize rawPremiseCache : EnvExtension (Std.HashMap Name Bool) ←
+  registerEnvExtension (pure {}) (asyncMode := .local)
+
+open Lean Meta in
+/-- Inspect a registered rule's hypotheses, including reducible proposition aliases. -/
+private meta def hasRawPremise (name : Name) : MetaM Bool := do
+  if let some result := (rawPremiseCache.getState (← getEnv)).get? name then return result
+  let some info := (← getEnv).find? name | return true
+  forallTelescope info.type fun xs _ => do
+    xs.anyM fun x => do
+      let premise ← inferType x
+      if ← isProp premise then rawTransitionPremise premise else pure false
+
+open Lean in
+/-- Modify only the search's environment copy, including during asynchronous proof elaboration.
+The change cannot escape `withEnv`, so it is local and needs no persistent write log. -/
+private meta def searchRuleState {α β σ : Type} (ext : ScopedEnvExtension α β σ)
+    (env : Environment) (f : σ → σ) : Environment :=
+  ext.ext.modifyState (asyncMode := .local) (log := .unlogged) env fun s =>
+    match s.stateStack with
+    | top :: stack =>
+      { s with stateStack := { top with state := f top.state } :: stack }
+    | [] => s
+
+open Lean Meta Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Shadow global function and composition rules only during public search. Local proof entries
+and the original databases remain available outside it, including explicit raw construction. -/
+private meta def plainRuleEnvironment (env : Environment) : MetaM Environment := do
+  let mut seen : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  let mut blocked : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for (_, properties) in (functionTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for (_, rules) in properties do
+      for rule in rules do
+        if let .decl name := rule.thmOrigin then
+          unless seen.contains name do
+            seen := seen.insert name
+            if ← hasRawPremise name then blocked := blocked.insert name
+  for (_, rules) in (lambdaTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for rule in rules do
+      unless seen.contains rule.thmName do
+        seen := seen.insert rule.thmName
+        if ← hasRawPremise rule.thmName then blocked := blocked.insert rule.thmName
+  let env := searchRuleState functionTheoremsExt env fun s =>
+    { s with theorems := s.theorems.map fun _ properties => properties.map fun _ rules =>
+      rules.filter fun rule => match rule.thmOrigin with
+        | .decl name => !blocked.contains name
+        | .fvar _ => true }
+  return searchRuleState lambdaTheoremsExt env fun s =>
+    { s with theorems := s.theorems.map fun _ rules =>
+        rules.filter fun rule => !blocked.contains rule.thmName }
+
+open Lean Meta Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Retain ordinary general rules while excluding raw construction premises.
+Both evaluated entries and lazy entries must be removed from this per-search tree. -/
+private meta def plainGeneralTheorems (thms : GeneralTheorems) : MetaM GeneralTheorems := do
+  let mut names : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for node in thms.theorems.tries do
+    for rule in node.values do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+    for (_, rule) in node.pending do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+  let mut blocked : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for name in names do
+    if ← hasRawPremise name then blocked := blocked.insert name
+  return { thms with theorems := { thms.theorems with
+    tries := thms.theorems.tries.map fun node =>
+      { node with
+        values := node.values.filter fun rule => !blocked.contains rule.thmName
+        pending := node.pending.filter fun entry => !blocked.contains entry.2.thmName } } }
+
+open Lean Meta Elab Tactic Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Classify global rules once for this tactic invocation. Aesop alternatives reuse these
+immutable answers; each backend still receives fresh rule tables and dynamic local evidence. -/
+meta def Internal.withPlainRuleCache (action : TacticM Unit) : TacticM Unit := do
+  let env ← getEnv
+  let mut names : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for (_, properties) in (functionTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for (_, rules) in properties do
+      for rule in rules do
+        if let .decl name := rule.thmOrigin then names := names.insert name
+  for (_, rules) in (lambdaTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for rule in rules do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+  for rules in #[morTheoremsExt.getState env, transitionTheoremsExt.getState env] do
+    for node in rules.theorems.tries do
+      for rule in node.values do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+      for (_, rule) in node.pending do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+  -- Imports are dependency-first. A theorem in a module with no raw-family declaration in
+  -- its import closure cannot hide one behind an alias: aliases cannot refer to later modules.
+  -- Unknown module metadata remains conservative, and current-module rules are always checked.
+  let mut rawModules : Std.HashMap Name Bool := {}
+  for i in [:env.header.moduleNames.size] do
+    let moduleName := env.header.moduleNames[i]!
+    let data := env.header.moduleData[i]!
+    let ownsRaw := data.constNames.any fun name =>
+      name.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidily" ||
+        name.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidily"
+    let importsRaw := data.imports.any fun imported => rawModules.getD imported.module true
+    rawModules := rawModules.insert moduleName (ownsRaw || importsRaw)
+  let mut cache : Std.HashMap Name Bool := {}
+  for name in names do
+    let mayUseRaw := match env.getModuleIdxFor? name with
+      | some i => rawModules.getD env.header.moduleNames[i.toNat]! true
+      | none => true
+    cache := cache.insert name (← if mayUseRaw then hasRawPremise name else pure false)
+  -- The cache is confined to this `withEnv`; unrelated tactics and later declarations see none.
+  withEnv (rawPremiseCache.setState env cache) action
+
+open Lean Meta Elab Tactic Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Shared compositional backend with a fresh alias-aware raw-premise boundary. The standard
+assumption discharger and ordinary transition depth are retained; callers keep their step limit.
+Consumers can reuse the same boundary for nested plain deterministic goals. -/
+meta def Internal.funPropWithPlainBoundary (maxSteps : Nat) : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
+  let goal ← getMainGoal
+  let target ← goal.getType
+  let disch : Expr → MetaM (Option Expr) := fun e => do
+    tacticToDischarge (← `(tactic| first | with_reducible assumption | infer_param)) e
+  let ctx : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Context := { config := { maxSteps }, disch }
+  let env ← getEnv
+  let state : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.State := {
+    morTheorems := ← plainGeneralTheorems (morTheoremsExt.getState env)
+    transitionTheorems := ← plainGeneralTheorems (transitionTheoremsExt.getState env) }
+  let ruleEnv ← plainRuleEnvironment env
+  let (result, state) ← withEnv ruleEnv <| (funProp target ctx).run state

+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
+wt_path = Path(sys.argv[2])
+worktrees_root = (root / ".worktrees").resolve()
+
+
+def in_primary_checkout(p: Path) -> bool:
+    return p == root or (p.is_relative_to(root) and not p.is_relative_to(worktrees_root))
+
+
+manifest = wt_path / "lake-manifest.json"
+if not manifest.is_file():
+    manifest = root / "lake-manifest.json"
+
+pin_name = None
+if manifest.is_file():
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        for pkg in data.get("packages", []):
+            if isinstance(pkg, dict) and pkg.get("name") == "cslib":
+                rev = pkg.get("rev") or ""
+                if isinstance(rev, str) and rev:
+                    pin_name = f"packages-cslib-{rev[:8]}"
+                    break
+    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
+        pass
+
+if pin_name is None:
+    cslib_dir = root / ".lake/packages/cslib"
+    if (cslib_dir / ".git").exists():
+        try:
+            rev = subprocess.check_output(
+                ["git", "-C", str(cslib_dir), "rev-parse", "--short=8", "HEAD"],
+                text=True,
+                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+            ).strip()
+            if rev:
+                pin_name = f"packages-cslib-{rev}"
+        except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
+            pass
+
+if pin_name is None:
+    if manifest.is_file():
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(manifest.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:8]
+        pin_name = f"packages-manifest-{digest}"
+    else:
+        pin_name = "packages-cslib-default"
+
+env_shared = os.environ.get("COMPLEXITYLIB_SHARED_PACKAGES_ROOT", "")
+if env_shared:
+    shared_root = Path(env_shared).resolve()
+    if in_primary_checkout(shared_root) or shared_root == worktrees_root:
+        print(
+            f"Refusing shared packages directory inside primary checkout: {env_shared}",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+    print(shared_root / pin_name)
+    raise SystemExit(0)
+
+candidates = []
+try:
+    wt_parent = wt_path.resolve().parent
+    if not in_primary_checkout(wt_parent) and wt_parent != worktrees_root:
+        candidates.append(wt_parent / ".shared" / pin_name)
+except OSError:
+    pass
+candidates.append(worktrees_root / ".shared" / pin_name)
+candidates.append(Path(f"{root}-wt") / ".shared" / pin_name)
+
+for cand in candidates:
+    if cand.is_dir() and not in_primary_checkout(cand.resolve()):
+        print(cand)

+# check_worktree_safety <worktree_path> <expected_shared_pkg_dir>: refuse if the target worktree

+  local expected_shared="$2"

+

+    return p == root or (p.is_relative_to(root) and not p.is_relative_to(worktrees_root))

+        )

+    print(f"Refusing to seed or point at primary checkout: {wt_raw}", file=sys.stderr)
+    raise SystemExit(1)
+
+if expected_shared is not None and in_primary_checkout(expected_shared):
+    print(
+        f"Refusing shared packages directory inside primary checkout: {expected_shared}",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    raise SystemExit(1)
+
+for rel in (".lake", ".lake/build", ".lake/config"):
+    cand = wt_raw / rel
+    if cand.is_symlink():
+        target = cand.resolve()
+        if in_primary_checkout(target):
+            print(
+                f"Refusing destination cache symlink pointing into primary checkout: {cand} -> {target}",
+                file=sys.stderr,
+            )
+        else:
+            print(f"Refusing to seed through destination cache symlink: {cand}", file=sys.stderr)
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+pkg_link = wt_raw / ".lake/packages"
+if pkg_link.is_symlink():
+    target = pkg_link.resolve()
+    if in_primary_checkout(target):
+        print(
+            f"Refusing destination cache symlink pointing into primary checkout: {pkg_link} -> {target}",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+    if expected_shared is None or target != expected_shared:
+        print(f"Refusing to seed through destination cache symlink: {pkg_link}", file=sys.stderr)
+        raise SystemExit(1)

+    for child in pkg_link.iterdir():
+        if child.is_symlink():
+            target = child.resolve()
+            if in_primary_checkout(target):
+                print(
+                    f"Refusing package symlink pointing into primary checkout: {child} -> {target}",
+                    file=sys.stderr,
+                )
+                raise SystemExit(1)

+                print(
+                    f"Refusing to seed through destination cache symlink: {child}",
+                    file=sys.stderr,
+                )
+                raise SystemExit(1)

+}

+# cslib git revision and $ROOT/.lake/packages/cslib is a git checkout at a different revision.
+root_packages_match_manifest() {
+  local wt_path="$1"
+  python3 - "$ROOT" "$wt_path" <<'PY'
+import json

+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
+wt_path = Path(sys.argv[2])

+if not manifest.is_file():
+    manifest = root / "lake-manifest.json"
+if not cslib_git.exists() or not manifest.is_file():
+    raise SystemExit(0)
+
+try:
+    data = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    manifest_rev = None
+    for pkg in data.get("packages", []):
+        if isinstance(pkg, dict) and pkg.get("name") == "cslib":
+            manifest_rev = pkg.get("rev")
+            break
+    if not manifest_rev:
+        raise SystemExit(0)
+    actual_rev = subprocess.check_output(
+        ["git", "-C", str(cslib_git.parent), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
+        text=True,
+        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+    ).strip()
+    if actual_rev and not actual_rev.startswith(manifest_rev[:8]) and not manifest_rev.startswith(actual_rev[:8]):
+        print(
+            f"Root .lake/packages/cslib ({actual_rev[:8]}) does not match manifest pin ({manifest_rev[:8]}); skipping mismatched package seed.",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
+    pass
+PY
+}
+
+# ensure_shared_packages <worktree_path> <shared_pkg_dir>: create <shared_pkg_dir> once as an
+# isolated read-only copy of $ROOT/.lake/packages when not already present; never update in place.
+ensure_shared_packages() {
+  local wt_path="$1"
+  local shared_pkg_dir="$2"
+  if [ -d "$shared_pkg_dir" ]; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if [ ! -d "$ROOT/.lake/packages" ]; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! root_packages_match_manifest "$wt_path"; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$shared_pkg_dir")"
+  local staging
+  staging="$(mktemp -d "$(dirname "$shared_pkg_dir")/.staging-$(basename "$shared_pkg_dir").XXXXXX")"
+  local pkg name
+  for pkg in "$ROOT"/.lake/packages/*; do
+    [ -d "$pkg" ] || continue
+    name="$(basename "$pkg")"
+    seed_package "$pkg" "$staging/$name" "true"

body: [P2] Protect the shared directories as well as file contents. This chmod makes artifacts 0444, but their parent directories remain 0775. In the fake two-worker fixture, an ordinary `os.replace` of a new file onto one shared artifact succeeded without chmod and changed the artifact observed by the other worker. That defeats the promised read-only/never-update-in-place pool and can let ordinary build/cache replacement modify another active worker. Make the published tree resist replacement/deletion too, while keeping explicit writable copies functional; cover atomic replacement in the test rather than only `write_bytes`.

body: [P2] Key and validate the pool against the complete compatible dependency/toolchain state. With cslib unchanged, I seeded a pool at mathlib A, advanced both the root and target manifests/checkouts to mathlib B, then seeded a fresh worker. The existing cslib-keyed pool was accepted by the early return in `ensure_shared_packages`, and the worker contained mathlib A. The current guard also checks only cslib when initially copying root packages. Include all relevant pins/toolchain in identity and validate the actual seed source, or skip incompatible seeding. This finding is the incorrect seeded checkout itself; I am not claiming a later Lake/bootstrap build was tested.

body: [P2] Restrict this introductory tightness claim to n≥1 (or use cost+1≤n). At n=0 a constant output circuit has full empty support and binaryCost0≤n-1=0, but the constant-free LitFormula0/PosFormula0 types have no constructors. The actual theorems correctly keep the nonzero/stronger numerical premises; the module description should retain them.

body: [P2] Name the actual table-size endpoint and keep its precise lower-bound scope. `ETH.exists_not_decidableInTimeO_PartialMCSP_tableSize` does not exist here; the declaration is `ETH.not_decidableInSubexpTime_PartialMCSP_tableSize` (with its binary-encoding counterpart).
